The verse thus conveys that external change follows internal change, and that divine justice operates through natural consequences tied to the spiritual state of human hearts and deeds.

translation: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and those before them - they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh. And all of them were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine pattern of justice wherein nations that persistently deny God's signs and evidence face destruction proportional to their transgressions. The repetition of the fate of Pharaoh's people alongside previous nations demonstrates that this is not arbitrary punishment but a consistent divine law: rejection of truth leads to ruin. The emphasis on their status as wrongdoers (ظالمين) indicates that their destruction is not merely causation but moral consequence - those who wrong themselves through disbelief inevitably face the destruction they have earned.

translation: Indeed, the worst of creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieved, for they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse establishes the spiritual degradation of those who reject faith. Despite being human beings with rational faculties, the rejecters of Allah's truth are characterized as 'the worst of creatures' because they willfully turn away from guidance despite having the capacity to understand it. Their refusal to believe is presented not as mere intellectual disagreement but as a fundamental moral and spiritual corruption that places them beneath other creatures in Allah's estimation. The repetition of the concept (those who disbelieved/do not believe) emphasizes that this rejection is not a momentary lapse but a persistent, habitual state of the heart and mind. Their station is degraded not because of their human form, but because of their deliberate choice to resist the truth they have been shown.

translation: Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they are not conscious of God
interpretation: This verse describes the pattern of treachery and repeated covenant-breaking among those who made agreements with the Prophet, emphasizing their habitual violation of oaths and their lack of God-consciousness (taqwa) which would otherwise restrain them from such dishonorable conduct. The repetition of 'in every time' underscores that this breaking of covenants was not a single mistake but a persistent character trait revealing their spiritual corruption and unworthiness as treaty partners.

translation: So if you encounter them in battle, disperse those behind them that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse addresses the practical application of justice in warfare. When Muslims engage enemies in combat, they should demonstrate decisive victory not merely to eliminate opponents, but to send a clear message to their supporters and allies who observe from afar. The dispersal of those following behind represents both a tactical advantage and a moral lesson—showing strength and resolve to potential allies of the enemy so that they reconsider their allegiances and reflect on the consequences of enmity with the believers. The phrase 'that they might remember' emphasizes that the ultimate goal is reformation and deterrence through clear demonstration of consequences, not mere punishment for its own sake.

translation: And if you fear from a people betrayal, then throw back to them [your treaty] on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the traitors.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic principle of transparency and fair dealing in breaking agreements when betrayal is suspected. Rather than secretly violating a treaty or using deception in response to anticipated treachery, the command is to openly and directly inform the other party of the termination on equal footing. This reflects the Qur'anic ethic that Muslims must maintain moral superiority even in conflict, rejecting duplicity and matching the other party's level of clarity. The statement that Allah does not love traitors serves as divine affirmation that betrayal itself is morally repugnant, making it incumbent upon believers to avoid emulating such behavior and instead respond with honor and justice.

translation: And let not those who have disbelieved think that they have outpaced [us]. Indeed, they will not escape [Allah's punishment].
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers against presuming they have evaded divine reckoning through worldly success or survival. The phrase 'they have not outpaced' signifies that no amount of temporal power or evasion can prevent the inevitable consequence of rejecting Allah's message. The statement 'they will not weaken [His will]' emphasizes that their disbelief does not diminish Allah's omnipotence or His ability to bring them to account. The verse thus serves as a corrective to any arrogance disbelievers may harbor about escaping divine justice, whether in this life or the Hereafter.

translation: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war through which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others beyond them whom you do not know [but] whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that Muslims must develop military capability and strength proportionate to their ability as a means of deterrence against aggressors, while emphasizing that this preparation is ultimately for the sake of Allah rather than worldly ambition. The reference to enemies 'beyond them whom you do not know' indicates that defensive preparedness serves a broader purpose of protecting Islamic interests against unforeseen threats. The verse concludes by assuring that all expenditures made sincerely in Allah's path will be recompensed in full, thereby encouraging believers to allocate resources for both temporal security and spiritual commitment without fear of loss.

translation: And if they incline toward peace, then incline toward it and rely upon Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of accepting peace when the enemy seeks it, teaching that Muslims should not perpetuate conflict when an opportunity for reconciliation presents itself. The command to 'incline toward peace' mirrors the same verb used for the enemy's inclination, emphasizing mutual agreement and genuine settlement. By coupling this with reliance upon Allah, the verse reassures believers that accepting peace from a position of strength and trust in God is not weakness but wisdom, as Allah possesses complete knowledge of all circumstances and consequences, hearing the sincere intentions of all parties involved.

translation: And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed Allah is sufficient for you. He is the one who supported you with His help and with the believers.
interpretation: This verse conveys divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad that Allah's protection and support are complete safeguards against the deception and plots of his enemies. The mention of both Allah's victory and the believers' support emphasizes that the Prophet is never abandoned—he relies on Allah's infinite power while also benefiting from the solidarity of the faithful community, creating a multi-layered spiritual and social fortress against harm.

translation: And He united their hearts. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah united them. Indeed, He is Mighty and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true unity and harmony between believers' hearts is exclusively a divine act that cannot be achieved through material means or human effort alone. No amount of worldly wealth or resources can create genuine spiritual and emotional brotherhood; only Allah's wisdom and power can inspire hearts to truly reconcile and bond together. The verse stresses human limitation in matters of the heart while affirming Allah's supreme ability to transform inner dispositions and create lasting social cohesion among people.

translation: O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those of the believers who follow you.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that Allah's support and protection are all that is needed against adversaries. It emphasizes that reliance on divine aid transcends numerical strength or material resources, and extends this assurance to all believers who genuinely follow his guidance, teaching that faith in Allah's sufficiency produces spiritual resilience regardless of worldly circumstances or opposition faced.

translation: O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who have disbelieved, because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that faith, perseverance, and understanding give believers a qualitative advantage in struggle that transcends mere numerical superiority. The specific ratios (1:10 and 1:10 again) convey that believers fortified with conviction and wisdom possess a force multiplier that allows them to prevail against vastly larger numbers of those lacking spiritual insight. The characterization of disbelievers as 'a people who do not understand' reveals that their numerical strength is hollow because it lacks the foundation of true comprehension—of divine truth, purpose, and moral clarity—which forms the basis of genuine strength. This teaches that success in confronting falsehood depends primarily on the quality of belief and understanding rather than on material advantages alone.

translation: Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are from you one hundred steadfast [fighters], they will overcome two hundred. And if there are from you one thousand, they will overcome two thousand by permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse establishes a principle of divine assistance that is conditional upon human steadfastness and perseverance. It teaches that while Allah acknowledges human limitations and weaknesses, He empowers believers with supernatural strength when they remain resolute in faith and patience. The progressive ratios (1:2) illustrate that the power of steadfastness is not merely numerical but spiritual—those who are patient and constant receive divine support that multiplies their strength beyond natural proportions. The repeated emphasis on "the steadfast" indicates that victory is fundamentally tied to maintaining faith and resolve rather than to material advantages alone.

translation: It is not for a prophet to have captives of war until he has inflicted a massacre upon the land. You desire the gains of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter. And Allah is Mighty and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the taking of prisoners of war and reveals the divine priority in warfare: the establishment of Allah's authority on earth must precede the consideration of worldly benefits from captives or ransom. The verse rebukes the companions for preferring the immediate material gain of ransoming prisoners over the strategic objective of decisively subduing the enemy forces and consolidating the Islamic state's strength. The underlying principle is that believers must align their intentions with Allah's ultimate purpose—the afterlife and the spread of His religion—rather than being motivated by temporary worldly advantages, regardless of how beneficial they may appear.

translation: If not for a decree from Allah that had preceded, there would have touched you for what you took a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and forbearance toward the believers. The 'decree that preceded' refers to Allah's prior decision to delay punishment and grant respite to His servants, demonstrating His wisdom in not immediately punishing transgressions. It serves as a reminder that believers are protected by Allah's grace and foreknowledge, and that worldly punishment is withheld by divine wisdom—a mercy that should inspire gratitude and repentance rather than continued wrongdoing.

translation: So eat from what you have captured as lawful and good, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the permissibility and sanctity of war spoils in Islamic warfare, emphasizing that what is legitimately captured becomes lawful sustenance for the believers. The command to fear Allah and the reminder of His forgiveness and mercy frame this permission within moral boundaries, indicating that while the spoils are lawful, they must be obtained through proper Islamic conduct and distributed justly, with God-consciousness guiding the believers' handling of such matters.

translation: O Prophet, say to those captives in your hands: 'If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you something better than what has been taken from you, and He will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse establishes a principle of divine mercy and redemption for those who are in a vulnerable position of captivity. It conveys that sincere reformation and faith in the hearts of captives can lead to their material restoration and spiritual forgiveness from Allah, emphasizing that divine judgment is based on inner condition rather than outward circumstances, and encouraging both captives and the Muslim community to believe in the possibility of transformation and God's compassion even in situations of conflict.

translation: And if they desire to betray you, they have already betrayed Allah before, so He gave you power over them. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse assures the Prophet that those who seek to betray him have already shown their treachery against Allah Himself through their disbelief and broken covenants. Allah's granting of power and victory over them is not arbitrary but is the natural consequence of their own transgression. The verse emphasizes that Allah's wisdom encompasses all actions and intentions, and His justice ensures that those who oppose His signs will ultimately be subdued, while He protects His messenger and those who follow the truth.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and emigrated and strived with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah and those who gave shelter and aided them - those are allies of one another. But those who believed and did not emigrate - for you there is no guardianship of them until they emigrate. And if they seek help of you for the religion, then you must help, except against a people between you and whom is a treaty. And Allah is, of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of mutual loyalty and brotherhood among those who sacrifice for the faith through migration and struggle, while emphasizing that faith alone without commitment through migration and striving does not create the same bonds of communal obligation. The exception regarding treaties teaches that even in matters of religious duty, Muslims must honor their covenants with others, demonstrating that justice and integrity in agreements transcend religious boundaries and supersede certain obligations. This reflects the balance between religious commitment and ethical responsibility in dealing with non-Muslims.

translation: And those who disbelieve, some of them are protectors and allies of others. If you do not do so, there will be turmoil on earth and great corruption.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of Muslim unity and mutual support as a defense against the collective strength of disbelievers. The disbelievers stand together as a unified force against Islam, and therefore Muslims must similarly maintain strong bonds of brotherhood and solidarity with one another. Without such cohesion among believers, society would fall into chaos and widespread corruption, as the absence of righteous collective action would allow falsehood and disorder to flourish unchecked.

translation: And those who believed and emigrated and struggled in the way of Allah, and those who gave refuge and aided them - those are the believers in truth. For them is forgiveness and a generous provision.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith is not merely internal belief but must be manifested through action and sacrifice. It elevates those who suffer persecution for their faith by emigrating, those who actively strive in Allah's cause, and those who show compassion by sheltering and supporting the persecuted believers, placing them all on equal footing as genuine believers deserving of Allah's forgiveness and abundant reward. The verse teaches that solidarity with the oppressed and willingness to risk one's own security for righteousness are defining characteristics of authentic faith.

translation: And those who believed after [the initial revelation] and emigrated and strived with you - those are of you. But those of [blood] relations are more worthy of inheritance of one another in the decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes that while believers who came later and joined in the struggle are part of the Muslim community and deserve honor and brotherhood, the laws of inheritance revert to blood relations rather than being based solely on the bonds of faith or migration. The verse clarifies the priority order in inheritance law, subordinating the broader spiritual kinship established between early migrants to the natural family bonds that Allah has ordained in His law. This represents a return to established patrilineal inheritance rules after the period when emigrants to Medina were previously designated as heirs to the Helpers, demonstrating that Islamic law balances both spiritual community and natural familial obligations according to divine wisdom.

translation: A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger to those polytheists with whom you made a covenant
interpretation: This verse marks the abrogation of treaties with the polytheists of Arabia, signifying that the obligation to honor previous agreements with those who persistently rejected Islam and fought against the Muslims has been lifted. It represents a pivotal moment where the Muslim community, having grown stronger, was freed from the burden of maintaining peace with those who sought their destruction, allowing them to take decisive action to establish Islamic authority and protection.

translation: So travel throughout the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who have broken their covenant with the believers, granting them a period of safety and freedom of movement for four months to prepare themselves or depart. The verse emphasizes that this respite is not an escape from Allah's ultimate justice—those who reject Him cannot evade His power or plan. The assurance that Allah will humiliate the disbelievers serves as a warning that delay is temporary, and the final outcome is predetermined: those who persist in disbelief will face disgrace, affirming that security and immunity are not theirs to claim, only Allah's justice prevails.

translation: And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the Day of Hajj al-Akbar: Indeed, Allah is free from obligation to the polytheists, and [so is] His Messenger. So if you repent, that is better for you. And if you turn away, then know that you will not escape Allah. And give glad tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes the declaration of Allah's disassociation from polytheism and those who practice it, publicly announced during the great pilgrimage. The verse presents a clear choice to humanity: repentance and returning to monotheistic faith brings benefit and proximity to Allah, while turning away from faith brings inevitable accountability before Allah from whom no one can escape. The verse emphasizes that rejecting divine guidance leads to severe punishment, making the disbelievers' choice of turning away from truth the source of their own doom rather than any failure on Allah's part to guide them.

translation: Except for those of the polytheists with whom you have made a covenant, and they have not been deficient toward you in anything, nor have they aided anyone against you—so fulfill their covenant until their term expires. Indeed, Allah loves those who are conscientious.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of honoring treaties and covenants made with non-Muslims who have proven themselves to be trustworthy and peaceful. It emphasizes that fidelity to agreements is a moral obligation in Islam, even with those outside the faith, and that such integrity is a manifestation of piety (taqwa) which Allah loves. The condition that a covenant should be honored only if the other party has not breached it or supported enemies demonstrates that Islamic law recognizes mutual obligation and reciprocal trust as the foundation of lasting agreements.

translation: So when the sacred months have passed, then fight the polytheists wherever you find them, and seize them, and confine them, and wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that warfare against those who reject Islam becomes permissible after the sacred months conclude, yet it simultaneously emphasizes that the ultimate goal is not perpetual conflict but rather the acceptance of Islam and righteous conduct. The detailed description of military tactics—seeking them out, capturing them, besieging them, and setting ambushes—reflects the totality of effort required, but this is immediately qualified by the offer of amnesty and peaceful coexistence upon genuine repentance, prayer, and charity. The verse thus reveals that Islam's approach to conflict is conditional and reversible: it is not rooted in vengeance or permanent enmity, but rather in the pursuit of submission to Allah and moral transformation. The concluding affirmation of Allah's forgiveness and mercy indicates that even after warfare, the door to reconciliation remains open, teaching that the use of force is a means toward a higher spiritual and moral end, not an end in itself.

translation: And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection so that he may hear the word of Allah. Then convey him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of conditional asylum and safe passage for non-Muslims seeking to understand Islam, emphasizing that the primary goal is to allow them to hear the divine message. The reasoning given—that polytheists lack knowledge—suggests that lack of understanding, not inherent wickedness, is the root cause of their disbelief, and therefore they deserve an opportunity to learn before judgment is passed. This reflects Islam's commitment to clear communication of its message as a prerequisite for accountability.

translation: How can there be a covenant with Allah and His Messenger for the polytheists, except for those with whom you made a covenant near the Sacred Mosque? So as long as they remain upright with you, remain upright with them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous (those who fear Him).
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that while polytheists who break their oaths have no binding covenant protection with the Muslim community, those specific polytheists with whom Muslims had made explicit agreements near the Sacred Mosque retain the validity of their covenant—on the condition of their continued faithfulness. The verse emphasizes reciprocal loyalty and integrity in honoring agreements, teaching that the fulfillment of covenants is not absolute for all, but conditional upon the other party's adherence, and that such conduct of honoring obligations is a characteristic of those who truly fear Allah and seek His protection.

translation: How could they [have a covenant with you] when, if they overcome you, they do not respect toward you any kinship or covenant? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse [compliance], and most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse reveals the deceptive nature of those who make false covenants with the believers. It demonstrates that their outward words of agreement mask their true hostile intentions, warning the believers not to be deceived by verbal pledges from those whose actions and hearts demonstrate their enmity. The verse emphasizes the importance of judging people by their actual conduct and genuine commitment rather than by hollow words alone, establishing that true covenants require sincerity of both word and heart.

translation: They exchanged the signs of Allah for a small price, and thus turned away from His path. Evil indeed is what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who knowingly reject divine truth in exchange for worldly gain or personal benefits. The 'small price' represents the temporary, insignificant worldly advantages they choose over guidance from Allah. The verse emphasizes that such exchange is fundamentally irrational and destructive, as believers are deliberately choosing to abandon the path of Allah for trivial material or social gain. The phrase 'evil indeed is what they were doing' underscores the gravity and wickedness of consciously turning away from divine guidance, highlighting that such action is inherently wrong regardless of the benefits sought, and that this deliberate rejection constitutes a grave transgression against one's own soul and against God's truth.

translation: They do not observe toward a believer any pact or obligation. And those are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse describes the lawlessness and treachery of those who violate their covenants and oaths with believers, showing no regard for the bonds of kinship ('illah) or the protection (dhimmah) that should exist between people. By characterizing such behavior as transgression (i'tida'), the Qur'an emphasizes that breaking covenants and failing to respect sacred obligations is a fundamental moral violation that places one outside the bounds of righteousness and justice.

translation: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in faith. And We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that repentance combined with active obedience—manifested through prayer and charitable giving—restores one's standing within the Muslim community as a full brother or sister in faith. The condition is not merely verbal repentance but genuine transformation demonstrated through commitment to the central pillars of Islamic practice. The final clause indicates that such detailed explanations of divine guidance are specifically beneficial for those who possess understanding and wisdom, suggesting that the recognition of this principle of forgiveness and restoration requires intellectual reflection on the signs of Allah.

translation: And if they break their oaths after their covenant and attack your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief. Indeed, they have no [binding] oaths. Perhaps they will desist.
interpretation: This verse establishes the conditions and justifications for warfare against those who initiate hostilities against Muslims. The breaking of covenants and active attacks on faith are presented as the triggering causes for military engagement, with the instruction to target leadership rather than indiscriminate violence. The phrase 'they have no binding oaths' indicates that such people have forfeited the protection that comes from honoring agreements, making them legitimate targets of defense. The concluding phrase 'perhaps they will desist' reveals that the ultimate purpose of such combat is not vengeance but rather to deter aggression and create conditions for peace, suggesting that military action should be proportionate to the goal of ending hostility.

translation: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and plotted to expel the Messenger, and initiated aggression against you the first time? Do you fear them? Allah is more worthy of your fear, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, establishing the divine sanction and moral justification for defensive warfare against those who have shown themselves to be aggressors through multiple transgressions: oath-breaking, conspiracy, and initiation of hostilities. The rhetorical question 'Will you not fight' combined with the enumeration of these grievances serves to awaken the believers' sense of duty and courage, while the concluding statement reasserts that true fear (taqwa) must be directed toward Allah alone, not toward enemies, as this is the essence of genuine faith. The verse teaches that legitimate self-defense against those who initiate aggression is not only permissible but morally necessary for those who truly believe in Allah.

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and will heal the breasts of a believing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that when believers engage in just struggle against those who oppose them and transgress against them, they become instruments through which Allah's divine justice is executed. The 'healing of breasts' refers to the removal of the psychological pain, anger, and distress that the believers have endured from persecution and oppression, indicating that righteous struggle brings both outward victory and inner peace and satisfaction to the faithful community.

translation: And the rage in their hearts will depart, and Allah will turn in forgiveness to whom He wills. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transformative power of divine grace in reconciling hearts that harbor resentment and anger. By mentioning that Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, the verse emphasizes that reconciliation and the healing of animosity depend ultimately upon God's will and wisdom. The phrase 'all of whose hearts are contained' suggests that only God possesses perfect knowledge of the inner state of hearts and the sincerity of intentions, making Him alone capable of determining who deserves forgiveness and genuine transformation. Thus, the verse conveys that while humans may struggle with anger and grudges, true resolution comes through God's mercy and the sincere turning back to Him.

translation: Or do you think that you will be left, while Allah has not yet made clear those among you who have striven hard and have not taken anyone as confidants besides Allah, His Messenger, and the believers? And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that sincere faith and action are tested and revealed through time - Allah will distinguish the genuine believers whose loyalty is exclusively to Him, His Prophet, and the community of believers from those whose hearts are divided or whose commitment is insincere. The verse implies that true membership in the Muslim community requires complete devotion without divided loyalties, and that such authenticity cannot remain hidden as Allah is fully aware of the innermost conditions and deeds of all people.

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while testifying against themselves of disbelief. Those - their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse establishes that polytheists are unfit to manage and maintain places of worship dedicated to Allah because their disbelief - which they openly demonstrate through their actions and beliefs - renders their religious works invalid and meaningless. The phrase 'testifying against themselves' emphasizes that their polytheism is a self-evident contradiction to monotheism, making any attempt on their part to oversee sacred spaces a fundamental incongruity. The eternal consequence in the Fire underscores that such actions, rooted in disbelief, cannot earn divine reward but only lead to spiritual ruin.

translation: Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and establish prayer, and give zakah, and fear none but Allah - it is these who may be among the guided ones who build and maintain the mosques of Allah.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the true builders and maintainers of mosques are not those who merely construct physical structures, but those whose inner conviction and righteous deeds demonstrate genuine faith. The verse emphasizes that building mosques in the material sense is an act of worship only when accompanied by sincere belief, obedience to Allah's commandments through prayer and charity, and complete freedom from fear of anyone except Allah. Thus, the verse redefines what it means to 'build' a mosque - it is a spiritual undertaking that reflects one's entire relationship with the Divine, not merely a physical or social achievement.

translation: Have you made the providing of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to [the deeds of] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse establishes a hierarchy of deeds in Islam, emphasizing that physical service and charitable works, while good, cannot be equated with sincere faith in Allah combined with righteous struggle in His cause. The verse rebukes those who relied on social or worldly accomplishments and public works as substitutes for genuine spiritual commitment and striving against their own souls and for the truth. It teaches that true worth before Allah is measured by the sincerity of belief and dedication to His path, not merely by outward charitable acts performed without faith.

translation: Those who have believed and emigrated and striven in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in degree in the sight of Allah. And those are the attainers of success.
interpretation: This verse establishes a hierarchy of faith and righteousness based on sacrifice and commitment. It emphasizes that true believers demonstrate their faith through concrete actions—migration from places of persecution, struggle in God's cause, and willingness to expend both material resources and personal effort. The verse conveys that spiritual elevation and ultimate success in God's sight is not merely theoretical belief, but rather belief tested and proven through costly sacrificial action, placing those who surrender their worldly security and personal safety at the highest rank of achievement.

translation: Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and pleasure, and gardens wherein is a permanent blessing for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise of reward to the believers, showing that Allah's announcement of mercy and satisfaction is a source of spiritual joy in this life, and that the eternal gardens represent not merely material comfort but a state of continuous, uninterrupted blessings that transcend worldly pleasures, thus encouraging steadfastness in faith through the assurance of meaningful, permanent reward.

translation: Abiding therein forever. Indeed, Allah - with Him is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward that awaits the righteous in Paradise, and underscores that the greatest reward available to humanity originates from Allah alone. The repetition of the concept of eternality and the emphasis on the magnitude of Allah's reward serves to motivate believers toward righteous action and steadfast obedience, while reminding them that the true measure of success is not worldly gain but divine approval and the eternal bliss that comes from it.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith. And whoever among you does so - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the bonds of faith supersede familial ties in matters of religious conviction. A believer must prioritize their commitment to God's guidance over loyalty to family members who actively choose disbelief, as doing otherwise would constitute a form of injustice (dhulm) against oneself and one's faith. The verse addresses the conflict between natural family loyalty and religious duty, stipulating that when these two are in direct opposition, the obligation to God takes precedence, and aligning with those who reject faith constitutes a grave spiritual error.

translation: Say: 'If your fathers and your sons and your brothers and your wives and your kindred, and wealth which you have acquired, and commerce in which you fear decline, and dwellings in which you take pleasure are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His way, then wait until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the transgressing people.'
interpretation: This verse tests the believer's priorities and ultimate allegiance, establishing that love for Allah and His Messenger, combined with sincere striving in His cause, must supersede all worldly attachments and temporal relationships. The verse is not condemning natural affection for family or permissible commerce, but rather exposing the reality of one's faith through the hierarchy of values—when these worldly loves become obstacles to obedience to Allah and His Messenger, they reveal a heart inclined toward transgression, which distances the person from divine guidance. The warning 'wait until Allah brings His command' implies that those who prioritize worldly concerns over Allah's way will inevitably face the consequences of their misaligned hearts, as Allah's guidance is withheld from those whose choices demonstrate internal corruption.

translation: Allah has certainly helped you on many occasions, and on the day of Hunayn, when you were pleased with your numbers, but they availed you nothing, and the earth became strait for you despite its spaciousness, then you turned back in retreat.
interpretation: This verse teaches that military victory depends not on numerical superiority or material resources, but entirely on Allah's support. The defeat at Hunayn, despite the Muslims' confidence in their larger forces, was a humbling reminder that reliance on worldly means while neglecting divine aid leads to failure. The verse emphasizes that Allah tests the believers through apparent hardship to purify them from arrogance and self-sufficiency, redirecting their trust toward Him alone rather than their own strength and numbers.

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and He sent down soldiers (angels) whom you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine support extended to the believers during their struggle, manifesting through both spiritual comfort (tranquility of heart) and unseen divine assistance (angelic forces). The punishment of the disbelievers is presented as a necessary consequence of their rejection of truth, establishing the principle that Allah's aid accompanies those who remain steadfast in faith while those who persist in disbelief face retribution—a reflection of the universal law that faith brings divine support and disbelief brings divine displeasure.

translation: Then Allah turns in forgiveness after that upon whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme authority and discretion in granting repentance and forgiveness. The phrase 'after that' indicates that even those who have committed grave sins are not permanently excluded from Allah's mercy if He chooses to accept their repentance. The repetition of divine attributes—'Forgiving' (Ghafoor) and 'Merciful' (Raheem)—underscores that forgiveness is central to Allah's nature and that His justice is tempered by unlimited compassion. This teaches that while consequences and accountability exist for sin, the door to redemption remains open for whoever Allah chooses to guide toward sincere repentance.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after [this] year of theirs. And if you fear a loss of profit, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that spiritual purity and correct faith are prerequisites for entry into the sacred sanctuary, and that the Muslims' trust should be placed entirely in Allah's provision rather than in material transactions with polytheists. The reassurance that Allah will compensate economically for losing trade during the pilgrimage season teaches believers that obedience to divine command and maintaining the sanctity of sacred spaces takes precedence over worldly gain, and that Allah's wisdom encompasses both spiritual and material welfare.

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah, nor in the Last Day, nor forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, nor adopt the religion of truth, from among those who were given the Scripture, until they pay the jizya with willing submission, and feel themselves subdued.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic legal framework for engaging in defensive warfare against People of the Book who actively oppose Islam's principles and refuse peaceful coexistence. The jizya system represents an alternative to conversion or conflict, allowing non-Muslim communities to maintain their faith while acknowledging Islamic sovereignty and contributing to the state's defense and welfare, thereby establishing a contractual relationship of mutual responsibility and protection rather than forced religious conversion. The condition of submission reflects the political subordination inherent in accepting Islamic governance, not spiritual humiliation or persecution.

translation: And the Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of Allah,' and the Christians say, 'The Messiah is the son of Allah.' That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before. May Allah fight them; how deluded they are!
interpretation: This verse exposes the theological error of both Jews and Christians by highlighting that their claims of divine sonship are hollow utterances lacking spiritual truth, and that such false beliefs simply echo the pagan idolatry of earlier nations, demonstrating a perennial pattern of human deviation from monotheism regardless of which revelation was previously given. The verse emphasizes that God's curse befalls those who persist in such fabrications, and rhetorically questions how they can continue in such delusion despite the clear guidance available to them.

translation: They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of blind obedience to religious scholars and monks, treating them as authorities equivalent to God. The verse teaches that obedience to human intermediaries in matters of religion—whether through accepting their interpretations, laws, or commands without reference to God's revelation—constitutes a form of shirk (associating partners with God). It emphasizes that God's commandment to humanity is singular and unambiguous: the worship of one God alone, without intermediaries or partners. The verse serves as a warning against elevating any human being or institution to a status that belongs only to the Divine, and reaffirms God's transcendence and absolute authority over all matters of faith and worship.

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even if the disbelievers hate it.
interpretation: This verse conveys the futility of human opposition to God's divine guidance and truth. Those who disbelieve attempt through their words and arguments to suppress the truth of Islam, but their efforts are insignificant against God's will. The 'light of Allah' symbolizes divine guidance and the religion of Islam, which cannot be diminished by mere human speech or rejection. The verse assures believers that despite the disbelievers' hatred and resistance, God's plan is inevitable and will be fully realized. It emphasizes God's supreme power and the ultimate triumph of His religion, regardless of human opposition.

translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He may make it prevail over all [other] religions, even though those who associate partners with Allah dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate victory and supremacy of Islam as the true religion of Allah, regardless of opposition from those who reject monotheism. The phrase 'even though those who associate partners with Allah dislike it' acknowledges that worldly resistance and disbelief cannot prevent the fulfillment of Allah's promise. The verse establishes that the mission of the Prophet Muhammad is divinely ordained to establish the truth and eliminate falsehood, and that Allah's will shall be accomplished despite the enmity of the disbelievers.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars and monks consume the wealth of people unjustly and divert [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah – give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against the corruption of religious leaders who exploit their followers for personal gain, and extends that warning to all who selfishly accumulate wealth without using it for charitable purposes. The juxtaposition of the two groups—those who abuse religious authority and those who hoard resources—emphasizes that both forms of greed constitute a turning away from God's path, as true faith requires both honesty in religious guidance and generosity in the use of material blessings.

translation: The Day when that (wealth) will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, sides, and backs will be branded with it (and it will be said to them): 'This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of greed and the hoarding of wealth. The metaphorical branding of the body with heated wealth signifies that the misguided priorities and selfish accumulation in this life will become the source of one's punishment in the Hereafter. The repeated use of 'what you hoarded' emphasizes personal responsibility—individuals will directly experience the consequences of their own actions and choices regarding material wealth, serving as a warning that true gain comes not from accumulation but from proper stewardship and generosity.

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth, of which four are sacred. That is the correct religion. So do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight against the polytheists collectively as they fight against you collectively. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Islamic lunar calendar consists of twelve months as divinely ordained, with four designated as sacred months in which warfare is prohibited, thereby establishing a system of spiritual discipline and moral restraint. The command to fight the polytheists despite the sacred months' restrictions does not contradict the prohibition on fighting within those months, but rather emphasizes that believers should maintain vigilance and righteousness in their defense against aggression, trusting in Allah's protection and victory for those who maintain piety and fulfill their religious obligations with complete commitment.

translation: Indeed, the postponement of a sacred month is an increase in disbelief. By it those who disbelieve are led astray - they make it permissible one year and forbidden another year to correspond in number with what Allah has forbidden, so they make permissible what Allah has forbidden. Their evil deeds have been made attractive to them, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of Nasi' (postponement of sacred months) as a manifestation of deliberate rebellion against Allah's divine law. The verse exposes how the disbelievers manipulated the lunar calendar system to suit their worldly desires, treating sacred months as negotiable rather than as absolute divine ordinances. The essence of their transgression lies in the arrogance of believing they could reorder Allah's commands according to their convenience, which represents a fundamental rejection of divine authority. The phrase 'their evil deeds have been made attractive to them' indicates that such people have become so entrenched in rationalization and self-deception that they no longer perceive their violations as wrong, having lost the capacity for moral discernment - a spiritual condition from which only Allah's guidance can rescue them.

translation: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that, when you are told to go forth in the cause of Allah, you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter is but little.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the believers for their reluctance to participate in jihad and struggle in Allah's path, using the metaphor of 'adhering to the earth' to describe their spiritual lethargy and attachment to material comfort. The passage confronts them with the reality that preferring the transient pleasures of this world over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter is a grave misvaluation, establishing the principle that worldly concerns must never eclipse one's commitment to Allah's cause and the eternal life to come.

translation: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of refusing to participate in jihad or obligatory military campaigns for the cause of Allah. The verse teaches that neglecting one's duty to support and defend the faith through striving in Allah's way results in severe divine punishment. Moreover, it conveys the reality that Allah's will and plan are independent of human cooperation—if the Muslim community collectively refuses their obligation, Allah will raise up another people to fulfill His purpose, rendering the disobedient community's refusal meaningless and ineffectual. The final phrase reasserts Allah's absolute power and sovereignty, indicating that the execution of His will does not depend on any human effort, yet humans are still held accountable for their choices and obedience.

translation: If you do not aid him, Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved drove him out [from Mecca] as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.' And Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with armies you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that divine support for the Prophet Muhammad and his cause transcends human assistance. The historical reference to the cave serves as evidence that Allah's aid is independent of material forces or numbers—it operates through spiritual strengthening (tranquility) and invisible divine support. The verse teaches that the ultimate triumph belongs to those whom Allah sustains, regardless of worldly circumstances, and that the degradation of the disbelievers' position and elevation of Allah's word is an inevitable divine law, not contingent upon human effort alone. This principle invites believers to place their confidence in divine providence rather than being discouraged by apparent weakness or numerical disadvantage.

translation: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and yourselves in the way of Allah. That is best for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to participate in jihad (striving in the way of Allah) without excuse or hesitation, emphasizing that everyone—regardless of circumstances (whether burdened or unencumbered)—must contribute to this struggle through both material and personal sacrifice. The phrase 'if you only knew' suggests that the ultimate benefit and divine reward of such sacrifice may not be immediately apparent to the believers, yet they are assured that obedience to Allah's command is inherently the best course for them, implying that trust in Allah's wisdom should override any doubt about the immediate hardship of such sacrifice.

translation: If it had been an easy gain and a short journey, they would have followed you; but the distance seemed long to them. Yet they will swear by Allah, 'If we had been able, we would have gone forth with you.' They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are liars.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how worldly comfort and ease are the primary motivations for the hypocrites' actions, while their claims of willingness to participate in jihad are merely false excuses. Their swearing by Allah is a futile attempt to conceal their true nature—that they lack genuine faith and commitment. The verse exposes the contradiction between their words and their intentions, emphasizing that Allah's knowledge penetrates their hearts and perceives the reality of their disbelief, rendering their oaths meaningless and their self-deception ultimately destructive to their own souls.

translation: May Allah forgive you. Why did you give them permission (to stay behind) until those who told the truth became clear to you and you knew the liars?
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad regarding his decision to permit some of the Bedouins to remain behind from an expedition. The verse conveys divine rebuke for allowing them to absent themselves without verification of their truthfulness, suggesting that the Prophet should have waited to distinguish between the sincere believers and the hypocrites through their actions and conduct before granting them leave, thereby emphasizing the importance of discernment and caution in leadership decisions.

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to strive with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is knowing of the God-fearing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers possess such conviction and eagerness in their faith that they do not seek the Prophet's permission to participate in jihad and defense of the faith. Rather than needing encouragement or authorization, their belief in Allah and the Hereafter naturally drives them to sacrifice their resources and risk their lives. The verse contrasts this with those whose faith is weak or insincere, suggesting that genuine faith manifests in spontaneous, willing sacrifice without hesitation or requirement for permission. The concluding phrase assures that Allah fully knows and recognizes the sincere devotion of the God-fearing, implying that such sacrifice does not go unrecognized or unrewarded.

translation: Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day ask your permission [to be excused from jihad]. And their hearts have become filled with doubt, so they waver in their doubt.
interpretation: This verse reveals that the hesitation and excuse-seeking of certain individuals regarding participation in righteous struggle stems from their fundamental lack of faith in Allah and the accountability of the Hereafter. Their internal state of doubt—characterized by spiritual instability and wavering conviction—is the root cause of their external resistance and reluctance. The verse teaches that true belief provides certainty and resolve, while disbelief and doubt create internal turmoil that manifests as vacillation and evasion. This suggests that addressing people's spiritual certainty is more important than addressing their excuses, as their excuses are merely symptoms of deeper spiritual disease.

translation: And if they had intended to go forth, they would have prepared for it some equipment. But Allah disliked their being sent forth, so He kept them back, and it was said, 'Remain with those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Allah's will supersedes human intention and effort. Those who were reluctant to fight lacked the internal resolve despite outward capability, and Allah allowed this reluctance to manifest as a restraining force, preventing them from participating in the struggle. The divine displeasure with their lack of sincere commitment meant that their hesitation became a mercy in itself, as their participation would have been hypocritical and harmful. The command to remain behind with those excused from fighting represents both a consequence of their unwillingness and a recognition by the community of their unsuitability for the cause.

translation: If they had gone forth with you, they would not have increased you except in corruption, and they would have hastened among you seeking discord for you. And among you are those who listen to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that hypocrisy and disloyalty weaken the community's purpose and unity. Those who are unreliable in faith and commitment, had they joined an expedition, would have sown discord and confusion rather than provided strength. The warning extends to the believers themselves, cautioning them against being influenced by the hypocrites' whisperings, while reassuring them that Allah is fully aware of the transgressions of these deceitful individuals and will ultimately hold them accountable.

translation: They sought to cause discord before, and they turned matters upside down for you until the truth came and the command of Allah appeared, while they were displeased.
interpretation: This verse reveals the persistent enmity of the disbelievers who continuously plotted against the Prophet Muhammad and his message. Despite their relentless schemes and reversals of truth, Allah's ultimate will prevailed when His command became manifest, regardless of their disapproval. The verse emphasizes that human opposition cannot obstruct Allah's established plan, and that truth will ultimately triumph over falsehood, even when those who reject it remain resentful of this outcome.

translation: And among them are those who say, 'Grant me permission [to stay behind] and do not subject me to trial.' Unquestionably, they have fallen into trial, and indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the self-deception and spiritual blindness of the hypocrites who sought exemption from the hardships of jihad. Their request to be spared from 'trial' (fitnah) reveals their misunderstanding of what constitutes true trial—they feared physical hardship while already being ensnared in the greater trial of spiritual corruption and doubt. The verse demonstrates that those who flee from the obligations of faith and the struggle in God's path have already succumbed to the ultimate trial: the wavering of their hearts and the loss of their conviction. Their attempt to avoid difficulty becomes itself a manifestation of their already-fallen state, showing that spiritual ruin precedes or accompanies the refusal to submit to God's commands.

translation: If good befalls you, it displeases them; and if a misfortune strikes you, they say, 'We had already taken our precautions beforehand,' and they turn away rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the hypocritical and spiteful attitude of those who oppose the Prophet and believers. Their hostility is so deep-rooted that they find no satisfaction in the believers' good fortune—they are grieved by it—yet when the believers face hardship, they gloat and falsely claim to have anticipated it, using it as vindication of their own stance. Their turning away in joy at the believers' misfortunes demonstrates that their opposition is not based on rational concern but on malice and hatred, and they derive pleasure from seeing others suffer.

translation: Say, 'Nothing will befall us except what Allah has decreed for us. He is our Master. And in Allah let the believers place their trust.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that all events, whether perceived as good or harmful, occur only by Allah's decree and predestination, which should inspire believers with absolute confidence in Divine wisdom. By accepting Allah's sovereignty and placing complete trust in Him rather than fearing misfortune, believers achieve spiritual tranquility and liberation from anxiety, understanding that their reliance upon Allah's providence is the source of true protection and strength.

translation: Say, 'Are you waiting for us except one of two good outcomes? While we are waiting for you that Allah will strike you with punishment from Him or by our hands. So wait; indeed, we are waiting with you.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the believers' steadfast conviction and resolve in the face of hostility. Despite being persecuted, the Muslims maintain that they are content with either of two favorable outcomes: victory and triumph in this world, or martyrdom and paradise in the next. Meanwhile, they warn their adversaries that they too are awaiting divine justice—either through Allah's direct punishment or through the believers' own righteous struggle. The repeated use of 'tarbassun' (waiting/watching) emphasizes the psychological warfare and moral certainty of the believers, who remain patient and resolute while their enemies face the inevitable consequences of their transgression, creating a powerful message of confidence in ultimate victory despite present weakness.

translation: Say: 'Spend willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. Indeed, you are a people who are transgressors.'
interpretation: This verse conveys that sincere charity and good deeds are contingent upon faith and obedience to God. The external act of spending, whether done voluntarily or under compulsion, holds no value when the heart is devoid of true faith and righteousness. The rejection of the disbelievers' spending reflects the divine principle that actions are only acceptable when rooted in genuine submission to God and a righteous character. Mere material giving without spiritual integrity and belief cannot earn divine favor or expiate one's rebellion against God's commands.

translation: And nothing prevented their charitable contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and in His Messenger, and they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy, and they do not spend except while they are unwilling.
interpretation: The verse reveals that the rejection of the hypocrites' deeds is rooted in the corruption of their hearts - their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger - which taints all their outward actions. Their reluctance and aversion in fulfilling religious duties (prayer and charity) demonstrate that without sincere faith and willing obedience, external acts are spiritually worthless and unacceptable to Allah. The verse establishes that true acceptance before Allah requires both authentic belief and genuine willingness in worship.

translation: So let not their wealth and their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them therewith in the worldly life, and [that] their souls depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that worldly possessions and offspring should not be a source of envy or admiration, as they may actually be signs of Divine punishment rather than favor. The material abundance granted to those who reject faith is not a blessing but a trial through which Allah tests them, allowing them to accumulate more sin and pursue misguidance until they meet their end as disbelievers. This inverts the common perception of wealth as success, revealing that true success lies in faith and obedience to Allah.

translation: And they swear by Allah that they are indeed of you, while they are not of you; but they are a people who split apart (in obedience and loyalty).
interpretation: This verse describes the hypocrites (munafiqun) who outwardly claim solidarity with the believers through oaths, yet their hearts and true allegiance lie elsewhere. Their splitting (tafriq) refers to their internal division between their public profession of faith and their hidden disbelief, as well as their tendency to sow discord and division within the Muslim community. The verse emphasizes that true membership in the community of believers is not determined by verbal claims alone, but by sincere conviction and unified commitment, which these people lack.

translation: If they could find a refuge or caves or any place of entry, they would turn towards it, running away in haste.
interpretation: This verse depicts the intense fear and desperation of those who deny the truth on the Day of Judgment, showing how the certainty of divine punishment would cause them to seek any escape, no matter how futile, demonstrating their complete abandonment of hope and dignified resistance in the face of inevitable divine justice.

translation: And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities. If they are given from it, they are satisfied, and if they are not given from it, then they become angry.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the hypocrisy and mercenary nature of those whose faith is weak and whose motives are worldly rather than spiritual. Their criticism of the Prophet's distribution of charitable funds reveals that they are motivated by personal gain rather than genuine concern for righteousness. Their conditional approval—satisfied when benefiting, discontented when not—exposes the absence of sincere submission to Allah and proper understanding of charitable giving as an obligation of faith rather than a means of personal enrichment. The verse teaches that true believers should support the Prophet's just decisions without complaint, and that charitable distribution should be conducted with wisdom that may not always align with the preferences of recipients.

translation: And if only they had been satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger gave them, and said, 'Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us from His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger. Indeed, we are desirous toward Allah.'
interpretation: This verse presents the spiritual remedy for those plagued by discontent and insatiable desires: contentment with divine provision accompanied by reliance upon Allah's sufficiency. The phrase 'Allah is sufficient for us' (Hasbunallah) expresses unwavering trust in Allah's care, while 'we are desirous toward Allah' indicates that true longing should be directed toward Allah alone, not toward the material world. The verse teaches that satisfaction with one's portion from Allah and His Messenger, combined with conscious supplication to Allah, constitutes the path to spiritual peace and divine increase, suggesting that material contentment opens the door to spiritual wealth that far exceeds worldly possessions.

translation: Zakah (obligatory charity) is only for the poor, the needy, those employed to collect it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, the freeing of slaves, those in debt, in the way of Allah, and the traveler in need - an obligation from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that zakah is not a voluntary act of piety but a mandatory obligation (fariḍah) from Allah with specific recipients, signifying that Islamic charity is a structured social welfare system with clear categories of beneficiaries determined by divine wisdom, not personal preference or arbitrary distribution.

translation: And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, 'He is an ear.' Say, 'An ear of good for you—he believes in Allah and believes [the reports of] the believers and is a mercy to those who have believed among you.' And those who harm the Messenger of Allah will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the mockery of the Prophet by hypocrites who claimed he was too credulous, accepting whatever he heard without discernment. The Prophet's response reframes this accusation as a virtue: being receptive to the believers' testimonies and reports is praiseworthy because it reflects trust in Allah and compassion for the faithful community. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's openness to belief and his mercy toward believers are divine qualities, not flaws, and it establishes a serious warning that those who intentionally harm or ridicule the Messenger face severe divine punishment, thereby protecting the dignity of prophethood and the social cohesion of the Muslim community.

translation: They swear to you by Allah to please you, but Allah and His Messenger are more deserving that they please Him, if they are believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of those who prioritize pleasing people over pleasing Allah and His Messenger. It establishes a fundamental principle of faith: true belief requires that one's primary concern be satisfying Allah and following the guidance of His Messenger, not seeking approval from others through false oaths and deception. The conditional clause 'if they are believers' underscores that genuine faith is incompatible with placing human approval above divine command.

translation: Did they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger will surely have the Fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally? That is the great disgrace.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of rejecting Allah's guidance and the Prophet's message, warning that such opposition is not merely a political or intellectual disagreement but a fundamental rejection of divine truth that incurs the ultimate punishment. The phrase 'great disgrace' suggests that beyond the physical punishment of Hell, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger face profound humiliation and shame, as their rebellion represents a fundamental denial of reality and truth itself.

translation: The hypocrites fear that a surah will be sent down upon them informing them of what is in their hearts. Say: "Mock on! Indeed, Allah will bring forth what you fear."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the hypocrites' deep anxiety about their concealed disbelief and evil intentions being exposed through divine revelation. Their fear itself is a sign of their guilty conscience and recognition of God's knowledge of the hidden. The command to the Prophet to respond with "Mock on!" is not a concession to ridicule but a statement of confident defiance—whatever they fear or mock, God's truth will inevitably be revealed. This reflects that divine knowledge cannot be evaded and that the hypocrites' attempts to hide their true beliefs are futile against God's omniscience.

translation: And if you ask them, they will surely say, 'We were only joking and playing.' Say, 'Were you mocking Allah, His signs, and His Messenger?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates how those who mock the faith attempt to evade accountability for their mockery by claiming they were merely joking, when in reality their jesting about sacred matters constitutes serious ridicule of Allah's religion. The verse emphasizes that no excuse of levity can diminish the gravity of mocking Allah, His revelations, or His Messenger, as such mockery is fundamentally an act of disbelief and rejection, not mere entertainment.

translation: Do not apologize; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon one group among you, We will punish another group because they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who made excuses for their disobedience and waywardness after accepting faith. The verse emphasizes that mere excuses and apologies cannot erase the gravity of apostasy or rejection of faith after having embraced it. The divine justice operates with perfect discernment—some may receive forgiveness through repentance and sincere reform, while others will face punishment according to their criminal transgressions. The verse serves as a stern warning that returning to disbelief after faith is not a trivial matter that can be dismissed with excuses; rather, it requires genuine repentance and accountability before Allah's justice.

translation: The hypocrites, men and women, are of one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right, and they withhold their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse reveals the internal contradiction and spiritual isolation of the hypocrites: they are bound together by their shared hypocrisy, but their defining characteristic is the inversion of moral values—promoting evil while suppressing good—combined with spiritual stinginess. The phrase 'they have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them' conveys that their neglect of Allah's remembrance and commands results in Allah's removal of His guidance and care from them, a divine consequence that reflects the reciprocal nature of the relationship between servant and Lord, where abandonment of faith leads to abandonment by divine grace.

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers the Fire of Hell, wherein they shall abide forever. It is sufficient for them. And Allah has cursed them, and for them is an everlasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that hypocrisy and disbelief are grave transgressions that incur the severest divine consequences. The emphasis on the permanence of punishment ('khalidin' - abiding forever, 'adhaab muqim' - everlasting punishment) underscores the finality and irreversibility of the fate of those who reject faith and live in deception, while the statement that Hell 'is sufficient for them' indicates that no additional punishment is needed beyond this, as it encompasses all forms of torment, thus warning believers of the absolute seriousness with which Allah regards apostasy and the false profession of faith combined with inner rejection.

translation: Like those before you—they were greater than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion, and you have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion. And you have engaged in idle discourse as they did. Those—their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against following the precedent of disbelieving nations by abandoning their religious obligations and moral responsibilities in pursuit of worldly pleasures, just as previous peoples did. The comparison emphasizes that material superiority and numerical strength are not indicators of right conduct, and that engaging in the same destructive behaviors as those who came before leads to the annulment of one's good deeds and ultimate loss. The verse calls believers to distinguish themselves through obedience to Allah rather than mimicking the patterns of those whose works came to nothing.

translation: Has there not come to them the news of those who were before them - the people of Noah, 'Ad, and Thamud, and the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan, and those who were overturned? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. And it was not for Allah to wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that rejection of divine guidance is not due to Allah's injustice, but rather stems from human choice and self-inflicted spiritual harm. By recounting the destruction of previous nations who received clear signs through their messengers, the verse demonstrates that those who deny the truth are responsible for their own ruin, as they actively choose to turn away from obvious evidence of Allah's oneness and reject the path of righteousness.

translation: The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is evil, establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Muslim community forms a unified body bound by mutual loyalty and shared religious purpose. The believers' alliance is not based on tribal affiliation or worldly interests, but on their collective commitment to commanding good and prohibiting evil while fulfilling the core obligations of Islam. The promise of Allah's mercy is contingent upon this comprehensive engagement with both vertical devotion to Allah and horizontal responsibility toward society, emphasizing that faith must manifest through practical social reform and moral guardianship. The attributes 'Exalted in Might and Wise' affirm that Allah has both the power to reward such believers and the perfect wisdom to judge who truly merits His mercy.

translation: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. But the approval of Allah is greater than that. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the ultimate reward for believers transcends material blessings; while paradise with its physical gardens and rivers is promised to them, the greatest honor and true victory lies in achieving Allah's pleasure and approval. The verse prioritizes spiritual satisfaction over sensory pleasures, teaching that divine contentment is the supreme prize that surpasses all other rewards in paradise.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Prophet's obligation to combat unbelief and hypocrisy extends beyond mere doctrinal clarity to include firm, uncompromising opposition.
