The verse reveals that authentic monotheistic belief requires complete devotion without associating any partners with Allah in worship, attributes, or authority.

translation: Have they then become secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from Allah, or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?
interpretation: This verse expresses rhetorical astonishment at the arrogance and complacency of those who reject faith, highlighting their false sense of security. By posing this question, the Qur'an draws attention to their dangerous delusion—they live as if catastrophic divine punishment or the Day of Judgment will never reach them, despite having no rational basis for this assumption. The verse serves as a warning that such heedlessness is itself a grave peril, for they may indeed be seized by punishment or the Hour while in complete ignorance of their impending fate.

translation: Say, 'This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah, and I am not of those who associate partners with Him.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's message is rooted in clear knowledge and understanding rather than blind following or conjecture. The phrase 'on insight' (على بصيرة) indicates that the call to monotheism is based on rational conviction and divine guidance. By mentioning those who follow him alongside himself, the verse establishes that true faith requires personal comprehension and conscious commitment, not merely cultural inheritance. The affirmation of Allah's transcendence and the disavowal of polytheism serves as both the foundation and the ultimate aim of this enlightened path, contrasting the clarity of monotheism with the confusion of idolatry.

translation: And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed [Our message] from among the people of the cities. So have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Then will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse establishes that prophethood is not conveyed to exceptional beings but to ordinary human men chosen from among the communities they address, thereby refuting any claim that receiving revelation requires superhuman nature. The verse then invites reflection upon historical patterns—that previous nations faced destruction when they rejected their messengers—as empirical evidence available to the Meccans themselves through observation of ruins and archaeological remains. By connecting this observable historical consequence to the eternal superiority of the Afterlife for the God-fearing, the verse challenges the addressees to use rational judgment: recognizing that rejecting messengers leads to worldly ruin and loss of eternal reward should be sufficient motivation for accepting the truth.

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them, and We saved whom We willed. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the theme of divine testing and ultimate vindication of the righteous. The apparent despair of the messengers represents a crucial trial where their faith is tested to its limit, not because God's promise was false, but to demonstrate the depth of their conviction and patience. The arrival of divine aid after this moment of despair teaches that God's support comes at precisely the moment when human hope seems exhausted, emphasizing that deliverance depends entirely on God's wisdom and will, not on human expectation or timing. The final clause establishes that God's punishment for those who persist in transgression and denial is inevitable and cannot be prevented, creating a contrast between the salvation reserved for the chosen believers and the irreversible consequences faced by the defiant wrongdoers.

translation: Certainly, in their stories is a lesson for those possessed of understanding. It is not a narration fabricated, but a confirmation of that which was before it, and a detailed explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy for people who believe.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Qur'an as a source of spiritual and practical wisdom derived from historical examples, emphasizing that the Qur'anic narratives are not invented tales but rather authentic confirmations of previous revelation that provide comprehensive guidance and divine compassion specifically for those who embrace faith with sincere conviction and reflection.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Alif, Lam, Meem, Ra. These are the verses of the Book, and what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and absolute truth of the Qur'an despite widespread rejection. The mention of the mysterious letters (Alif, Lam, Meem, Ra) at the beginning signals the miraculous and inimitable nature of the text, while the statement that the revelation is 'the truth' from the Lord establishes its infallibility. The concluding observation that most people do not believe serves as both a realistic acknowledgment of human nature's tendency toward disbelief and an implicit call to the reader to be among the faithful few who recognize and accept divine truth.

translation: Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, then established Himself upon the Throne, and subjected the sun and the moon - each running for an appointed term. He administers all affairs and details the signs so that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete sovereignty and power by presenting His creation and governance as evidence of His existence and majesty. The imagery of unsupported heavens, the establishment on the Throne, and the precise regulation of celestial bodies demonstrates rational, purposeful order in the universe. The verse connects this observable cosmic order to the certainty of the Hereafter, suggesting that just as Allah has established perfect systems governing creation, His promise of the Day of Judgment is equally certain and inevitable. The detailed signs (ayat) throughout creation serve as proofs to strengthen faith and remove doubt about meeting one's Lord in the Afterlife.

translation: And it is He who spread out the earth and placed upon it mountains and rivers. And from every fruit, He made therein two kinds. He covers the night over the day. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the interconnectedness of creation as evidence of divine wisdom and design. The mention of mountains stabilizing the earth, rivers providing sustenance, and the complementary pairing of fruits symbolizes how the Creator has established a harmonious balance in nature where every element has its purpose and is matched with its complement. The covering of night by day represents the cyclical nature of existence and God's complete dominion over time. The verse culminates by directing attention to those who reflect and contemplate creation, suggesting that true understanding of God's oneness comes through observation and rational meditation on the natural world rather than mere passive witnessing.

translation: And in the earth are neighboring tracts of land and gardens of grapevines, crops, and palm trees—some having multiple trunks and some having single trunks—watered with the same water. Yet We make some of them exceed others in taste. Indeed, in that are signs for people who reason.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates Allah's power and wisdom through the diversity of creation despite uniform conditions. When identical water and soil nourish different plants producing varied fruits and tastes, it reflects Allah's control over nature and His deliberate diversification of creation. This diversity serves as evidence of divine intention and craftsmanship, inviting rational contemplation of how uniformity in means produces variation in results—a profound lesson that the universe's variations are not accidental but purposefully designed by the Creator.

translation: And if you are amazed, then amazing is their saying: 'When we have become dust, shall we indeed be brought forth in a new creation?' Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, and those - for them are shackles around their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire, wherein they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness of those who deny resurrection and the afterlife. Their astonishment at the possibility of being recreated from dust after death demonstrates a fundamental rejection of divine power and the reality of God's absolute dominion over creation and recreation. Their disbelief in resurrection is symptomatic of a deeper disbelief in God's lordship itself, which enslaves them spiritually (symbolized by shackles) and condemns them to eternal punishment. The verse emphasizes that denial of the hereafter is not merely intellectual disagreement but represents a complete severance from belief in God's authority and omnipotence.

translation: And they urge you to hasten with evil before good, though examples have passed before them. Yet your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse reflects the tension between God's infinite mercy and His absolute justice. Despite humanity's tendency to rush toward harmful desires and reject guidance, God's capacity for forgiveness remains available to those who turn back. However, this mercy is not unconditional—it coexists with God's severity in punishment for those who persistently reject His signs and continue in wrongdoing. The verse teaches that while divine clemency is a reality, it should not create false security, as God's justice and retribution are equally certain for those who persist in sin.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has not a sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?' Say, 'You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the persistent demand of disbelievers for miraculous signs as proof of the Prophet's message, revealing their spiritual blindness and obstinacy. The response clarifies that the Prophet's role is to warn and convey the message, while God Himself provides guidance to each people according to their receptiveness and circumstances. The verse teaches that faith is not merely contingent upon spectacular miracles, but upon the sincere seeking of truth and willingness to be guided; those who genuinely desire guidance will find it through the Prophet's message and their own hearts' inclination toward God.

translation: Allah knows what every female carries (in her womb), and what the wombs fall short of and what they exceed. And everything with Him is in due measure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute knowledge and complete awareness of all hidden realities that are beyond human perception. The specific reference to the knowledge of what occurs in wombs - the exact nature, timing, and details of conception and fetal development - serves as a profound example of the unseen knowledge that belongs exclusively to Allah. By juxtaposing this intimate divine knowledge with the principle that 'everything with Him is in due measure,' the verse communicates that Allah's knowledge is not merely awareness but is intrinsically connected to His precise determination and wisdom. Nothing exists outside of His knowledge or design, and all things, both visible and invisible, are ordered according to His perfect measure and divine plan. This serves as a reminder of human limitation and the necessity of reliance upon Allah's wisdom in matters beyond our comprehension.

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Most Great, the Most High
interpretation: This phrase describes Allah's absolute knowledge and transcendent nature - He alone knows both the hidden realities beyond human perception (the unseen/ghayb) and everything manifest and visible to creation (the seen/shahada), while being supremely great and exalted beyond any comparison or limitation. This emphasizes God's omniscience as comprehensive and His status as utterly beyond the creation He sustains.

translation: Alike among you are those who conceal their speech and those who declare it, and those who hide by night and those who go openly by day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and surveillance over all human actions, whether hidden or public, quiet or loud, done in secrecy or openness. It serves to remind believers that Allah's omniscience is not limited by time, place, or the nature of actions - He knows all intentions and deeds equally, making it futile to think any action can escape His awareness or judgment. This is meant to instill consciousness of God (taqwa) by recognizing that accountability before Allah is absolute and universal.

translation: For each one there are successive angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of Allah. Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves. And when Allah intends for a people harm, there is no repelling it. And there is for them besides Him no protector.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of divine justice and human responsibility in a profound way: Allah has appointed angels to protect and guide people according to His command, but ultimate change in a society's circumstances depends on the internal moral transformation of its members. The verse teaches that divine punishment or hardship for a people is contingent upon their own deterioration of character and values, not arbitrary; Allah does not alter their external condition without a corresponding change in their inner state. When Allah has determined adversity for a people due to their spiritual decline, this consequence becomes inevitable and irreversible, reinforcing that individuals and societies possess agency in their moral choices while remaining subject to the immutable laws of divine justice that Allah has established for human affairs.

translation: He is the One who shows you the lightning, causing fear and hope, and produces the heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's power and mastery over natural phenomena, using lightning and clouds as signs of His dominion. The dual emotional response to lightning—fear of its danger and hope for the rain it brings—demonstrates how the same phenomenon serves different purposes depending on human circumstances and needs. The verse points to how creation itself communicates Allah's might to those who reflect upon it, encouraging humility and trust in His providence.

translation: And the thunder celebrates His praises, and the angels too, in fear of Him. He sends the thunderbolt and strikes with it whom He will. Yet they dispute concerning Allah, while He is mighty in power.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the majesty and power of Allah through the natural phenomenon of thunder and lightning, demonstrating that all creation—both the thunder and the angels—glorify Him in awe of His might. The contrast between the cosmic obedience of creation and humanity's audacious argumentation about Allah's nature emphasizes human arrogance and ingratitude, suggesting that those who dispute about Allah's attributes while witnessing such displays of His overwhelming power are engaged in a fundamentally futile endeavor against one whose strength is unmatched.

translation: To Him belongs the call of truth. And those whom they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with anything except as one who stretches out his hands toward water that it might reach his mouth, but it will never reach it. And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and impossibility of seeking aid from false deities or created beings. Just as stretching one's hands toward distant water cannot bring it to the mouth—the action is futile and the goal unreachable—so too is the worship and supplication directed toward anything other than Allah devoid of any real benefit or response. The comparison emphasizes the absurdity and ineffectiveness of idolatry: the worshippers expend effort in a completely fruitless endeavor, receiving nothing in return. The verse thereby demonstrates that true guidance and true prayer can only come through adherence to Allah alone, while all other forms of worship represent a fundamental straying from reality and truth.

translation: To Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows in the morning and the afternoon.
interpretation: This verse conveys the absolute sovereignty of Allah and the universal submission of all creation to His will. Everything in existence—conscious beings who submit willingly through faith and obedience, those who resist out of disbelief, and even the inanimate shadows—are all subject to Allah's dominion and cosmic order. The mention of shadows emphasizes that even the most intangible and passive aspects of creation participate in this prostration, signifying that submission to Allah is not a matter of choice for creation, but an inescapable reality of existence itself. The verse affirms that denying or rebelling against Allah does not exempt one from being utterly dependent upon and subordinate to His will and decree.

translation: Say: 'Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say: 'Allah.' Say: 'Have you then taken protectors other than Him who have no power to benefit or harm themselves?' Say: 'Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are the darknesses and the light equal? Or have they assigned to Allah partners who created as He created, so that the creation seemed to them similar?' Say: 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Irresistible.'
interpretation: This passage employs a rhetorical interrogative method to establish the absolute uniqueness and incomparability of Allah's divine attributes and creative power. By progressively asking questions about lordship, protection, equivalence, and creation, the verse demolishes the logical foundation of polytheism by showing that false deities possess neither the power nor the qualities attributed to Allah. The final declaration that Allah is the Creator of all things and the One, the Irresistible (al-Qahhar), encapsulates the core Islamic principle of Tawhid—that all existence, all creative power, and all divine attributes belong exclusively to Allah, leaving no valid basis for associating partners with Him.

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the flood carries foam upon its surface. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking adornment or goods, comes forth foam like it. Thus does Allah set forth the parable of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum upon the banks, while that which is of benefit to mankind remains in the earth. Thus does Allah set forth parables.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inevitable separation of truth from falsehood through a natural analogy. Just as floodwater carries away worthless foam while nourishing substances settle and benefit the land, and just as the dross from smelting metals is discarded while the refined metal remains, so too will truth ultimately endure and false beliefs will be dispersed and forgotten. The verse teaches that despite the temporary prominence or appeal of falsehood, its nature is transient and ultimately futile, while truth, though it may sometimes appear less impressive, possesses inherent permanence and genuine benefit for humanity. This reflects the eternal divine pattern that falsehood cannot withstand the test of time.

translation: For those who have responded to their Lord is the best reward. But those who did not respond to Him - if they possessed all that is on earth and the like of it with it, they would ransom themselves with it. Those will have the worst reckoning, and their refuge is Hell. And wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental division between those who accept divine guidance and those who reject it, establishing that worldly wealth and possessions hold no value in the face of accountability before God. The hypothetical scenario of possessing all earthly treasures yet being unable to use them as ransom underscores the irreversible nature of rejecting God's call and the inescapable consequences that follow, demonstrating that spiritual obedience to God's signs is the only currency of true worth in the afterlife.

translation: Is then one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, like one who is blind? Only those of understanding will remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental distinction between those who recognize and accept divine truth and those who remain willfully ignorant or heedless of it. The comparison of a person aware of God's revealed guidance to a blind person illustrates that spiritual blindness—the failure to recognize truth—is a deficiency far greater than physical blindness. The verse concludes by attributing the capacity to truly benefit from this knowledge to those possessed of 'al-albab' (intellect and understanding), suggesting that recognizing divine truth requires both intellectual capability and sincere reflection, and that this discernment is not equally distributed among all people.

translation: Those who fulfill their covenant with Allah and do not break the contract
interpretation: This verse describes the character of the righteous who are steadfast in honoring their commitments and promises made to Allah. It emphasizes that true faith is demonstrated through loyalty and the keeping of one's word, showing that covenant-keeping is a fundamental aspect of piety and moral integrity in Islamic teaching. The emphasis on not breaking the covenant highlights the gravity of betraying one's commitments and the spiritual significance of maintaining trust and fidelity in all dealings, particularly with Allah and His commands.

translation: And those who maintain the ties that Allah has ordered to be maintained, and fear their Lord, and fear the evil reckoning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual obligation to preserve family relationships and social bonds that Allah has commanded to be upheld, while maintaining consciousness of divine accountability. The dual mention of fearing (khashya and khawf) underscores the importance of reverential awe before Allah and the anxiety about one's deeds being weighed on the Day of Judgment, which motivates righteous behavior in maintaining relational duties. The verse connects ethical conduct in relationships directly to one's relationship with the Divine and one's ultimate accountability before Him.

translation: And those who are patient seeking the Face of their Lord, and establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them secretly and openly, and repel evil with good - those will have the final reward of the abode (Paradise).
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual and moral characteristics of the righteous believers whose actions are motivated by sincere devotion to Allah rather than worldly recognition. Their constancy in patience, prayer, charity (both hidden and visible), and their practice of meeting evil with goodness demonstrates an integrated faith that transforms both inner intention and external conduct. The promise of the final reward suggests that such virtue is not transient or temporal, but leads to eternal dignity and honor in the afterlife, emphasizing that true success lies beyond this fleeting world.

translation: Gardens of perpetual bliss - they will enter them, and whoever among their fathers, spouses, and descendants were righteous - and the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that entry into Paradise is not limited to individuals alone, but extends to the righteous members of one's family across generations. The mention of angels entering from every gate symbolizes the multiple and continuous blessings, honor, and welcome that the righteous will receive in Paradise, suggesting that their joy will be complete and comprehensive, encompassing both their reunion with believing family members and the honor bestowed upon them by the angels of God.

translation: Peace be upon you for what you have endured; how excellent is the final abode.
interpretation: This verse addresses the righteous inhabitants of Paradise, greeting them with peace and acknowledging their patient endurance in this world. The greeting emphasizes that their reward is a direct consequence of their steadfastness in faith and trials. The phrase 'how excellent is the final abode' underscores the ultimate triumph and reward awaiting those who persevere with patience—that Paradise is not merely pleasant, but represents the perfection of all desires and the fulfillment of the believer's hopes. The verse teaches that patience in adversity is the gateway to eternal peace and bliss.

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after pledging it, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption in the land - for them is the curse, and for them is an evil abode.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that breaking sacred commitments to Allah, severing family and social bonds that Allah has ordained to maintain, and perpetuating corruption on earth are grave sins that incur divine condemnation and punishment in the afterlife. The verse establishes that integrity in covenant-keeping and maintenance of righteous relationships are fundamental obligations, and their violation results in spiritual estrangement from Allah's mercy both in this world and the next.

translation: Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it. And they rejoiced in the worldly life, but the worldly life compared to the Hereafter is only a brief enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse teaches that material wealth and sustenance are not indicative of God's favor or disfavor, as He distributes provision according to His wisdom and for reasons beyond human comprehension. The verse cautions against the spiritual danger of becoming attached to worldly possessions and pleasures, warning that those who find joy primarily in material life have fundamentally misunderstood human purpose and destiny—treating the temporary world as an end in itself rather than recognizing it as a transient test preceding the eternal reality of the Hereafter.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has not a sign from his Lord been sent down to him?' Say, 'Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides to Himself those who repent.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogant demand of the disbelievers for a miraculous sign as proof of the Prophet's message, revealing that their request stems from obstinate hearts rather than genuine seeking of truth. The response indicates that guidance is not merely a matter of presenting signs, but rather depends on the state of one's heart and willingness to submit to God—those who turn to Allah in repentance find guidance, while those whose hearts are sealed in denial are left astray as a consequence of their own rejection and unwillingness to receive the message.

translation: Those who have believed and whose hearts find tranquility in the remembrance of Allah. Indeed, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find tranquility.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith is not merely intellectual assent but is accompanied by inner peace and spiritual contentment that arises specifically from remembering and being conscious of Allah. The repetition of the principle underscores that the tranquility of the heart is causally dependent on maintaining awareness of the Divine—suggesting that disconnection from this remembrance is the root cause of anxiety and spiritual unease, while constant consciousness of Allah's presence and attributes is the remedy for the restless soul seeking meaning and security.

translation: Those who have believed and done righteous deeds - for them is good tidings and an excellent return (to their Lord).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith must be accompanied by righteous action; belief alone without good deeds is insufficient. The 'good tidings' (Tooba) and 'excellent return' refer to the spiritual rewards and ultimate success in the afterlife that await those who combine sincere faith with virtuous conduct in this life. The verse establishes the fundamental principle that belief and action are inseparable components of a believer's journey towards Allah.

translation: Thus We have sent you among a community before which other communities have passed away, so that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say: 'He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Prophet's mission follows the pattern of all previous prophets, whose peoples similarly rejected the message of divine mercy. The juxtaposition of the people's disbelief with the Prophet's declaration of absolute reliance upon Allah and rejection of all other deities emphasizes that the Prophet's strength lies not in the acceptance of his people, but in his unwavering faith and complete dependence upon God alone. This teaches that a messenger's success is measured by his faithfulness to his mission, not by whether his audience believes, and that true victory comes through exclusive devotion to the One God rather than through worldly approval.

translation: And even if We had sent down to them a Qur'an upon which the mountains moved, or the earth was split apart, or the dead were made to speak - nay, but to Allah belongs all command. Have those who believed not known that had Allah willed, He would have guided all the people? And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck by disasters for what they have done, or disasters will land near their homes, until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not break His promise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur'an's power lies not in its supernatural effects on creation, but in its truth and clarity of guidance. Guidance is ultimately a matter of divine will, and disbelief naturally brings about its consequences through the laws Allah has established in creation. The verse teaches that Muslims should not despair about the disbelievers' rejection, as Allah's plan unfolds according to His perfect timing and immutable promise, regardless of the signs given.

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them. So how was My punishment?
interpretation: This verse reassures Prophet Muhammad that mockery of messengers is not new, and serves as a warning that while Allah grants the disbelievers time and opportunity to repent, He ultimately seizes them with His punishment. The rhetorical question emphasizes the certainty and severity of divine retribution, implying that those who mock the current messenger should reflect on the fate of those who mocked previous messengers.

translation: Is He who keeps watch over every soul and knows what it has earned [like the idols they associate with Him]? Yet they assign partners to Allah. Say, 'Name them! Or are you informing Him of something He does not know on earth, or merely speaking empty words?' Rather, their deeds have been made to appear good to those who disbelieve, and they have been turned away from the path. And whoever Allah causes to go astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and sovereignty over all human actions and their consequences, contrasting His perfect justice with the futility of polytheism. The verse teaches that those who reject Allah's oneness are self-deceived by their desires and actions, which have been beautified to them by their own spiritual blindness, thereby removing their ability to perceive truth—a state of misguidance that results from their own rejection of signs and is beyond remedy.

translation: For them is punishment in this worldly life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. And they will have no protector from Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of divine justice, warning that wrongdoers face consequences both in this life and eternally in the next. The phrase 'more severe' (أشق) indicates that while worldly punishment may seem significant, the Hereafter's punishment is qualitatively and quantitatively greater. The final clause establishes that no power, authority, or intermediary can shield them from Allah's judgment, underscoring absolute divine sovereignty and the futility of seeking refuge anywhere but with God through repentance.

translation: The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: beneath it rivers flow, its fruits are perpetual, and its shade (is perpetual). That is the outcome for those who are righteous, and the outcome for the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse establishes a contrast between the ultimate destinies of the righteous and the disbelievers by presenting a vivid, sensory description of Paradise. The emphasis on perpetual provision (eternal fruits) and perpetual comfort (eternal shade) underscores that righteousness leads to endless blessing without deprivation or hardship. By juxtaposing Paradise with Hell as the respective outcomes (عقبى), the verse emphasizes that one's moral choices in this life have eternal consequences, motivating the listener to cultivate taqwa (God-consciousness) as the means to secure this permanent abode of peace and abundance.

translation: And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you, but among the factions are some who deny part of it. Say, 'I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divided reception of the Qur'an among different communities: some believers from among the People of the Book recognize the truth of the revelation and are gladdened by it, while others among various factions selectively reject portions of it according to their desires. The Prophet is instructed to respond to this rejection with unwavering clarity about his singular mission - to call all people to pure monotheism without associating partners with Allah. The emphasis on 'I have only been commanded' underscores that the Prophet is bound by divine instruction, not by the acceptance or rejection of those he addresses, making his duty independent of people's responses. This reflects the core Islamic principle that religious truth and the call to monotheism stand absolute regardless of how different groups receive or deny them.

translation: And thus We have revealed it as an Arabic judgment. And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have no protector from Allah and no defender.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and perfection of the Qur'an as a source of law and guidance revealed in the Arabic language, and it contains a serious warning to the Prophet (and by extension to all believers) against abandoning the truth in favor of following the whims and desires of people, regardless of their status or pressure. The verse stresses the absolute sovereignty of Allah and the reality that no one can protect or save those who turn away from divine guidance, establishing that adherence to revelation is the only safe path.

translation: And certainly We sent messengers before you, and We made for them wives and children. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a decree.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the prophets before Muhammad were human beings with natural human experiences like marriage and offspring, emphasizing their humanity despite their prophetic mission. The verse then clarifies that miracles and signs are not within the autonomous power of the messengers themselves, but rather require divine permission and occur according to Allah's predetermined wisdom and timing. This serves to redirect focus from the messenger to Allah as the source of all miraculous signs, and emphasizes that Allah's plan unfolds according to a precise schedule that He alone determines.

translation: Allah effaces what He wills and establishes [what He wills]; and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse speaks to Allah's absolute sovereignty over all knowledge and reality. The 'Mother of the Book' (Umm al-Kitab) refers to the Preserved Tablet, which contains the complete record of all that occurs. The verse teaches that while Allah erases and establishes things in the earthly realm—whether commands, legislation, or the manifestation of events—the ultimate and eternal knowledge of all things remains preserved with Him in their original form. This reconciles human experience of change and variability with divine omniscience, suggesting that temporal alterations do not affect Allah's perfect, unchanging knowledge of all matters, past and future.

translation: And if We show you some of what We promise them, or We cause you to die, then upon you is only the conveyance (of the message), and upon Us is the reckoning.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the Prophet's responsibility is limited to clearly communicating God's message to humanity, regardless of whether he witnesses the fulfillment of God's promises of punishment or reward in this life, or whether he passes away before seeing them. The ultimate judgment and accountability of people belongs to God alone. This absolves the Prophet of the burden of ensuring outcomes and emphasizes that his duty is faithfulness in transmission of the message, not control over results.

translation: Do they not see that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders? And Allah judges; there is no one to reverse His judgment. And He is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's sovereignty over the world through the observable phenomenon of lands being conquered and diminished through military conquest and territorial loss. The 'reduction from the borders' serves as a metaphorical and literal sign of divine authority over worldly affairs, demonstrating that the rise and fall of civilizations follow divine judgment rather than chance. The verse emphasizes that resistance to Allah's decree is futile, as His verdicts are irreversible and He executes justice with perfect knowledge and swiftness, thereby calling the disbelievers to recognize the signs of divine power in the apparent instability of earthly kingdoms.

translation: And indeed, those before them had plotted, but to Allah belongs all plotting. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will come to know for whom is the final outcome of the abode.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty over all human schemes and deceptions. While human beings may devise their plots and stratagems, ultimately all power and control belong to Allah alone. The verse reassures the believers that despite the machinations of the disbelievers and those who came before, Allah is fully aware of every deed and intention, and will ultimately judge affairs according to justice. The disbelievers will eventually witness the consequences of their actions and recognize that true victory and dwelling belong only to those who obey Allah.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and [whoever has knowledge of the Scripture].''
interpretation: This verse addresses the rejection faced by the Prophet Muhammad from disbelievers who denied his divine mission. The response given emphasizes that the Prophet's legitimacy does not depend on human acceptance or acknowledgment. By invoking Allah as the witness and invoking those with knowledge of Scripture (referring to righteous believers and scholars), the verse establishes that truth stands independent of rejection, and that genuine understanding of the revealed scriptures confirms the veracity of the message. The disbelievers' denial does not negate the Prophet's mission; rather, it is their loss, while those with true knowledge recognize and attest to his authenticity.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Alif-Lam-Ra. This is a Book which We have revealed to you in order that you might lead mankind out of darkness into light, by the permission of their Lord, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Qur'an's fundamental purpose: to serve as divine guidance that transforms human consciousness from ignorance and moral darkness to enlightenment and righteous understanding. The mention of 'by the permission of their Lord' indicates that while the Prophet is the messenger conveying the message, true guidance and acceptance ultimately depend on Allah's will, teaching humility about the limits of human agency in spiritual matters. The attributes 'the Almighty, the Praiseworthy' underscore that the path being revealed leads to recognition of Allah's power and deserves absolute praise, emphasizing that submission to this divine path is the ultimate expression of wisdom and gratitude.

translation: Allah is He to Whom belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah's absolute sovereignty and ownership of all creation in the heavens and on earth, emphasizing that all dominion belongs to Him alone. The warning of severe punishment directed at disbelievers underscores the consequences of rejecting Allah's lordship and the reality of His complete authority - those who deny His oneness and fail to submit to His will face intense torment. The verse serves as both a declaration of divine power and a stern admonition against disbelief.

translation: Those who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter and turn away from the path of Allah and seek to make it crooked - those are in far error.
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual condition of those who prioritize material existence and physical desires over eternal consequences, actively rejecting divine guidance and seeking to distort Allah's straight path through their opposition and corruption. Their state of profound misguidance is a consequence of their fundamental choice to value transient worldly gains over the eternal truth, demonstrating that spiritual deviation stems from deliberate preference and rejection rather than mere ignorance.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, so that he might make [the message] clear to them. Then Allah causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine guidance is conveyed through clear communication in a people's own language, removing any excuse of incomprehension. The verse then presents the profound theological principle that while Allah provides clarity through messengers, ultimate guidance and misguidance remain within Allah's absolute will and wisdom. This reflects the balance between human responsibility (understanding a clear message) and divine sovereignty (the final determination of who receives true guidance), illustrating that Allah's wisdom encompasses both the means of communication and the outcomes, which transcend human limited perspective.

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs, saying: 'Bring your people out from darkness into light, and remind them of the Days of Allah.' Indeed, in that are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the fundamental mission of divine guidance is to liberate people from the darkness of ignorance, misguidance, and disbelief into the light of knowledge, faith, and understanding. The reminder of 'the Days of Allah' refers to the lessons from divine judgments and consequences in history—both punishments and rewards—which serve as warnings and encouragements for those who possess both spiritual patience (sabr) and gratitude (shukr), qualities that enable one to perceive and benefit from divine signs.

translation: And when Moses said to his people: 'Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were imposing upon you a terrible punishment, slaughtering your sons and keeping alive your women. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and remembrance of God's blessings by reminding the Israelites of their deliverance from Egyptian oppression. The severe afflictions they endured—forced labor, infanticide of male children, and enslavement of women—are presented as a trial that tested their faith, making their salvation all the more significant as a demonstration of God's mercy and power over tyranny. The invocation to remember serves as a spiritual lesson that recognizing and acknowledging divine blessings strengthens faith and develops consciousness of God's sovereignty.

translation: And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed My punishment is severe.'
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental principle of divine reciprocal justice: gratitude (shukr) toward Allah's blessings is rewarded with increase and abundance, while ingratitude and denial (kufr) result in severe punishment. The verse emphasizes human accountability and the direct consequences of one's response to divine favor, teaching that the direction of one's life—whether toward prosperity or hardship—is fundamentally determined by whether one acknowledges and appreciates God's blessings or rejects them.

translation: And Moses said, 'If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, Allah is free from need and praiseworthy.'
interpretation: Moses reminds his people that their disbelief does not diminish Allah's perfection or affect His dominion, as Allah is self-sufficient and independent of creation. This statement serves to emphasize the consequence of ingratitude: that rejecting Allah's signs and guidance is ultimately a loss for humanity alone, while Allah's greatness, glory, and praiseworthiness remain absolute regardless of human acceptance or rejection.

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those who were before you - the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud, and those after them? None knows them except Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands over their mouths and said, 'Indeed, we have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent, and indeed, we are in doubt about that to which you call us - suspicious doubt.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recurring pattern of human rejection of divine guidance throughout history, illustrating that disbelief is not a new phenomenon but a persistent choice made by communities when confronted with clear evidential signs. The gesture of placing hands over their mouths symbolizes their willful refusal to listen and their defensive closure to the message, demonstrating that their disbelief stemmed not from lack of clarity in the message but from deliberate rejection and stubborn doubt rooted in suspicion of the truth itself.

translation: Their messengers said: 'Is there doubt concerning Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you that He may forgive you your sins and delay you until an appointed term.' They said: 'You are nothing but human beings like us. You wish to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship. Then bring us a clear authority.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the fundamental nature of the conflict between divine guidance and human resistance: the messengers appeal to rational evidence of Allah's existence through creation itself, offering forgiveness and divine mercy as motivation for faith, yet the people reject them not on intellectual grounds but through social conformity and ancestral allegiance. The people's demand for 'clear authority' reveals that their skepticism is not truly epistemic but rather rooted in tribal pride and the fear of abandoning inherited practices, exposing how the rejection of truth often stems from spiritual stubbornness masquerading as intellectual rigor.

translation: Their messengers said to them, 'We are nothing but human beings like you, but Allah confers His favor upon whom He wills from among His servants. And it is not for us to bring you any authority except by the permission of Allah. And in Allah let the believers put their trust.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the epistemological humility required of believers and messengers alike—that the transmission of divine truth does not depend on the messenger's inherent superiority or independent authority, but solely on God's will and permission. The phrase 'We are nothing but human beings like you' serves not as a limitation but as a crucial clarification that divine guidance flows through human vessels without requiring them to possess superhuman qualities or autonomous power, thereby directing all ultimate reliance and trust toward God alone rather than toward the messenger as an intermediary source of authority.

translation: And why should we not rely upon Allah when He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely be patient upon what you have caused us to suffer. And upon Allah let those who rely [truly] rely.
interpretation: This verse exemplifies the spiritual fortitude of the believing servants who, despite persecution and harm, maintain their unwavering trust in Allah and commitment to His path. The passage teaches that true reliance (tawakkul) upon Allah is not merely passive acceptance, but an active choice to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity. By questioning why they should not trust in Allah after receiving divine guidance, the speakers establish that reliance on Allah and patience in persecution are inseparable expressions of faith, demonstrating that the ultimate success of the believer lies not in avoiding harm, but in maintaining their trust in Allah's wisdom and providence despite it.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers: 'We will surely drive you out from our land, or you must return to our religion.' Then their Lord revealed to them: 'We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle of justice and retribution: when the disbelievers reject the messengers and resort to threats and coercion to suppress the truth, Allah responds with a firm declaration of the inevitable destruction of the oppressors. The verse demonstrates that resistance to divine guidance, coupled with the attempt to eliminate or silence those who convey it, triggers God's decisive judgment—a warning that no matter how powerful the oppressors appear, they cannot escape divine punishment for their transgression and injustice.

translation: And We will cause you to dwell in the earth after them. That is for whoever fears My standing (before Me) and fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse conveys that Allah's promise of inheritance of the land and dominion is contingent upon moral and spiritual conduct—specifically the fear of standing before Allah in judgment and the fear of His punishment. The verse emphasizes that worldly success and settlement are not arbitrary gifts but are earned through conscious reverence for Allah and accountability before Him, suggesting that true human flourishing and stability come through maintaining awareness of divine justice and consequences.

translation: And they sought victory [through prayer], but every stubborn tyrant was disappointed.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate failure of those who persistently reject faith and oppose God's truth. Despite their outward strength and dominance in worldly affairs, arrogant and obstinate rulers are ultimately defeated because they lack the spiritual foundation and divine support that comes with submission to God. Their apparent power is rendered hollow and ineffective in the face of God's will. The verse emphasizes that true victory comes not through tyranny or stubbornness, but through faith and reliance on God, while those who refuse guidance and persist in rebellion inevitably face disappointment and ruin.

translation: Behind him is Hell, and he will be given to drink from the water of festering pus,
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment of the disbeliever in the Hereafter, emphasizing the inescapable nature of Hell's torment. The image of Hell being 'behind him' suggests that it is an inevitable and ever-present reality he cannot escape or turn away from. The specific punishment of drinking purulent water (pus) represents the ultimate humiliation and disgust of the punishment, emphasizing that Hell's torments are not merely physical pain but also profound degradation and despair. This vivid imagery is meant to awaken the conscience and compel reflection on the consequences of rejecting God's guidance in this life.

translation: He sips it but can barely swallow it. Death comes to him from every direction, yet he does not die. And beyond that awaits a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse depicts the spiritual and psychological torment of the disbeliever in the Hereafter, particularly those who amassed wealth unlawfully. The imagery of struggling to swallow represents the inescapability of divine consequence—no matter how one tries to find relief or escape, the punishment persists from all directions. The paradox of approaching death from every angle yet not dying illustrates the eternal nature of punishment in the Hereafter, where the soul cannot find the mercy of cessation. This conveys that divine justice is absolute and inescapable; the wrongdoer experiences continuous suffering without the relief of death, and beyond this present torment lies an even more severe punishment, emphasizing the gravity of transgression against God's laws.

translation: The example of those who disbelieved in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes that the wind carries away on a stormy day. They have no power over anything they have earned. That is the far straying.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and worthlessness of the deeds of those who reject their Lord. Just as strong winds scatter ashes into nothingness, leaving no trace or benefit, the works of disbelievers are rendered completely void and powerless in the sight of God. They possess no ability to benefit from their labors or to derive any lasting value from them, because their actions, being rooted in disbelief and separation from the Divine, lack any spiritual substance or consequence. The verse teaches that rejection of God fundamentally invalidates one's entire enterprise of living, stripping all accomplishment of meaning and consequence.

translation: Do you not see that Allah has created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Divine omnipotence and the contingency of human existence. The universe's creation with purpose and order demonstrates that humanity's continued existence is not guaranteed but depends entirely upon God's will. The reminder that Allah can replace humanity with another creation serves as a humbling warning against arrogance and disobedience, suggesting that our survival is a blessing that can be withdrawn, and should therefore inspire gratitude, humility, and righteous conduct rather than complacency or rebellion against the Creator.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes God's absolute power and unlimited capability. Whatever task or action is being referenced is not burdensome or impossible for the Almighty, highlighting that all things are easy for God and no matter how vast or complex something may seem to human understanding, it is effortless within God's infinite power and knowledge.

translation: And they will be presented before Allah altogether. Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant: 'Indeed, we were followers of you. So can you avail us anything against Allah's punishment?' They will say: 'If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is the same for us whether we show distress or patience. There is no escape for us.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the mutual recrimination and helplessness that will occur between followers and leaders on the Day of Judgment. The weak acknowledge their role as followers, holding their leaders accountable while simultaneously revealing that no one will be able to protect anyone else from divine punishment. The arrogant leaders' response exposes the futility of their position—they cannot claim ignorance as an excuse because their guidance or misguidance was tied to Allah's will, yet this does not absolve them of responsibility. The phrase 'it is the same for us whether we show distress or patience' conveys the complete hopelessness and resignation of those facing the consequences of their deeds, emphasizing that once in Allah's presence, no action or emotion can change the inevitable outcome.

translation: And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: 'Indeed, Allah promised you a promise of truth, and I promised you but broke my promise to you. I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I reject your association of me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers there is a painful punishment.'
interpretation: Satan's confession reveals that his power over humans is entirely dependent on their voluntary response to his call; he possessed no inherent authority to compel them into sin. By explicitly rejecting responsibility and shifting blame to human choice, the verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of human free will and accountability—that every individual bears personal responsibility for their decisions and cannot excuse themselves by blaming external temptation. This serves as a profound reminder that on the Day of Judgment, such excuses will be exposed as invalid, and each soul must answer for its own choices.

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein by the permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be 'Peace.'
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate reward for believers who combine faith with righteous actions - eternal residence in Paradise through divine permission, emphasizing that entry to Paradise is not by human achievement alone but by God's grace and decree, while 'Peace' as their greeting signifies the complete absence of suffering, conflict, and anxiety that characterizes the Paradise the believers will inhabit.

translation: Have you not seen how Allah sets forth a parable: a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches reach into the sky?
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of a well-rooted tree to illustrate the nature of righteous words and beliefs in the hearts of the faithful. The firm root represents the solid foundation of authentic faith and sincere intention within the believer's heart, while the branches reaching toward heaven symbolize the outward manifestations of righteousness through good deeds and moral conduct that ascend toward Allah. Together, the parable teaches that true goodness must be both internally grounded in genuine faith and externally expressed in virtuous actions, creating a harmonious balance between inward conviction and outward practice that sustains spiritual growth.

translation: It yields its fruit every season by permission of its Lord, and Allah puts forth parables for mankind so that they may remember.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Allah's creation operates in perfect, ordained cycles of productivity and fruitfulness, demonstrating that all natural processes depend upon divine permission and will. By drawing this parallel between the predictable and beneficial cycles of nature (the tree bearing fruit seasonally) and the use of parables in teaching humanity, the verse emphasizes that just as we can observe divine wisdom and care in the physical world, so too should we reflect upon the spiritual lessons contained in Allah's parables, which are specifically given to awaken our hearts and minds to remember our Creator and His guidance.

translation: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree uprooted from above the earth - it has no stability.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the nature of falsehood, disbelief, and corrupt speech using the metaphor of a tree without roots. Just as a bad tree cannot take hold in the earth and can be easily uprooted and scattered, corrupt words and false beliefs have no firm foundation in reality or in the hearts of people. They lack the lasting strength and stability that comes from truth and divine guidance, and are therefore destined to be destroyed and forgotten, unable to produce any lasting benefit or positive fruit.

translation: Allah keeps firm those who have believed, with the firm word, in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. And Allah lets the wrongdoers go astray. And Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the divine principle of spiritual steadfastness and moral accountability: Allah grants unwavering conviction and resolute faith to the believers through adherence to divine truth, protecting them from spiritual wavering both in this life and the next, while those who persist in injustice and wrongdoing are allowed by Allah to further distance themselves from guidance as a consequence of their choices, ultimately affirming that all outcomes rest entirely within Allah's sovereign will and wisdom.

translation: Have you not considered those who have exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and have led their people to the abode of destruction?
interpretation: This verse condemns those who reject Allah's blessings and guidance, replacing them with ingratitude and denial. By doing so, they not only distance themselves from divine mercy but actively mislead their entire communities toward ruin and perdition, demonstrating how the rejection of truth becomes a corrupting force that spreads destruction beyond the individual to the collective society.

translation: Hell - they will burn in it. And what an evil place of settlement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe punishment and consequences of rejecting God's guidance, depicting Hell as a place of torment that the disbelievers will experience, while also highlighting the eternal nature of their suffering by describing it as an utterly wretched and permanent abode, serving as a warning about the gravity of turning away from divine truth.

translation: And they have made for Allah equals to lead (people) astray from His way. Say, 'Enjoy (yourselves), for indeed, your destination is the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse condemns the polytheists' deliberate act of creating rivals and counterparts to Allah in worship, which they do with the explicit intention of misleading people away from monotheism and the straight path. The command to 'enjoy yourselves' is a warning that carries within it an implicit threat—their temporary enjoyment and false sense of security in this life will be followed by their inevitable punishment in the Hereafter, emphasizing that no false god or rival to Allah can save them from the final judgment.

translation: Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before there comes a Day in which there is no buying and selling, nor will there be friendship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that believers must prepare for the Day of Judgment through righteous deeds—prayer and charity—since worldly transactions and relationships will be of no avail on that day. The mention of both secret and open spending illustrates that sincerity in worship and generosity must characterize all aspects of a believer's life, whether observed or unobserved, demonstrating that preparation for the Hereafter should be comprehensive and constant rather than selective or superficial.

translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water from the sky, by which He brought forth fruits as provision for you. And He has subjected for you the ships to sail in the sea by His command, and He has subjected for you the rivers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete sovereignty and provision by highlighting the interconnected systems of creation that sustain human life. The progression from the creation of heavens and earth to the provision of water, fruits, ships, and rivers demonstrates that every means of survival and prosperity is divinely ordained and placed at humanity's disposal. The phrase 'by His command' underscores that even the natural laws governing the movement of ships and rivers operate under Allah's will, implying that gratitude and acknowledgment of divine favor should accompany the utilization of these blessings, as humanity is merely benefiting from what has been made subject to their use by divine wisdom.

translation: And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, both constantly pursuing their courses. And He has subjected to you the night and the day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's continuous provision and divine mercy toward humanity by placing the celestial bodies and the cycles of day and night in service to human needs. The word 'سخر' (subjected) conveys that these cosmic phenomena operate in perfect, unwavering obedience to divine command for the benefit of creation. By highlighting that the sun and moon are 'دائبين' (constantly pursuing), the verse underscores both the reliability of divine order and humanity's dependence on these arrangements for sustenance, navigation, and the regulation of life. This subjugation of natural forces to human benefit is presented as evidence of divine care and wisdom, inviting believers to recognize and be grateful for these blessings.

translation: And He has given you of all that you asked Him. And if you count the favors of Allah, you cannot enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is most unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the abundance of Allah's provision and blessings upon humanity, contrasting it with human ingratitude and injustice. Despite receiving all that they request and countless unquantifiable blessings, humans are characterized as inherently inclined toward wrongdoing and denial of these favors. The verse serves as a reminder of human weakness and tendency to overlook divine mercy, while underscoring the necessity of gratitude and recognition of Allah's boundless generosity.

translation: And [remember] when Abraham said: 'My Lord, make this city [Mecca] a place of security and provide me and my sons [with sustenance] that we may avoid the worship of idols.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates Abraham's deep concern for establishing monotheism and protecting his descendants from idolatry. His supplication reveals the fundamental struggle between true faith in God and the temptation of idolatry, emphasizing that security and provision from God are intrinsically linked to the preservation of pure faith. Abraham's prayer demonstrates that a righteous leader must proactively seek divine protection for his community against spiritual corruption, recognizing that material security without spiritual integrity is meaningless. The verse underscores the principle that devotion to God and rejection of false worship are prerequisites for true peace and blessing in society.

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people. So whoever follows me - he is of me. And whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reflects the speaker's (Prophet Ibrahim) acknowledgment of the spiritual struggle between guidance and misguidance, and his ultimate trust in God's wisdom. By invoking God's attributes of forgiveness and mercy in the context of those who reject his message, Ibrahim demonstrates a profound teaching: that a messenger's responsibility is to convey the truth clearly, but the final judgment of hearts and destinies rests entirely with God. The verse emphasizes that both obedience and disobedience fall within God's knowledge and plan, and that God's mercy encompasses all situations, even those of rejection and error.

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley with no cultivation near Your Sacred House, Our Lord, so they may establish prayer. Make the hearts of some people incline toward them, and provide them with fruits so that they may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound wisdom behind Ibrahim's prayer in settling his family at Mecca. His primary intention was not material prosperity but the establishment of worship ('ibadah), specifically the prayer. The request for hearts to be inclined toward them reflects the divine strategy of making Mecca a destination and center of pilgrimage through natural human inclination rather than force, demonstrating that true provision and blessing come through fulfilling Allah's purpose. The mention of gratitude at the end emphasizes that material sustenance without spiritual foundation is incomplete; true thankfulness emerges when people recognize that their provision is connected to their obedience and the sacred mission they are part of.

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare. And nothing is hidden from Allah of anything on earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute and omniscient nature of God's knowledge, which extends to all dimensions of human action—both the hidden intentions and secret thoughts as well as the open, manifest deeds. It serves to remind believers that they are eternally accountable before Allah for the entirety of their inner and outer states, leaving no room for deception or self-delusion, and thus should live with conscious awareness of divine scrutiny and maintain sincerity in all their affairs.

translation: Praise be to Allah, who has granted me in my old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: This verse expresses profound gratitude for the extraordinary blessing of fatherhood in advanced age, highlighting the miraculous nature of this gift and affirming that Allah hears and responds to the sincere prayers of His servants. The mention of both sons emphasizes the completeness of the blessing granted to Abraham, and his acknowledgment of Allah's power over what appears impossible to human capability, thereby teaching that no supplication is beyond Allah's reach and ability to grant.

translation: My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and [make] of my descendants [as well]. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: This verse expresses the spiritual aspiration to be constant in performing prayer not merely as a ritual, but as an integral part of one's identity and character, while extending this noble prayer for descendants so that piety becomes a legacy passed through generations. The supplication acknowledges that true acceptance and answered prayer depends entirely on God's will and mercy, emphasizing the servant's dependence on divine acceptance rather than relying on the sufficiency of one's own efforts.

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning will take place.
interpretation: This verse teaches that one's supplication for forgiveness should encompass not only oneself but also extend mercy and compassion to one's parents and the broader Muslim community. It reflects the Islamic principle that personal righteousness is intertwined with communal responsibility, and that seeking divine mercy is an act that acknowledges our interdependence and shared accountability before God. The specific mention of the Day of Reckoning emphasizes the urgency and gravity of seeking forgiveness while there is still opportunity in this life.

translation: And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare in horror.
interpretation: This verse warns against the misconception that God's forbearance and delay in punishing transgressors means He is heedless or indifferent to their actions. Rather, the verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge is all-encompassing, and any apparent delay in punishment is deliberate and purposeful—reserved for a specific Day of Judgment when the full consequences of their deeds will become manifest with overwhelming clarity, as represented by the fixed, wide-eyed staring of those confronted with their fate. This reframes patience and forbearance not as weakness but as divine wisdom in allowing accountability to reach its fullest expression.

translation: Hastening forward, their heads raised up, their eyes not returning to them, and their hearts are void.
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual and cognitive state of those who reject faith and turn away from guidance. The imagery of hastening forward with raised heads but unseeing eyes, combined with hearts devoid of substance (described as 'void' or 'empty air'), portrays a people who rush toward destruction with apparent confidence but lack true perception, consciousness, and spiritual depth. Their outward haste and posturing cannot compensate for their inner spiritual emptiness and blindness to truth. The verse illustrates the consequences of rejecting divine guidance: despite their apparent forward motion, they are fundamentally disconnected from understanding and spiritual reality.

translation: And warn the people of the Day when punishment will come to them, and those who wronged will say, 'Our Lord, postpone for us a near term; we will respond to Your call and follow the messengers.' Did you not swear before that you would not be overthrown?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of seeking repentance on the Day of Judgment when it is too late. Those who lived unjustly will desperately plead for another chance, promising obedience if given more time, but they will be reminded of their earlier oaths and false confidence that they would never face accountability. The verse emphasizes that the opportunity for repentance is only in this worldly life, and once the divine punishment arrives, all promises and regrets become meaningless. It serves as a warning to believers that they must not delay their obedience and righteousness, for death and the Final Day can come unexpectedly.

translation: And you dwell in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it has become clear to you how We dealt with them, and We have set forth for you examples.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of the tangible consequences of disobedience and injustice. By physically inhabiting the ruins of previous nations who committed wrongdoing, the Muslims are presented with visible evidence of divine punishment, serving as a stark warning against following the same path of transgression. The verse emphasizes that God's punishment of past peoples is not merely a historical account, but a living lesson whose physical remnants stand as perpetual reminders, and the examples provided through these ruins are meant to guide the believers away from the same errors that led to the destruction of their predecessors.

translation: And they have plotted their plot, but with Allah is their plot, and even if their plot were to remove the mountains thereby.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of human schemes and deceptions against God's will. The repetition of the word 'makr' (plot/scheme) underscores the reality that despite the elaborate and cunning plans devised by those who oppose Allah's guidance, these plans are fully known and recorded by Allah, who is all-seeing and all-knowing. The hyperbolic image of plots being powerful enough to move mountains conveys that even if such schemes possessed extraordinary strength, they would ultimately amount to nothing in the face of Allah's supreme power and divine will. The verse teaches that reliance should be placed in Allah rather than in worldly cunning, as all machinations are ultimately subject to His judgment and control.

translation: So do not think that Allah will fail to keep His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Mighty, Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute certainty and reliability of Allah's commitments to His messengers. The instruction 'do not think' addresses believers' hearts and minds, warning against doubt or skepticism regarding divine promises of victory, support, and ultimate triumph. By concluding with 'Mighty' and 'Owner of Retribution,' the verse reinforces that Allah possesses both the power to fulfill His promises and the authority to punish those who oppose His messengers, making the fulfillment of His word inevitable and unquestionable.

translation: On the Day when the earth will be changed into a different earth, and the heavens as well, and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Irresistible.
interpretation: This verse depicts the resurrection and the transformation of creation at the end of time. The replacement of the earth and heavens symbolizes the complete renewal and restructuring of the physical universe as we know it, indicating that nothing in this creation is permanent except Allah's dominion. The phrase 'they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Irresistible' emphasizes that on that Day, all creatures will stand before Allah alone with no intermediaries or places of refuge, stripped of all power and facing the One who has absolute power over all things. This conveys the certainty of Divine judgment and the futility of any resistance against Allah's will.

translation: And you will see the criminals on that Day linked together in chains.
interpretation: This verse depicts the humiliation and helplessness of the criminals on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing their complete loss of freedom and dignity.
