His swift return and repentance (inabah) demonstrates that true nobility lies not in avoiding trials, but in responding to them with humility, submission, and restoration of one's relationship with the Divine.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates how a servant of Allah seeks forgiveness and then makes a supplication for a unique blessing that would set him apart from all others. The supplication reflects an understanding that true kingship comes from Allah alone, and the qualifier 'lā yanbaghī li-aḥad min ba'dī' (will not belong to anyone after me) demonstrates both humility and recognition that such exceptional favor is entirely dependent on divine grace. By naming Allah as 'al-Wahhāb' (the Bestower), the supplicant acknowledges that all gifts originate solely from Allah's generosity, not from human effort or merit, thereby combining both the request for divine forgiveness and the recognition that extraordinary provisions are exclusively within Allah's power to grant.

translation: So We subjected the wind to him, running by his command wherever he willed, gently.
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's subjugation of the wind for Prophet Solomon as a divine gift and sign of his prophethood. The phrase 'by his command' indicates that the wind obeyed Solomon's will as a supernatural miracle, demonstrating Allah's absolute power and favor upon him. The specification that it ran 'gently' (rakhaa) emphasizes the miraculous nature of this control—the wind operated precisely as Solomon desired without harmful effects, serving his purposes of transport and other needs. This represents a test of Solomon's gratitude and wisdom in using this blessing, which complements the theme in his story of being granted extraordinary powers as a righteous king who depended upon Allah's guidance.

translation: And the devils - every builder and diver
interpretation: This verse refers to how the devils were compelled to work for Solomon, undertaking various forms of labor and skilled work. The 'builders' refers to those who construct buildings and structures, while the 'divers' refers to those who dive into the sea to retrieve treasures and pearls. The verse illustrates the supernatural subjugation of the jinn to Solomon's command, demonstrating his exceptional power granted by Allah and emphasizing that even the invisible realm of creation was made subject to his authority as a divinely chosen king.

translation: And others bound together in shackles
interpretation: This phrase refers to groups of disbelievers or prisoners who will be chained and restrained together, emphasizing their collective punishment and helpless state. The binding together in shackles symbolizes the complete loss of freedom and dignity that awaits those who reject the truth, highlighting the severity and inescapability of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief.

translation: This is Our gift; so give or withhold without any reckoning
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty over His blessings and gifts. The passage teaches that once Allah grants wealth or favors to someone, they have full discretionary authority to use it as they see fit—whether to give charitably or retain it—without being subject to divine accountability for how they dispense their own possessions. This reflects the principle that a person's ownership of their own gifts from Allah is complete and unrestricted, establishing the theological foundation for personal property rights and the voluntary nature of generosity in Islamic ethics.

translation: And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the elevated spiritual status and proximity to Allah that awaits the righteous servant of God. 'Nearness' (zulfa) signifies closeness to divine mercy and favor in the Hereafter, while 'a good place of return' (husn ma'ab) refers to a noble and blessed final destination. Together, these phrases convey that those who obey Allah will be honored with His special favor and granted the highest stations in Paradise, highlighting the divine reward system that encourages righteous conduct and steadfast faith.

translation: And mention Our servant Job, when he called upon his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and punishment."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound patience and faith of Prophet Job despite his severe afflictions. His immediate recourse to calling upon Allah—rather than despairing or blaming God—demonstrates the exemplary way a believer should respond to trials. The mention of Satan's touch emphasizes that while external forces may cause suffering, true refuge and relief come only through sincere supplication to the Almighty, establishing that faith and direct communication with God are the means through which believers transcend their suffering.

translation: Strike with your leg; this is a cool bath and a drink.
interpretation: This verse refers to a miraculous provision granted to Prophet Job (Ayyub) after his prolonged suffering and patient endurance of hardship. The command to strike the ground with his leg resulted in a spring of cool water emerging, which served both as a restorative bath for his afflicted body and as a pure drink. This miracle represents Allah's reward for steadfast patience and faith, demonstrating that divine mercy and relief come to those who remain obedient despite trials, and it symbolizes the restoration of health, dignity, and comfort after endurance of hardship.

translation: And We granted him his family and the like of them with them as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's blessing upon Prophet Ayub (Job) after his trial and affliction. The phrase indicates that Allah restored to him not only his original family but multiplied his blessings by granting him additional children and household equal in number to what he had before, as a divine grace and compassionate gift following his patient endurance. This serves as a reminder to people of sound intellect that patience in hardship is rewarded by Allah, and that divine mercy often exceeds what was lost, demonstrating that trials are temporary and Allah's generosity is boundless.

translation: And take in your hand a bundle of grass and strike with it, and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient. Excellent is the servant. Indeed, he is ever returning [to Us].
interpretation: This verse illustrates the wisdom of divine justice and mercy combined. The command to strike Job's wife with a bundle of grass—which causes no real harm—represents a way for Job to fulfill his oath while showing clemency and compassion. This demonstrates that obedience to God does not require cruelty, and that one can maintain integrity and fulfill commitments while still exercising mercy and moderation. The verse teaches that true servitude to God is characterized by patience in trial, consistent return to repentance and obedience (awwab), and the ability to balance justice with gentleness in all circumstances.

translation: And mention to them Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob - possessors of strength and vision.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to recall and honor these righteous patriarchs, emphasizing that they possessed both physical and spiritual strength ('strength' referring to their moral fortitude and capability), as well as profound spiritual insight and wisdom ('vision' referring to their deep understanding of divine truth). The phrase 'our servants' elevates their status as devoted worshippers of Allah, while the mention of these specific attributes indicates that their righteousness was not merely passive faith but was accompanied by active strength of character and clarity of spiritual perception, making them exemplars for believers to emulate in combining faith with steadfast action and discernment.

translation: Indeed, We have chosen them for a pure [quality] - the remembrance of the home [i.e., the Hereafter].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the righteous are distinguished by their constant remembrance of the afterlife, which purifies their intentions and directs their actions toward the eternal rather than the temporal. Their selection by God is characterized by this singular focus on the remembrance of the eternal abode, making it the defining feature of their spiritual excellence and the criterion by which they are distinguished from others.

translation: And indeed, they are among the chosen and the best with Us.
interpretation: This verse affirms the elevated spiritual station of certain individuals whom Allah has selected and favored. The phrase 'with Us' (عندنا) indicates divine proximity and honor, suggesting that these chosen ones possess qualities of righteousness and excellence that earn them Allah's special regard and distinction. This conveys the principle that Allah's selection of individuals is based on their moral excellence and virtue, not arbitrary factors.

translation: And remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl; and all of them were among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue and righteousness of these chosen servants of Allah, presenting them as exemplars of goodness and obedience to Allah. By mentioning them together with the descriptor 'al-akhyar' (the best/righteous), the verse underscores that righteousness is the defining characteristic that unites all the prophets and righteous servants of Allah across different times and communities, serving as an inspiration for believers to emulate their devotion and moral excellence.

translation: This is a reminder. And indeed, for the righteous there is a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a divine guidance and admonition for humanity. The assurance that the God-conscious will have an excellent final destination (Paradise) is meant to motivate believers to embrace this reminder and live according to its teachings. The verse connects the purpose of revelation with the hope of reward, establishing that acceptance of divine guidance leads to ultimate success and honor in the Hereafter.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence with their gates wide open for them
interpretation: This verse depicts the ultimate reward of the righteous in the afterlife, emphasizing both the permanence of their dwelling (Jannat Adn - eternal gardens) and the welcoming reception they will receive, symbolized by the open gates. The opening of gates signifies divine welcome, ease of entry, and the removal of all barriers between them and their reward, reflecting God's mercy and their honored status.

translation: Reclining therein, they will call therein for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: This verse describes the blessed state of the inhabitants of Paradise, emphasizing their comfort and contentment. The image of reclining (متكئين) conveys a state of ease and dignity, while their calling for abundant fruit and drink symbolizes the fulfillment of all desires and the sufficiency of their provision without want or deprivation. The abundance and variety available to them reflect the infinite generosity of Allah and the complete satisfaction that awaits the righteous in the Hereafter, where every wish is granted without effort or hardship.

translation: And with them will be maidens with modest gaze, companions of equal age.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards of the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing that the believers will be accompanied by women of virtuous character whose gaze is restrained and modest, reflecting their purity and propriety. The phrase 'companions of equal age' (atrab) suggests they are matched in their spiritual development and perfection, symbolizing harmony and compatibility in the blessed gardens of Paradise. This imagery conveys that ultimate reward includes not only material comfort but also righteous companionship characterized by virtue and dignity.

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse refers to the inevitable reality of the afterlife and divine accountability. The phrase emphasizes that the Day of Judgment is not merely a concept but an actual promise from Allah that will certainly come to pass. The declaration serves as a reminder that all deeds in this worldly life will be accounted for, and individuals will face the consequences of their actions. It underscores the certainty and inescapability of divine justice, warning humanity that the temporal nature of this world does not negate the eternal nature of what awaits in the hereafter.

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision which will never diminish.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal and inexhaustible nature of Allah's provision and blessings. It conveys the divine assurance that God's sustenance is boundless and will never run out or decrease, encouraging believers to have complete trust in Allah's unfailing generosity and care for His creation.

translation: This is so; and indeed, for the transgressors there is an evil return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences that await those who exceed bounds and reject divine guidance. The phrase "evil return" (شر مآب) refers to the ultimate destination and consequence in the afterlife for those who persist in transgression and disobedience. It serves as a warning that defiance of God's commands inevitably leads to punishment and ruin, reinforcing the Qur'anic principle that every action has consequences before God.

translation: Hellfire - they will enter it. And what an evil abode it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and undesirability of Hell as the ultimate punishment for those who reject faith and divine guidance. The phrase 'what an evil abode' (bئs al-mihād) expresses strong condemnation of Hell as a dwelling place, underscoring that it is the worst possible destination and outcome for humanity, serving as a warning of the consequences of turning away from God's path.

translation: This [is the punishment], so let them taste it - scalding water and pus
interpretation: This verse describes a severe punishment in the Hereafter, warning of the consequences of disbelief and wickedness. The 'scalding water' (hamim) and 'pus' (ghassaq) represent the intensified torment that awaits the deniers, emphasizing that such suffering is a direct result of their own actions and choices in the worldly life. The verse uses vivid, concrete imagery to awaken the conscience and instill fear of Allah's justice.

translation: and other [things] of similar kind in pairs
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of diverse things in complementary pairs or matched forms, emphasizing God's design of creation in balanced and symmetrical ways. It suggests that creation operates through a principle of duality and pairing, reflecting divine wisdom in how different creatures and things are structured to work together in harmony and serve specific purposes in the cosmic order.

translation: This is a group bursting in upon you. No welcome to them! Indeed, they are the fuel of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene on the Day of Judgment where the people of Hell rush forward in confusion. The phrase 'This is a group bursting in upon you' refers to the sudden arrival of the condemned in Hell alongside those already there. The rejection expressed through 'No welcome to them' emphasizes their utter desolation and the absence of any comfort or reception. The final clause 'Indeed, they are the fuel of the Fire' conveys a profound warning about the eternal punishment of the wrongdoers - they are not merely inhabitants of Hell but rather the very substance that perpetually fuels it, signifying both the completeness of their destruction and the perpetual nature of their torment.

translation: They said, 'Rather, you [do not have welcome]. No welcome to you! You have brought this upon us. How evil is this destination!'
interpretation: This verse reveals the mutual recrimination and blame that occurs between the transgressors and those who led them astray on the Day of Judgment. The verse illustrates the complete breakdown of false alliances and relationships that were based on worldly desires and disobedience. Those who followed are rejecting those who led them, showing that neither party will show mercy or sympathy to the other in the Hereafter. The phrase 'how evil is this destination' emphasizes the despair and regret that characterizes Hell, where all bonds of loyalty dissolve and each soul confronts the consequences of their choices without support or consolation.

translation: They said: 'Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase for him the punishment doubled in the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the people of Hell expressing their anguished plea, cursing those responsible for misleading them away from truth. The verse illustrates a profound consequence of following misguidance: the damned will not only suffer their own punishment but will turn their anger upon those who led them astray, seeking severe retribution for them. This serves as a powerful warning about the gravity of leading others away from the path of Allah and the ripple effects of one's influence on others, extending accountability and punishment beyond oneself.

translation: And they said: "Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the perspective of the inhabitants of Paradise observing that certain individuals they considered to be among the worst of people in their earthly life are not present among them. This statement expresses the surprise and realization that those deemed irredeemable sinners did not enter Paradise, confirming the justice of divine judgment and the distinction between the truly wicked who were denied entry and the believers who were admitted. It serves as a vindication of their faith and a testimony to the truthfulness of the divine separation between the righteous and the unrighteous in the Hereafter.

translation: Did We take them in mockery, or have their eyes turned away from the truth?
interpretation: This verse rhetorically questions whether Allah made these people objects of ridicule or whether they themselves have willfully turned away from understanding the signs, implying personal accountability for their spiritual blindness rather than divine mockery—emphasizing that their failure to perceive truth stems from their own aversion and deliberate turning away from guidance.

translation: Indeed, that is the truth - the disputation of the people of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the inevitable reality of the disputes and quarrels that will occur among the inhabitants of Hell. The phrase 'that is the truth' emphasizes the certainty of this consequence, serving as a reminder that those who reject faith and commit sins will face not only physical punishment but also internal conflict and blame among themselves in the afterlife. The verse underscores the justice of divine punishment, where sinners will turn against one another, further intensifying their suffering and regret.

translation: Say, 'I am only a warner, and there is no god except Allah, the One, the Irresistible.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger of warning to humanity about the consequences of turning away from Allah, while establishing the core Islamic principle of strict monotheism (tawhid). The attributes 'al-Wahid' (the One) and 'al-Qahhar' (the Irresistible/Overpowering) underscore that Allah alone possesses absolute unity without partners and supreme power over all creation, making obedience to Him and His message inevitable and inescapable.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the Mighty, the Forgiving One
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and dominion over all creation, while simultaneously highlighting His dual attributes of power and mercy. The mention of being 'Mighty' demonstrates His overwhelming strength and authority, while 'Forgiving' reveals His boundless compassion toward His servants, suggesting that despite His supreme power to punish, He chooses mercy and forgiveness as defining characteristics of His nature.

translation: Say: 'It is a great news.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an itself as a momentous and life-changing message from Allah. The Prophet is commanded to declare that the Qur'an is a matter of supreme importance that transcends ordinary understanding, serving as a divine guidance that calls humanity to recognize the oneness of Allah and the reality of the resurrection. The phrase emphasizes the gravity and transformative power of the revelation, inviting listeners to recognize its profound significance in their spiritual and moral development.

translation: You are from it turning away.
interpretation: This phrase describes a state of heedlessness and deliberate avoidance, where people consciously disregard or ignore what is being presented to them. The turning away suggests both a physical and spiritual distance from divine guidance or truth, indicating willful neglect rather than mere forgetfulness. It conveys the idea of rejecting or refusing to engage with something important, whether it be a warning, a message, or the signs of God.

translation: I had no knowledge of the highest assembly when they disputed among themselves.
interpretation: This verse, spoken by Prophet Muhammad, conveys profound humility regarding the unseen realm of the angels. It emphasizes that the Prophet's knowledge comes only from revelation granted to him by God, not from personal observation or speculation about the celestial council. This serves to distinguish between revealed knowledge (which is reliable and authoritative) and human conjecture about divine matters, teaching that one should not claim knowledge beyond what has been explicitly revealed, while also establishing the Prophet's credibility as a messenger rather than an independent source of information about the unseen.

translation: It is not revealed to me except that I am only a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet's (peace be upon him) humility and clarity of mission. He is emphasizing that his role is limited to conveying the divine message and warning humanity, and he does not claim knowledge of the unseen or supernatural powers. This establishes the distinction between the messenger and the message—the Prophet is merely a human instrument chosen to warn people clearly, while true knowledge and authority belong to Allah alone. This interpretation underscores the Prophet's consistency in refusing to make claims beyond his divinely appointed function as a messenger.

translation: When your Lord said to the angels: 'Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay.'
interpretation: This verse marks the beginning of creation of mankind and establishes the foundational relationship between God, the angels, and humanity. God's announcement to the angels emphasizes divine sovereignty and the intentionality behind human creation, setting the stage for humanity's unique role and purpose in creation despite being fashioned from humble material, which serves as a humbling reminder of human origin and dependence upon the Creator.

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse describes the completion of Adam's creation as a perfect form, after which Allah breathed His spirit into him, conferring upon him a unique dignity and honor above other creatures. The command for the angels to prostrate to Adam signifies the special status and vicegerency that Allah granted to humanity, establishing humanity's position as honored representatives on earth, distinct from the rest of creation through the divine spirit placed within them.

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely
interpretation: This verse describes the angels' obedience and submission to God's command. Their collective prostration demonstrates the unity of creation in submitting to the divine will, and emphasizes that there is no dissent or hesitation among the angels in fulfilling God's orders. The repetition of 'all of them entirely' (kuluhum ajmacun) stresses the completeness and unanimity of their obedience, serving as a model of perfect servitude to the Almighty.

translation: Except Iblis, who was arrogant and was among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the nature of Iblis's rebellion against Allah's command through two interconnected characteristics: arrogance (istikbar) and disbelief (kufr). His refusal to prostrate to Adam despite Allah's command was not merely an act of disobedience, but stemmed from a fundamental spiritual disease—pride that blinded him to the wisdom and authority of his Creator. The mention of his arrogance preceding his disbelief suggests that his pride was the root cause of his rejection of faith, revealing how spiritual arrogance inevitably leads one away from submission to Allah and truth itself.

translation: He said, 'O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My own hands? Did you grow arrogant, or were you among the exalted?'
interpretation: This verse reveals God's direct confrontation with Iblis after his refusal to bow to Adam, emphasizing both the divine act of creation (Adam being created by God's hands) and the gravity of Iblis's transgression. The dual question structure—asking whether arrogance or a false sense of superiority motivated his disobedience—presents the root cause of Iblis's fall as a spiritual disease of the soul: either pride in refusing to humble himself before God's command, or an inflated self-estimation of his own status that placed him above obedience. The question format itself serves as a rebuke, making Iblis confront the irrationality and indefensibility of his position, as there is no legitimate excuse for disobeying God's direct command.

translation: He said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'
interpretation: This verse reveals the arrogance and false reasoning of Iblis, who relied on his supposed superiority based on his material composition rather than submitting to God's command. His argument that fire is inherently superior to clay reflects how pride blinds one to the reality that nobility comes not from one's origin, but from obedience to God and moral character. Iblis's refusal to prostrate to Adam, despite being commanded to do so, demonstrates how intellectual superiority without humility and submission leads to destruction and eternal wretchedness.

translation: He said, 'Then get out of it, for indeed, you are expelled.'
interpretation: This verse represents Allah's command to Satan (Iblis) to leave Paradise after his refusal to obey the divine command to prostrate to Adam. The word 'رجيم' (rajim) meaning 'expelled' or 'accursed' signifies Satan's permanent banishment from Allah's mercy and his status as an outcast, establishing the eternal nature of his punishment and his separation from the divine presence due to his arrogance and disobedience.

translation: And indeed, My curse is upon you until the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse, spoken by Allah to Iblis (Satan) after his refusal to prostrate to Adam, establishes that Satan's punishment and rejection from Divine mercy are permanent and irrevocable until the final day. The curse signifies complete abandonment by Allah's grace, establishing the absolute nature of Satan's condemnation as a consequence of his arrogant defiance and disobedience, serving as a warning about the severity of rejecting divine commands.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day when they will be resurrected.'
interpretation: This verse expresses Iblis's request for God to delay his punishment until the Day of Judgment, revealing how those who rebel against God attempt to negotiate or defer the consequences of their disobedience, yet ultimately remain bound by God's divine will and predetermined timeline for accountability.

translation: He said, 'Then indeed, you are of those given respite.'
interpretation: This verse represents Allah's response to Iblis's request for delay until the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'from those given respite' (min al-munẓarīn) indicates that Allah has granted Iblis's supplication for a temporary reprieve, allowing him to remain alive until the appointed time of judgment. This demonstrates a divine principle: that those who persist in arrogance and rejection may be given time to continue their actions, which ultimately becomes a test and evidence against them. The respite is not a favor but a trial, as Iblis will use this time to lead humans astray, thereby proving his own damnation and the justness of his eventual punishment.

translation: Until the Day of the Appointed Time
interpretation: This phrase refers to the Day of Judgment (Yawm al-Qiyamah), which is known only to Allah. It signifies that all matters appointed by Allah have a fixed term, and on the Day of the Appointed Time, all souls will meet their reckoning. This emphasizes the certainty of the Final Hour while highlighting that its exact timing remains with Allah alone, serving as a reminder to humans of their accountability and the transient nature of worldly life.

translation: He said, 'By Your might, I will surely seduce them all'
interpretation: Iblis accepts Allah's challenge and declares his rebellious intention to lead humanity astray, swearing by Allah's own power. This verse reveals Iblis's arrogant defiance and his resolve to prove that humans are unworthy of Allah's favor, while simultaneously acknowledging that all power ultimately belongs to Allah alone, even as he uses it as the object of his oath of disobedience.

translation: Except Your servants among them, the sincere ones
interpretation: This phrase refers to the exception of those true servants of Allah who maintain unwavering devotion and sincerity in their faith, despite the general corruption or waywardness of others. It emphasizes that among a group prone to error or transgression, there remain those whose hearts are purified and whose obedience is genuine and uncontaminated by ulterior motives or hypocrisy.

translation: He said, 'By the truth, and the truth I speak.'
interpretation: This verse expresses a solemn oath by which the speaker emphasizes the absolute truthfulness and reliability of what they are about to say. The repetition of 'the truth' (al-haqq) serves to reinforce the gravity and certainty of the statement, indicating that the speaker is invoking truth itself as both the medium of their oath and the content of their message. This linguistic construction conveys both divine authority and unwavering commitment to veracity.

translation: I will certainly fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all together.
interpretation: This verse represents Allah's declaration of punishment against Iblis (Satan) for his disobedience and arrogance in refusing to prostrate to Adam. The verse emphasizes that Iblis's punishment is not solitary but extends to all those who choose to follow his path of rebellion against Allah's guidance. It conveys that Hell will be populated by those who deliberately reject faith and follow Satan's whispers, serving as a warning about the ultimate consequence of persistent disobedience and turning away from divine guidance. The comprehensive nature of 'all together' underscores that this fate applies universally to all who align themselves with Iblis's rejected stance.

translation: Say, 'I do not ask you for any reward for it, nor am I among those who pretend or fabricate.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet's sincere and disinterested mission, establishing that his call to faith is purely for the sake of Allah and the welfare of humanity, free from any personal gain or pretense. By denying any compensation and rejecting artificiality, the verse authenticates the message and invites believers to recognize the truthfulness of the prophetic mission, encouraging them to respond based on genuine conviction rather than suspicion of hidden motives.

translation: It is naught but a reminder for all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves a universal function as a message of guidance and admonition intended for all of humanity and creation. By describing it as merely a 'reminder,' the verse highlights that the Qur'an calls people back to fundamental truths about God and morality that should already resonate within human conscience and reason, rather than presenting entirely novel concepts. The phrase 'for all the worlds' underscores the Qur'an's comprehensive relevance transcending time, culture, and nation, suggesting that its principles and warnings apply universally to all people regardless of their circumstances or background.

translation: And you will surely know the news of it after a while
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth and consequences of events will eventually become clear and evident, even if understanding is delayed. It conveys the principle that time reveals what is hidden and clarifies what was uncertain, and that patience in awaiting knowledge of outcomes is necessary, as divine wisdom operates according to its own timeline rather than human expectations.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, affirming that its revelation comes directly from Allah who possesses supreme power (Al-'Aziz) and perfect wisdom (Al-Hakim), thereby assuring believers of the authenticity and infallibility of the scripture's guidance.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, sincere to Him in faith.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundation of monotheistic worship: that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah containing ultimate truth, and therefore all devotion and service must be directed exclusively to Allah alone, without associating partners with Him or allowing worldly concerns to dilute one's sincerity. The command to worship with sincere faith means that internal intention and external action must align in complete dedication to Allah, rejecting all forms of hypocrisy, ostentation, and divided loyalties.

translation: Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion. And those who have taken protectors other than Him [say], "We do not worship them except that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a liar and disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse establishes that sincere monotheism and undivided worship belong exclusively to Allah, while addressing the spiritual delusion of those who seek intermediaries. Those who venerate saints, idols, or other entities while claiming they only do so to draw closer to Allah are engaged in self-deception; Allah will ultimately judge between believers and those who engage in shirk (associating partners with Allah), and such guidance is withheld from those who persist in denying the truth while maintaining false claims about their intentions.

translation: If Allah had intended to take a son, He would have chosen from His creation what He willed. Exalted is He! He is Allah, the One, the Irresistible.
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim that Allah has a son by presenting a logical argument: if Allah were to choose a son from His creation, He would select according to His will and wisdom. However, the fact that Allah is transcendent, unique, and all-powerful demonstrates that He is beyond such human-like relationships. The emphasis on His oneness and dominion serves to highlight the absurdity of associating partners or offspring with the Creator, establishing His absolute uniqueness and self-sufficiency as the foundation of Islamic monotheism.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a term appointed. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's creation operates with perfect order and purpose, demonstrating both His absolute power and His wisdom. The cyclical movement of night and day illustrates the precision and justice built into creation, while the subjugation of the celestial bodies serves humanity and reinforces Allah's dominion. The description of Allah as 'Al-Aziz' (The Mighty) reflects His complete control over creation, and 'Al-Ghaffar' (The Forgiving) suggests that despite His overwhelming power, He shows mercy and forgiveness to His creation, inviting reflection on the balance between His justice and compassion in the cosmic order.

translation: He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and He sent down for you of the cattle eight pairs. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs sovereignty. There is no deity except Him. So how are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of human origin and divine creative power as a foundation for rejecting polytheism and recognizing Allah's absolute lordship. By highlighting that all humans stem from a single soul and are created through a precise developmental process in darkness, the verse underscores human equality and shared origin, while simultaneously demonstrating Allah's complete mastery over creation. The reference to the 'three darknesses' (the darkness of the womb, the amniotic sac, and the placenta) illustrates the hidden nature of creation and Allah's knowledge of what occurs beyond human perception. The verse's conclusion questions how humanity can turn away from monotheism when confronted with such clear evidence of Allah's unique creative power and dominion.

translation: If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Self-Sufficient beyond need of you. And He does not approve disbelief for His servants. But if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of individual accountability before God while emphasizing that belief and gratitude are ultimately matters of personal choice and responsibility. It illustrates that God's perfection is unaffected by human acceptance or rejection of faith, yet He desires guidance and gratitude from His servants. The statement that no soul bears another's burden affirms that each person stands alone before God with their own deeds, negating any notion of inherited sin or vicarious salvation, and the promise of divine knowledge of hidden intentions demonstrates that God's judgment transcends mere outward actions to encompass the true state of hearts.

translation: And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He grants him a favor from Himself, he forgets that for which he called upon Him before, and he sets up rivals to Allah to mislead [people] from His way. Say: 'Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed, you are among the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ingratitude and inconsistency of human nature in its spiritual negligence. When a person faces adversity, desperation drives them to sincere supplication to God, yet once relief comes and blessings are bestowed, they promptly forget their former devotion and abandon their reliance on God alone. Instead of recognizing the source of their blessings and maintaining gratitude and obedience, they revert to associating partners with Allah and pursuing false gods or worldly desires. The verse reveals how material comfort becomes a trial that exposes the weakness of faith when it is rooted in self-interest rather than genuine conviction. The final command to say 'enjoy your disbelief for a little while' is a stark reminder of the transient nature of worldly pleasures and a warning of the inevitable divine punishment that awaits those who persist in such ingratitude and idolatry.

translation: Is one who is devout during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, [equal to one who does not]? Say: 'Are those who know and those who do not know equal?' Only those of understanding will remember.
interpretation: This verse establishes that spiritual devotion and knowledge are not trivial matters, but rather they are the qualities that fundamentally distinguish people. The implicit comparison is between the person engaged in night worship—combining fear of God's punishment and hope for His mercy—and the ignorant person. The verse teaches that true knowledge is inseparable from spiritual awareness and that intellectual understanding of divine truths manifests in righteous action and devotion. The emphasis on 'those of understanding' (ulu al-albab) indicates that recognizing this distinction requires intellectual and spiritual acuity, suggesting that comprehending the value of knowledge and piety is itself a mark of wisdom.

translation: Say, 'O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world, there is good; and the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without measure.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that piety and righteousness toward God yield tangible blessings in this worldly life, not merely in the afterlife. The mention of Allah's spacious earth serves as a reminder that believers need not compromise their faith or integrity to survive or prosper—there are always alternatives and paths available for those who remain steadfast. The closing affirmation that the patient receive their reward without limit or reckoning elevates patience (sabr) as the paramount virtue that transforms temporal hardship into eternal, immeasurable gain, thereby encouraging believers to endure trials with the certainty that their perseverance will be rewarded beyond all calculation.

translation: Say: 'Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion.'
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental principle of sincere monotheism as the core of the Prophet's mission. The command to declare this publicly emphasizes that true worship requires undivided devotion to Allah alone, free from polytheism, hypocrisy, or mixing divine worship with worldly motives. It underscores that sincerity in faith and practice is not optional but a binding obligation for the Prophet and his followers, serving as a counter to those who would dilute Islamic teaching with associationism or insincerity.

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Divine command to the Prophet Muhammad to lead by example in submission to Allah and to be foremost among those who submit to God's will. It emphasizes the Prophet's role not merely as a messenger who conveys God's message, but as the exemplary embodiment of Islam itself, demonstrating complete obedience and submission as the model for all believers to follow. The phrase 'first of the Muslims' denotes precedence in faith and practice, establishing the Prophet as the benchmark for sincere commitment to Allah's guidance.

translation: Say: 'Indeed, I fear, if I were to disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet's profound awareness of accountability before Allah and illustrates that even the greatest of prophets maintains absolute obedience out of genuine fear of divine punishment. It establishes that righteousness stems not from compulsion but from sincere consciousness of Allah's majesty and the ultimate consequences of disobedience. By emphasizing the Prophet's own fear, the verse teaches believers that obedience to Allah should be motivated by genuine reverence and understanding of the Day of Judgment, rather than mere social convention or outward compliance.

translation: Say: 'I worship Allah with sincere devotion in my religion.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of pure monotheism (tawhid) and sincere devotion exclusively to Allah. The speaker is commanded to declare that their worship, beliefs, and religious practice are dedicated solely to Allah without any association of partners with Him, and with complete sincerity of heart and intention free from hypocrisy, ostentation, or worldly motives.

translation: So worship what you will besides Him. Say: 'Indeed, the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Judgment. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss.'
interpretation: This verse employs ironic rhetoric to expose the utter foolishness of associating partners with Allah. The command to 'worship what you will besides Him' is a rhetorical challenge that implicitly condemns idolatry by highlighting its ultimate futility. The verse then pivots to explain what true loss means: not material deprivation in this world, but the irreversible spiritual ruin of the self and the separation from one's loved ones on the Day of Judgment. This juxtaposition reveals that the polytheists believe they are gaining something of value through their worship, when in reality they are securing their eternal damnation—a loss so severe and obvious that it is called 'the manifest loss.' The verse thus reframes worldly concerns and underscores that the only genuine loss is the failure to worship Allah alone, which results in the permanent destruction of both individual souls and familial bonds.

translation: For them above are layers of fire, and below them are layers. That is how Allah frightens His servants with this. O My servants, fear Me.
interpretation: This verse describes the comprehensive punishment in Hell, where the damned are trapped between layers of fire from above and below, unable to escape. The phrase 'that is how Allah frightens His servants with this' indicates that Allah uses this graphic depiction of punishment as a means to warn believers, encouraging them to develop taqwa (God-consciousness and piety). The final command 'O My servants, fear Me' is a direct exhortation from Allah, not a command from the inhabitants of Hell, emphasizing that this terrifying imagery serves as a divine warning to the living to obey Him and avoid such a fate.

translation: And those who avoided at-Taghut, lest they worship it, and turned back to Allah - for them is good tidings. So give good tidings to My servants
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith requires both a negative and positive dimension: the active rejection of false deities and systems of oppression (taghut), combined with a sincere turning toward Allah in obedience and submission. The promise of good tidings (bashara) is reserved for those who demonstrate this dual commitment - they do not merely passively avoid idolatry but consciously repudiate it and redirect their devotion entirely to Allah. This establishes the principle that genuine belief is demonstrated through decisive action against falsehood and wholehearted return to the Divine.

translation: Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it - those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristic of the truly guided people: they possess discernment and wisdom to distinguish between good and bad counsel, sound and unsound teachings. Rather than blindly following all that they hear, they carefully evaluate what they encounter and commit themselves to what is best and most righteous. Their ability to make this distinction and their commitment to the highest standards of truth and morality is itself evidence of Allah's guidance upon them. The verse teaches that true guidance manifests as active discernment and deliberate choice of excellence, not passive reception of information, and this quality of thoughtful evaluation is the mark of those possessed of sound intellect and spiritual wisdom.

translation: Is one against whom the word of punishment has been justly decreed [comparable to one who believes]? Can you rescue those who are in the Fire?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of attempting to save those whom Allah has decreed shall be punished. It presents a rhetorical question directed at the Prophet Muhammad to illustrate that human effort cannot override Allah's divine decree and justice. The verse underscores the distinction between those destined for punishment due to their disbelief and rejection of truth, and the powerlessness of even the most noble intercessor to alter their fate. It serves as a reminder that Allah's judgment is absolute and that salvation depends on one's faith and submission to Allah, not on external intervention.

translation: But those who feared their Lord will have chambers above which are chambers built, with rivers flowing beneath them. [This is] the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the distinction between the righteous and the unrighteous through contrasting descriptions of their eternal dwelling places. The elaborate architecture of the righteous's dwellings—chambers layered upon chambers with flowing rivers—symbolizes the infinite abundance, elevation, and hierarchical perfection of Paradise. The mention of God's promise emphasizes that this reward is not contingent upon human whim but is a divine covenant, thereby providing absolute assurance to believers that their piety and God-consciousness will be recompensed with unimaginable blessings that exceed all earthly understanding.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, then makes it flow as springs in the earth, then produces thereby crops of varying colors, then they wither and you see them turning yellow, then He makes them into broken pieces? Indeed, in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse uses the natural cycle of water and vegetation to teach a profound spiritual lesson about the transient nature of worldly life and the inevitability of death and return to God. The progression from water's descent to vibrant crops to withering and decay mirrors the human journey from creation through life to death, serving as a powerful metaphor for those who possess intellect to reflect upon their own mortality and the temporary nature of all earthly possessions, and to turn their hearts toward the eternal rather than the perishable.

translation: Is he whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord, [like he whose heart rejects it]? So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound spiritual contrast: those whose hearts Allah has opened to accept Islam receive divine guidance (nur—light) that illuminates their path, while those who harden their hearts against Allah's remembrance are willfully rejecting the signs of truth. The 'woe' pronounced upon the hard-hearted emphasizes the tragic consequence of self-imposed spiritual blindness. The verse teaches that receptiveness to divine guidance is itself a blessing from Allah, and that rejection of this guidance—despite its clarity—is not mere weakness but a deliberate choice that leads to manifest misguidance. The hardening of the heart becomes both cause and effect of spiritual ruin.

translation: Allah has sent down the best of statements as a Book, with verses that are consistent and repetitive. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it, then their skins and hearts soften at the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And whoever Allah sends astray—for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an's impact on the believers is not merely intellectual but profoundly emotional and spiritual. The description of skins shivering and then softening illustrates the transformative power of God's word upon those with genuine God-consciousness—first producing awe and reverence, then melting hearts into submission and remembrance. This progression demonstrates that true guidance from Allah is not simply information received by the mind, but a complete transformation of the soul that manifests in both physical and emotional responses, revealing the distinction between those whom Allah guides with sincere hearts and those whom He allows to go astray due to their inner condition.

translation: Is he who protects his face from the evil of punishment on the Day of Resurrection [equal to others]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers: 'Taste what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperate and humiliating state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, where they will futilely attempt to shield themselves from divine punishment, only to be mocked and reminded that they are merely experiencing the consequences of their own deeds. The rhetorical question emphasizes the futility of their resistance and the justice of God's retribution, as their punishment is nothing but the manifestation of their own evil actions in the worldly life.

translation: Those before them denied, so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of divine justice wherein those who reject the truth face consequences they do not anticipate or expect. The punishment comes unexpectedly, suggesting that denial of divine signs does not exempt one from accountability—rather, it may compound it by removing the awareness and preparation that acknowledgment might provide. The phrase 'from where they did not perceive' emphasizes that the consequences of rejecting truth are inevitable and inescapable, often arriving in ways that catch the heedless off guard, serving as a warning to subsequent generations to heed the message before it is too late.

translation: So Allah made them taste disgrace in the worldly life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater—if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of divine justice wherein those who reject faith and commit wrongdoing experience the consequences of their actions both in this world and in the next. The disgrace mentioned refers to the humiliation, shame, and downfall that befalls the disbelievers and wrongdoers in their earthly lives—through loss of dignity, defeat, or the exposure of their falsehood. The verse emphasizes that this worldly punishment, despite being severe, pales in comparison to the eternal punishment awaiting them in the Hereafter. The concluding phrase 'if only they knew' underscores the theme of human ignorance and neglect of truth despite clear signs, suggesting that the primary obstacle to their salvation is their refusal to understand and internalize the reality of divine accountability and the ultimate consequences of their choices.

translation: And indeed, We have presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of parable, so that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an employs diverse parables and examples suited to different capacities of understanding, as a pedagogical method to awaken human consciousness and facilitate reflection. The purpose of this variety of examples is not merely intellectual exercise, but rather to move people toward remembrance (tadhakkur)—to recall their Creator, their covenant with Him, and the truth of His message. The phrase 'every kind of parable' indicates that Allah has addressed human understanding through multiple approaches, acknowledging the diversity of human minds and experiences, so that each person might find a path to recognition and spiritual remembrance.

translation: An Arabic Qur'an, free from any crookedness, so that they might become God-fearing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfect clarity and internal consistency of the Qur'an as a divine revelation in the Arabic language. The phrase 'free from any crookedness' signifies the absence of contradictions, falsehoods, or deviations from truth. The purpose of this flawless presentation is to guide people toward taqwa (God-consciousness and piety), suggesting that when the message is conveyed with perfect clarity and eloquence, it becomes more effective in moving hearts and minds toward righteousness and obedience to God.

translation: Allah presents an example: a man belonging to (several) quarrelsome partners and a man belonging entirely to one man - are they equal in example? Praise be to Allah. But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the fundamental inequality between those who associate partners with Allah in worship and those who submit exclusively to the One God. Just as a person owned by multiple quarreling masters experiences confusion, conflict, and divided loyalties, the one who divides his worship and obedience among many gods is in a state of spiritual confusion and fragmentation. Conversely, the person devoted entirely to one master experiences clarity, unity of purpose, and proper direction. The verse emphasizes that tawhid (absolute monotheism) provides coherence and harmony to human life, while shirk (associating partners with Allah) creates internal contradiction and spiritual disorder, yet most people fail to comprehend this fundamental truth about the superiority of Allah's unity.

translation: Indeed, you will die and indeed, they will die.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Prophet Muhammad (and by extension all humanity) of the universal reality of death as an inevitable fate. It serves to console the Prophet during moments of hardship and conflict with his opponents, emphasizing that both he and those who oppose him are temporary beings subject to the same mortality. The verse's deeper purpose is to redirect focus from worldly conflicts and material concerns toward the eternal consequences of one's deeds, implying that what matters is not victory in this fleeting life but rather one's standing before God in the afterlife.

translation: Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, people will engage in disputes and arguments before Allah regarding their deeds, beliefs, and the decisions made in their earthly lives. This serves as a warning that all contentious matters unresolved in this world will be brought before Allah for final judgment, where truth will be fully revealed and falsehoods exposed, emphasizing human accountability and the certainty of divine adjudication.

translation: So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is not Hell a dwelling place for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of deliberately rejecting divine guidance by highlighting the two compounded sins: fabricating lies against Allah's nature or revelation, and categorically denying the truth when it arrives with clarity. The rhetorical question 'who is more unjust' underscores that there is no greater injustice than this rejection, as it combines intellectual dishonesty with rebellion against ultimate reality. The verse establishes a direct causal connection between such rejection and the deserved consequence of Hell, portraying disbelief not as mere intellectual disagreement but as willful corruption of truth and betrayal of one's own rationality.

translation: And he who came with the truth and those who believed in it - those are the righteous ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true piety (taqwa) is characterized by two essential qualities: adherence to and propagation of truth, and sincere faith in that truth. The verse suggests that righteousness is not merely about ritual practice, but fundamentally about a commitment to truthfulness and an unwavering belief in it, indicating that integrity and honesty in both word and deed, combined with genuine conviction, are the hallmarks of those who truly fear and obey Allah.

translation: For them is whatever they will with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who perform excellence and righteous deeds will be granted unlimited fulfillment of their desires in Paradise, whatever their hearts wish for, as a direct reward from God. The phrase 'whatever they will' suggests a state of complete satisfaction and the fulfillment of all aspirations, indicating that the reward for sincere devotion and moral excellence transcends material or temporal limitations and enters into a realm of spiritual and eternal abundance where the righteous will lack nothing they desire.

translation: So that Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them for the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's merciful judgment system, where He overlooks and forgives the worst deeds of the righteous while rewarding them for their best actions. This reflects the divine principle of justice tempered with mercy—those who strive to do good will have their shortcomings pardoned by Allah, who focuses His reckoning on their virtuous deeds rather than their failings. The verse encourages believers to pursue excellence in their actions, assuring them that Allah's assessment is not absolute condemnation of mistakes but rather a merciful accounting that emphasizes their righteous conduct.

translation: Is not Allah sufficient for His servant? Yet they threaten you with those [gods] other than Him. And whoever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah's protection and guidance for the believer who places complete trust in Him, while rejecting the fear that disbelievers attempt to instill through threats of their false deities. The rhetorical question at the beginning asserts an absolute truth: that Allah alone is sufficient protector and provider. The verse then addresses the psychological warfare employed by opponents who use intimidation tactics, reminding the believer that such threats are baseless when one's reliance is upon Allah. Finally, it establishes the theological principle that human guidance is ultimately dependent on Allah's will and mercy - those whom Allah has not guided through their own choice to turn away from truth have no alternative source of guidance available to them, illustrating the complete dependency of creation upon the Creator's wisdom and justice.

translation: And whoever Allah guides, there is no one who can lead him astray. Is not Allah Mighty and Owner of Vengeance?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine guidance is a comprehensive protection against misguidance, as those guided by Allah are secured by His will and power. The rhetorical question that follows reinforces that Allah possesses both absolute power (might) and the authority to punish those who reject His guidance, suggesting that abandoning the path of guidance is not merely a loss but an act of defiance against an omnipotent God, making the consequences of such rejection inevitable and severe.

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they will surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Have you then considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends for me some harm, are they able to remove His harm? Or if He intends for me mercy, are they able to withhold His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him rely those who rely [on Him].'
interpretation: This verse exposes the contradiction in the beliefs of the polytheists who acknowledge Allah as the Creator of all things yet invoke other deities for protection and provision. The passage demonstrates that since only Allah possesses the power to bring harm or bestow mercy, the worship and reliance upon lesser beings is logically inconsistent and practically futile. The verse teaches that true trust (tawakkul) belongs exclusively to Allah, highlighting that the perfection of faith requires not only intellectual recognition of Allah's unique creative power but also a practical manifestation of complete dependence upon Him alone, rejecting the false security sought through idolatry.

translation: Say: 'O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am [also] working. So you will soon know'
interpretation: This verse represents the Prophet's defiant confidence in the face of opposition. Rather than responding with fear or despair to those who reject him, he asserts that both he and his opponents will proceed with their respective courses of action, and that time and events will ultimately vindicate the truth. The phrase 'according to your position' suggests that each party will act according to their own capacity and intention, but the outcome will be determined by God's justice. This reflects the Prophet's unshakeable conviction in his mission and his submission to God's will regarding the ultimate consequences.

translation: For whom the punishment comes will disgrace him, and upon him will be settled an eternal punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and shame of divine punishment in the Hereafter, teaching that those who reject Allah's guidance will face not merely temporal consequences but permanent, unrelenting punishment accompanied by profound humiliation. The succession of two types of punishment—the disgracing punishment and the settled eternal punishment—stresses both the immediate shame of facing judgment and the finality of hellish torment, conveying the gravity of rejecting divine revelation and the inescapable nature of divine justice.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind in truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own good; and whoever goes astray, it is only to his detriment. And you are not over them a guardian.
interpretation: This verse establishes that divine guidance is an offer extended to all humanity through the Qur'an, but responsibility for accepting or rejecting it ultimately rests with each individual. The Prophet's role is to convey the message clearly, not to compel belief or bear the consequences of others' choices. This underscores human free will and accountability before God—each person's spiritual destiny depends on their own conscious decision to accept or reject the truth presented to them.

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that die not during their sleep. Then He withholds those for whom He has ordained death and sends the others back until an appointed term. Verily, in this are signs for a people who think deeply.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's sovereignty over life and death, demonstrating that the soul's departure is a divinely ordained process occurring both in wakefulness and sleep. The verse emphasizes that death is predetermined by Allah for each soul, while those whose appointed time has not yet come are returned to life, establishing a divine system of justice where each person has a fixed lifespan decreed by Allah. The mention of these signs being for those who reflect invites believers to contemplate the mystery of death and life as evidence of Allah's perfect knowledge and control over all creation.

translation: Or have they taken intercessors other than Allah? Say, 'Even if they possess nothing and do not understand?'
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists' belief in intercession through false deities by highlighting the absurdity of seeking help from entities that lack power and understanding. The rhetorical questioning emphasizes that those whom the idolaters invoke as intercessors are incapable of bringing any benefit, as they possess neither authority in the heavens nor comprehension of divine matters, thereby establishing that intercession is exclusively within Allah's domain and cannot be achieved through powerless intermediaries.

translation: Say: 'To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned.'
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah's absolute authority over all matters of intercession and creation, meaning that no one can intercede with Allah except by His permission. The verse emphasizes divine monopoly over intercession as an assertion against false beliefs in the intercessory powers of idols or other entities. By connecting this to His ownership of the heavens and earth, the Quran reinforces that sovereignty and the power to grant or withhold intercession are inseparable attributes of divine authority alone. The final clause about returning to Him underscores that all souls will ultimately stand before Allah for judgment, where no intercession will avail except what He permits, thereby warning against relying on intermediaries rather than on Allah's mercy and obedience to His commands.

translation: And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion; but when those [worshipped] other than Him are mentioned, then they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse reveals the spiritual condition of the disbelievers whose hearts are naturally averse to the monotheistic message of Allah. Their rejection is not merely intellectual but deeply rooted in their emotional and spiritual disposition - they find distress and discomfort in the concept of worshipping Allah alone because it contradicts their desires and worldly inclinations. Conversely, their joy at the mention of idols and false deities demonstrates that their real concern is not truth-seeking but rather the preservation of their false beliefs and the worldly status these beliefs provide them. The verse shows that disbelief is fundamentally a disease of the heart that creates an inverted moral reality where falsehood brings happiness and truth brings revulsion.

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen. You judge between Your servants concerning that in which they used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse teaches the believer to appeal to Allah's complete knowledge and absolute authority when faced with disputes or disagreements. By invoking Allah as the Creator and Knower of all hidden and visible things, the verse emphasizes that only Allah possesses the wisdom and justice necessary to resolve human disagreements. It directs believers to trust in Allah's ultimate judgment rather than becoming entangled in endless human disputes, acknowledging that conflicts among people are inevitable, but their resolution lies exclusively with Allah's divine decree.

translation: And if those who have wronged possessed all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, they would ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Judgment. And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not reckoned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute inescapability of divine retribution on the Day of Judgment, illustrating that no amount of worldly wealth or material possession could ever serve as a means of redemption or escape from the consequences of one's wrongdoing. It conveys that the punishment for injustice is predetermined and inevitable, and that the sinner will be confronted with forms of torment and divine manifestations they never anticipated in their earthly life, highlighting the severity of divine justice beyond human comprehension or expectation.

translation: And there became apparent to them the evil of what they had earned, and there encircled them that which they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment of reckoning when the disbelievers and mockers will witness the consequences of their own deeds and the fulfillment of the divine punishment they ridiculed. The interpretation emphasizes that those who dismissed the signs of God and mocked the believers will face an inescapable reckoning where their actions and mockery return upon them, serving as a manifestation of divine justice that turns their own arrogance into their doom. It conveys that God's warnings are not empty threats but inevitable realities that will overtake the heedless.

translation: So when harm touches a person, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a blessing from Us, he says, 'I have been given this only because of knowledge.' But no, it is a trial, yet most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse reveals a fundamental human psychological weakness: ingratitude and false attribution of success to personal merit rather than divine favor. When people face hardship, they instinctively turn to God in desperation, yet when granted blessings, they arrogantly attribute these to their own intelligence and abilities, forgetting God's role entirely. The verse emphasizes that prosperity itself is a test (fitnah) from God—potentially more dangerous than adversity—because it often leads to spiritual corruption through pride and self-deception. The ignorance mentioned at the end points to humanity's failure to recognize that all blessings originate from God's will, not human capability, and that this very arrogance in attributing success to oneself becomes the true trial.

translation: Those before them have already said the same thing. But what they earned did not avail them at all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recurring pattern of human resistance to divine truth across generations. The disbelievers' objections and rejections are not novel, but have been repeated by previous nations throughout history. Despite their accumulated wealth, power, and worldly achievements, these material gains and worldly accomplishments provided them no protection against Allah's punishment. The verse underscores that reliance on wealth and transient worldly acquisitions cannot substitute for faith and obedience to Allah, and that the consequences of rejecting God's message are inevitable and inescapable regardless of one's material status.

translation: So they were struck by the evil consequences of what they earned. And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evil consequences of what they earned, and they will not escape [God's punishment].
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of divine justice wherein people face the consequences of their own actions and choices. The repetition of 'evil consequences of what they earned' emphasizes that wrongdoing inevitably returns to the wrongdoer, whether in this life or the next, and this is an inescapable law of God's creation - no one can evade or frustrate the execution of God's justice.

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that the distribution of sustenance in the world is entirely within Allah's control and wisdom, not determined by human effort alone or by chance. The sign of Allah's power and providence is evident to those who possess faith—they recognize that variations in wealth and poverty among people reflect divine wisdom and are tests of character and obedience, rather than reasons for envy, despair, or moral judgment of the rich or poor.

translation: Say: 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no matter how grave one's sins, despair is forbidden and repentance is always possible because God's mercy is infinite and precedes His judgment. The message is that the path to redemption remains open to all who turn back to God, thereby inverting the believer's focus from the magnitude of their sins to the magnitude of God's forgiveness.

translation: And turn back to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, then you will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency and necessity of sincere repentance and complete submission to Allah before the final consequences arrive. The phrase 'then you will not be helped' serves as a warning that once divine punishment is decreed, there will be no escape or divine assistance to prevent it, making repentance while still given opportunity a critical obligation for believers.

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of choosing and adhering to the most righteous and excellent teachings from the Qur'an, implying that not all commands carry the same weight or apply in the same circumstances. The urgency conveyed by the warning of sudden punishment encourages immediate spiritual commitment and ethical conduct, suggesting that delayed repentance or heedlessness invites divine consequences that arrive unexpectedly, catching those unmindful of their obligations to their Creator.

translation: Lest a soul should say, 'O my regret upon what I failed to do regarding the duty to Allah, and indeed I was among those who mocked.'
interpretation: This verse expresses the profound remorse that awaits those who neglected their obligations to Allah and treated divine guidance with ridicule and scorn. The exclamation of 'ya hasrataa' (O my regret) signifies the depth of despair on the Day of Judgment when the truth becomes undeniable and irreversible. The verse emphasizes that mocking faith and being negligent in one's duty to Allah will result in eternal regret, as the opportunity for repentance and righteous action will have passed. This serves as a warning to those who dismiss religious obligations or ridicule believers, showing that such attitudes will become a source of profound anguish when one faces the consequences of their choices.

translation: Or say, 'If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse rebukes those who make excuses for their failure to follow guidance by blaming Allah's will, when in reality they themselves rejected the clear signs and chose to disobey. It exposes the hypocrisy of blaming divine predestination while refusing to take responsibility for one's own choices and the guidance that was made available to them. The verse emphasizes that humans have agency and choice, and they cannot use Allah's decree as a justification for their disobedience when they actively turned away from the truth.

translation: Or when he sees the punishment, he says: 'If only I had another chance, so that I could be among the doers of good.'
