interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency and necessity of heeding the divine call to monotheism and faith as a means of salvation. The response to Allah's call is presented as the pathway to forgiveness and deliverance from torment, illustrating that acceptance of faith is not merely a personal matter but a communal responsibility where believers must invite their people to the truth. The promise of forgiveness and protection is contingent upon genuine belief, highlighting the direct relationship between submission to Allah and the attainment of mercy in both this life and the hereafter.

translation: And whoever does not answer the call of Allah is not weakening [Allah] upon the earth, and there are not for him besides Allah any protectors. Those are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of rejecting Allah's message and guidance. Those who refuse to respond to Allah's call cannot escape His power or authority, nor can they find alternative protectors or helpers who can shield them from the consequences of their rejection. Their refusal to heed Allah's guidance is fundamentally a form of clear misguidance, as they delude themselves into thinking they can evade accountability or find sufficient support elsewhere, when in reality they remain defenseless without Allah's favor and protection.

translation: Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse employs logical reasoning to address doubt about the resurrection. If Allah possessed the power to create the entire cosmos from nothing without fatigue or difficulty, then resurrecting the dead—who already exist and merely need to be brought back to life—is logically a lesser and simpler task. The phrase 'was not wearied' emphasizes that creation imposed no burden on Allah's power, establishing that His creative capacity is limitless. Thus, the verse does not merely assert that resurrection is possible, but demonstrates it through rational comparison: the one who can accomplish the greater feat (creating existence itself) can certainly accomplish the lesser (restoring life). This addresses a fundamental doubt in human reasoning by grounding belief in resurrection not in blind faith alone, but in rational consideration of Allah's demonstrated attributes of power and knowledge.

translation: And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire, [it will be said], "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord!" He will say, "Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of divine justice when disbelievers are confronted with the undeniable reality of Hell and the truth of God's signs they rejected in the worldly life. Their admission of truth at that point becomes a condemning testimony against themselves, as their acknowledgment comes too late to benefit them. The verse emphasizes that rejection of truth in this world inevitably leads to tasting its bitter consequences in the Hereafter, and no excuse or denial will be possible when faced with manifest reality.

translation: So be patient as those of firm resolve among the messengers were patient, and do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them. It is as if, on the Day they see what they are promised, they had not remained [in this world] except for an hour of a day. [This is a] notification. Then, is there destroyed except the people who are defiantly disobedient?
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith requires patient endurance in conveying the message, regardless of the mockery or rejection faced. The comparison to those of firm resolve among the messengers (such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad) serves as a model of steadfastness. The imagery of the promised Day seeming as though only an hour has passed reflects how the preoccupied lives of the heedless will appear insignificant and swift in retrospect when confronted with the reality of accountability. The verse emphasizes that patience is not passive weakness but active perseverance in truth, and that ultimately only those who willfully reject and transgress will face destruction, underscoring divine justice and the futility of resistance against God's will.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Those who disbelieve and turn away from the path of Allah - He has made their deeds go astray.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who reject faith and actively divert others from following Allah's guidance are deprived of success in their endeavors. Their actions, despite any worldly effort or appearance of achievement, are rendered futile and meaningless because they are disconnected from divine purpose and truth. This reflects the consequence of deliberate rejection of guidance - that one's life's work becomes hollow and leads nowhere of true value.

translation: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds, and believed in what has been sent down upon Muhammad—and it is the truth from their Lord—He will remove from them their misdeeds and improve their condition.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith requires both internal conviction (belief in God and His message) and external manifestation through righteous actions. The phrase 'it is the truth from their Lord' emphasizes the divine origin and legitimacy of Muhammad's revelation, serving as a foundation for acceptance. The consequence outlined—removal of sins and improvement of affairs—demonstrates that sincere belief coupled with righteous deeds results in God's mercy and blessing, indicating that these two elements are inseparable components of genuine faith and that God's reward is comprehensive, extending to both spiritual purification and worldly well-being.

translation: That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, while those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah set forth for people their examples.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the fundamental principle of divine justice: the divergent outcomes of humanity result from their conscious choices between truth and falsehood. The phrase 'thus does Allah set forth for people their examples' indicates that Allah makes these contrasts evident as lessons and reminders for mankind to understand the natural consequences of their beliefs and actions. The verse emphasizes personal accountability—people are not compelled toward either path, but rather their adherence to truth or falsehood is a reflection of their own decisions and moral orientation.

translation: So when you meet those who have disbelieved, strike [their] necks until when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure the bonds, and either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He has allowed war] so that He may test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of Allah - never will He cause their deeds to be lost.
interpretation: This verse establishes the laws of warfare in Islam, permitting fighting against those who reject faith while establishing moral boundaries: combatants must fight with severity to achieve victory, but once opponents are subdued, they must be treated humanely with binding agreements. The verse then provides divine perspective—Allah could enforce submission miraculously, but permits warfare as a test to distinguish the sincere believers from others through their conduct and sacrifice. The concluding statement affirms that those who die fighting for Allah's cause will not have their efforts wasted, providing spiritual reassurance that their sacrifice carries eternal value and reward. This frames warfare not as mere worldly conflict but as a trial that refines faith and a path through which believers can attain merit with their Lord.

translation: He will guide them and set right their condition.
interpretation: This verse expresses the divine promise that Allah will provide guidance and improvement to those who believe and follow the right path. The phrase indicates both spiritual guidance (hidayah) through the Quran and Sunnah, as well as practical rectification of their affairs and states in this life. It reflects the comprehensive mercy of Allah toward His servants, addressing both their spiritual orientation and their worldly circumstances.

translation: And He will admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them.
interpretation: This verse describes Allah's mercy and kindness toward the believers, not only granting them Paradise as their reward but also providing them with knowledge and understanding of Paradise beforehand. The phrase 'which He has made known to them' suggests that Allah bestows upon the believers awareness and description of Paradise during their lifetime in this world, through revelation and the teachings of the Prophet. This knowledge serves as an incentive for righteousness and a source of comfort and hope, demonstrating that Allah's guidance is comprehensive—He both promises Paradise and enlightens believers about its nature and beauty so they can aspire toward it with full understanding and conviction.

translation: O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.
interpretation: This verse establishes a reciprocal relationship between the believers' devotion to Allah's cause and their receipt of divine support. The act of supporting Allah—through obedience, spreading His message, and upholding His religion—is not a favor granted to the Divine, but rather a condition that invokes Allah's aid and strengthens the believers' resolve and stability in their faith and struggle. The promise of firm footedness signifies not merely military victory, but spiritual fortitude and unwavering certainty in one's conviction, suggesting that those who commit themselves to Allah's cause will be granted both material success and psychological steadfastness.

translation: And those who disbelieved - so hardship for them, and He has made their deeds go astray.
interpretation: This verse expresses the consequence of rejection and disbelief: those who turn away from guidance will face difficulty and ruin, and their actions will be rendered meaningless and ineffective. The verse emphasizes that deliberate rejection of truth leads to a state of hardship in this life and the nullification of any spiritual or moral worth in their deeds, establishing a divine law that disbelief carries inherent consequences for the soul and the significance of one's works.

translation: That is because they hated what Allah revealed, so He rendered their deeds void.
interpretation: This verse conveys that rejection of divine guidance leads to spiritual desolation and the nullification of all righteous actions. When people turn away from Allah's revelation out of animosity or dislike, their good deeds lose all value and reward, regardless of their outward form. This teaches that sincere faith and acceptance of Allah's message are the essential foundations upon which all righteous action must be built; without them, even seemingly good works are hollow and devoid of true merit in Allah's sight.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed upon them, and for the disbelievers is the like thereof.
interpretation: This verse invokes reflection on historical evidence as a means of spiritual awakening. By witnessing the ruins and remnants of past civilizations that rejected God's message, people should recognize the pattern of divine consequences for disbelief. The emphasis on personal observation ('have they not traveled') suggests that experiential learning and empirical evidence of God's judgment are available to all who seek them, and the parallel fate awaiting the present disbelievers serves as a warning that defiance of truth is not without consequence.

translation: That is because Allah is the Guardian of those who have believed, while those who disbelieve have no guardian.
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental protection and support that Allah provides to the believers in this world and the Hereafter, emphasizing that their reliance should be entirely upon Him. Conversely, it highlights the isolation and abandonment of the disbelievers, who deny Allah's guidance and thus are deprived of divine protection and assistance, underscoring the consequences of rejecting faith and the reality that without Allah's guardianship, one faces loss and vulnerability.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who have believed and done righteous deeds into Gardens beneath which rivers flow. And those who have disbelieved enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire will be their residence.
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental contrast between the believers and the disbelievers in terms of their ultimate destinies and present spiritual states. The believers' righteousness leads them to eternal gardens as a reward from Allah, while the disbelievers, despite their worldly enjoyment, are likened to cattle in their negligence and lack of spiritual consciousness, destined ultimately for punishment. The verse emphasizes that true success lies not in temporary material gratification but in faith coupled with righteous action, and warns against the delusion of worldly comfort divorced from spiritual purpose and accountability.

translation: And how many a city were stronger than your city which drove you out - We destroyed them, and there was no helper for them.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Prophet Muhammad that those who reject divine guidance face inevitable destruction regardless of their strength and power. The fortified cities that were more powerful than Mecca were completely annihilated when they rejected their prophets, demonstrating that material strength and fortifications offer no protection against divine punishment. This serves as a consolation to the Prophet during his persecution in Mecca and a warning to all who persist in disbelief - that earthly might and resources are ultimately insignificant before the will of Allah, and that no one can save them from divine consequence once the decree of destruction has been issued.

translation: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord like one to whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive, and they follow their desires?
interpretation: This verse contrasts two types of people: those who have received clear guidance and evidence from Allah (a clear proof, meaning the Qur'an and divine knowledge), versus those whose evil deeds have been embellished for them by Satan and their own desires. The rhetorical question emphasizes that these two groups are fundamentally incomparable - the guided person who possesses clear evidence from Allah cannot be equated with the one who follows their whims and allows their base desires to lead them astray. The verse illustrates the principle that while both may claim different paths, they are not equivalent in terms of their source of guidance or their ultimate standing before Allah.

translation: The description of Paradise which has been promised to the righteous is: within it are rivers of water undiminished, rivers of milk whose taste does not change, rivers of wine delightful to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey. And for them therein are fruits of every kind and forgiveness from their Lord. Are they like those who will abide eternally in the Fire, given to drink boiling water that cuts through their intestines?
interpretation: This verse establishes a profound contrast between the ultimate destinies of the righteous and the wicked, demonstrating that the rewards of obedience to God are incomparable to the punishment of those who reject Him. The detailed description of Paradise's physical delights serves not merely as literal depiction but as an illustration of ultimate satisfaction, pleasure, and abundance that transcends worldly experience, while the horrifying image of boiling water cutting through intestines represents the complete negation of comfort and the irreversible consequences of turning away from God. The rhetorical question 'Are they like those...' is meant to awaken the conscience and emphasize the utter disparity in outcomes, driving home the urgency of choosing the path of righteousness and taqwa (God-consciousness) in this life.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but when they leave your presence, they say to those who have been given knowledge, 'What did he just say?' Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed, and they follow their desires.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual condition of those who are physically present and hear the Message but lack genuine receptivity. Their hearts are sealed—a seal that is both a consequence of their deliberate turning away and the cause of their continued hardness. By asking others what was said immediately after hearing it themselves, they reveal the disconnect between their ears and their hearts; they hear with their bodies but not with their souls. Their following of desires over guidance demonstrates that they have chosen the path of willful ignorance, and this verse warns that persistent rejection of truth leads to a state where the capacity to truly understand becomes obscured.

translation: And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety (consciousness of God).
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of divine reciprocity in spiritual growth: those who actively seek and follow guidance receive additional guidance from Allah. The granting of taqwa (piety/God-consciousness) to those already guided suggests that sincere spiritual effort and openness to divine truth create a condition wherein Allah grants deeper awareness and reverence of Him. This reflects the Qur'anic principle that Allah does not withhold guidance from those genuinely seeking it, but rather rewards their earnest pursuit with increased understanding and spiritual consciousness.

translation: Do they then await anything except that the Hour should come upon them suddenly? But its signs have already come. So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and imminence of the Day of Judgment by highlighting the contradiction in the disbelievers' complacency. Despite the clear signs and portents of the Hour that have already appeared (through the Qur'an, the Prophet's message, and observable phenomena), they continue to reject the message. When the Hour finally arrives, reminders and repentance will be of no avail, as the time for heeding guidance will have passed. The verse serves as a powerful warning against willful negligence and the assumption that one can defer repentance indefinitely.

translation: So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows of your movement and your resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true knowledge begins with the absolute certainty of monotheism and Allah's oneness. The command to seek forgiveness for one's own sin alongside those of the believers reflects the spiritual responsibility of the Prophet and by extension all believers to maintain humility before Allah. The final phrase about Allah's knowledge of our movements and resting places serves as a reminder that nothing escapes Allah's awareness, which should motivate sincere repentance and constant consciousness of His presence, thereby transforming the act of seeking forgiveness from mere ritual into a genuine acknowledgment of human limitation and divine omniscience.

translation: And those who have believed say, 'Why has not a surah been sent down?' But when a clear surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with a look of one overcome by death. So woe unto them.
interpretation: This verse reveals the hypocrisy of the waverers among those who outwardly claim faith. Their demand for revelation is not genuine seeking of guidance, but rather a test of their true commitment. When clear legal verses regarding combat are revealed, their reluctance and inward sickness become evident through their expressions of fear and despair. The comparison of their gaze to that of the dying emphasizes the depth of their terror and the weakness of their faith. The verse exposes that their outward profession of belief conceals an internal spiritual malaise—a disease of doubt and cowardice—and thus pronounces condemnation upon them for their hypocrisy.

translation: Obedience and kindly speech. But when the matter is determined, if they had been truthful to Allah, it would have been better for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith requires both outward compliance and sincere commitment. The phrase 'if they had been truthful to Allah' indicates that merely offering pleasant words and superficial obedience is insufficient; what matters is genuine resolve and sincerity in one's covenant with Allah when critical moments demand decisive action and sacrifice. The conditional structure suggests that many people fail at this crucial juncture, choosing comfort over authentic dedication when tested, whereas those who truly submit to Allah with complete honesty would find their obedience far more beneficial and praiseworthy.

translation: So would you perhaps, if you turned away, cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?
interpretation: This verse addresses the human tendency toward moral deterioration when one abandons divine guidance. It presents a rhetorical question that reveals the natural consequence of turning away from God's message: the breakdown of social order and familial bonds. The verse emphasizes that adherence to God's guidance is not merely a matter of personal piety, but a prerequisite for maintaining the moral fabric of society and preserving the family relationships that form its foundation. By linking disbelief with corruption and severing of kinship ties, the Qur'an demonstrates that rejecting divine guidance inevitably leads to the dissolution of both societal and familial ethics.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He made them deaf and blinded their sight.
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual consequence of those who reject Allah's guidance: they suffer a progressive spiritual blindness and deafness that prevents them from perceiving truth. The 'curse' here represents divine abandonment and withdrawal of guidance, which results in their inability to hear the truth when presented and their inability to see the signs of Allah. This is both a cause (they turned away) and an effect (Allah seals their hearts) of their rejection, illustrating how persistent disbelief hardens the heart and closes the avenues through which divine truth might enter the soul.

translation: Do they not contemplate the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?
interpretation: This verse rebukes those who hear the Qur'an but fail to reflect upon its meanings and signs. The rhetorical question emphasizes that the inability to understand the Qur'an is not due to its clarity or lack of accessibility, but rather stems from a spiritual condition—hearts sealed by heedlessness, pride, and rejection. The verse suggests that understanding the Qur'an requires both intellectual engagement (tadabbur) and an open, receptive heart; those who possess hardened hearts despite exposure to the Qur'an bear responsibility for their own spiritual blindness.

translation: Indeed, those who have turned back on their heels after guidance has become clear to them - Satan has made their deeds seem attractive to them and has given them respite.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the psychological and spiritual mechanism of apostasy: those who reject faith after clearly understanding it do so not because of intellectual confusion, but because they have allowed their desires to be manipulated by Satan. The phrase 'turned back on their heels' emphasizes the deliberate rejection and reversal of their previous understanding. Satan's role is not to force them, but to make wickedness appear beautiful and appealing to their souls, while prolonging their delusion with false hopes. This reveals that apostasy is ultimately a moral choice enabled by surrender to base desires, demonstrating human responsibility in either accepting or rejecting divine guidance once it has become manifest to them.

translation: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allah had revealed: 'We will obey you in some of the matters.' And Allah knows their secrets.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who claimed faith while secretly conspiring with the disbelievers to undermine Islamic teachings. The verse reveals that certain people made a covenant with those who rejected Allah's guidance, promising partial obedience to their desires and commands. The final phrase emphasizes that despite their attempts at concealment, Allah's knowledge encompasses all hidden intentions and secret plots, serving as a warning that no conspiracy against the truth escapes Divine awareness, and that such duplicity will ultimately be brought to account.

translation: So how [will it be] when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: This verse depicts the agony and humiliation that the disbelievers will experience at the moment of death, when the angels of death come to extract their souls. The striking of their faces and backs symbolizes the severity of their punishment and the disgrace they will face for their rejection of Allah's signs during their earthly lives. This serves as a warning to those who turn away from the truth, emphasizing that death will be a moment of reckoning where they cannot escape the consequences of their choices.

translation: That is because they followed what displeased Allah and hated His pleasure, so He made their deeds void.
interpretation: This verse conveys that rejection of divine guidance and deliberate aversion to seeking Allah's approval constitute the root cause of spiritual ruin. When one consciously chooses paths that contradict Allah's will—not out of weakness but out of deliberate preference for displeasure—they sever themselves from the source of meaningful action. Their deeds become nullified not because the works themselves lack external form, but because they lack the essential spiritual foundation and sincere intention that would give them validity before Allah. This reflects the principle that acceptance by Allah depends fundamentally on alignment with His will and genuine desire for His approval, without which even ostensibly good actions lose their spiritual substance and reward.

translation: Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that Allah will never bring out their hatred (rancor)?
interpretation: This verse addresses the psychological reality that those harboring spiritual sickness (doubt, hypocrisy, or enmity toward the faith) delude themselves into believing their concealed malice will remain hidden forever. The verse implies that Allah's knowledge is all-encompassing and that eventually, through divine justice or natural consequences, such hidden enmity will be exposed and manifested. This serves as a warning that inward corruption cannot be perpetually concealed from Allah, and as a reminder that those who nurse hatred in their hearts while outwardly claiming faith deceive only themselves.

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their marks; but you will certainly know them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the hypocrites among the believers can be identified by their speech and behavior, even when their outward appearance may deceive. The phrase 'by their marks' refers to how Allah could make their hypocrisy visually apparent if He willed, but instead He has given believers the ability to discern them through careful observation of their words and mannerisms. The verse emphasizes that sincere believers should develop discernment to recognize insincerity in others, while Allah's knowledge encompasses all actions and intentions, serving as a reminder that deception cannot escape divine awareness.

translation: And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive [in the way of Allah] and the patient ones, and [until] We test your accounts/deeds.
interpretation: Allah reminds the believers that testing and trials are inevitable parts of the spiritual journey, serving as a means of distinguishing the truly committed from the weak in faith. The trials reveal not new knowledge to Allah, but rather manifest the hidden qualities of resolve and perseverance that already exist within individuals, allowing them to purify themselves through hardship and demonstrate their sincere devotion through perseverance in obedience.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and turned away from the way of Allah and opposed the Messenger after the guidance had become clear to them will not harm Allah at all, and He will render their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of opposition to Allah and His guidance. Despite the clear signs of truth having been revealed, those who reject faith, turn away from Allah's path, and actively resist the Prophet's message will ultimately achieve nothing of consequence. Their enmity cannot affect Allah's dominion or purposes, and their good deeds performed in a state of disbelief will be nullified because they were rooted in rejection of truth. The verse thus serves as a warning of the spiritual bankruptcy that comes from willful rejection of clear divine guidance, and reassures the believers that no harm from the disbelievers' schemes can disrupt Allah's plans or diminish His power.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not invalidate your deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith must be accompanied by obedience to both Allah's divine command and the guidance of His Messenger, warning that inconsistency between belief and action—or disobedience after faith—can render one's good works void and spiritually ineffective. The repetition of 'obey' underscores that both sources of guidance are equally binding, and the warning against invalidating deeds teaches that hypocrisy, contradiction, or abandoning the prescribed path undermines the spiritual value of all prior righteous acts.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and turn away from the path of Allah, then die while they are disbelievers - Allah will never forgive them.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah's forgiveness is withheld from those who persistently reject faith and actively oppose the way of Allah until their death. The emphasis on dying in a state of disbelief indicates that the fate of the soul is sealed by one's condition at the moment of death, making sincere repentance and acceptance of faith during one's lifetime essential for salvation. The verse underscores the finality and gravity of turning away from divine guidance.

translation: So do not weaken and call not for peace while you are the superior, and Allah is with you, and He will not deprive you of your deeds.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers not to lose resolve or seek peace from a position of weakness, as they possess both divine support and military superiority. The promise that Allah will not diminish their deeds emphasizes that perseverance in righteous struggle yields eternal reward, reinforcing that victory and divine pleasure come through steadfastness rather than premature compromise.

translation: The worldly life is nothing but play and amusement. But if you believe and are conscious of Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the transient nature of worldly pursuits with the eternal value of faith and piety. It teaches that believers should not be preoccupied with material accumulation, as true success lies in righteous conduct and trust in Allah's promise of reward in the Hereafter. The mention of not asking for wealth emphasizes that Allah's recompense is based on sincere faith and consciousness of Him, not on monetary sacrifice, thereby reassuring believers that devotion to faith does not require impoverishment.

translation: If He were to ask you for them and urge you, you would become stingy, and He would expose your ill-will.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah's wisdom in not making obligatory the detailed specifications of certain religious matters (such as the number of animals for sacrifice) is merciful, for if He had pressed the believers for exact compliance, it would have revealed the stinginess and hidden malice within their hearts. The verse demonstrates Allah's compassionate knowledge of human nature and how He moderates His commands to suit human weakness and disposition, thereby concealing the spiritual defects that might otherwise be exposed through impossible demands.

translation: Here you are being called to spend in the way of Allah, but among you are those who withhold. Whoever withholds does so only against himself. Allah is the Rich, and you are the poor. If you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you.
interpretation: This verse establishes that stinginess in spending for God's cause is fundamentally self-harm rather than a loss to God, since Allah is self-sufficient and needs nothing from creation, while humanity is dependent on His provision. The warning that God can replace the believers with others conveys that Divine favor is conditional upon obedience and generosity, and that no community is indispensable to God's plan if they fail to fulfill their obligations of sacrifice and spending in His path.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Indeed, We have opened for you a clear opening (victory).
interpretation: This verse addresses Prophet Muhammad and announces a decisive victory that Allah has granted him. The 'clear opening' (fath) refers to the conquest of Mecca and the establishment of Islam's dominance, symbolizing the triumph of truth over falsehood. It emphasizes that this victory is not a result of human effort alone, but is a gift from Allah, demonstrating His support for His messenger and His message. The verse serves as reassurance and affirmation of divine favor during a period of struggle, indicating that ultimate success belongs to those whom Allah guides and supports.

translation: So that Allah may forgive you what has preceded of your sin and what will follow, and complete His favor upon you, and guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of divine forgiveness granted to the Prophet Muhammad, covering both past and future sins, alongside the bestowing of complete divine grace and guidance. It reflects the principle that those chosen for sacred missions are supported by God's mercy to fulfill their responsibilities without the burden of unresolved spiritual debt, allowing them to lead with spiritual integrity and clarity of purpose.

translation: And Allah will give you a mighty victory.
interpretation: This verse expresses a divine promise of powerful and decisive assistance from Allah to His messenger. The phrase 'mighty victory' (nصرا عزيزا) emphasizes that the help will be overwhelming and invincible, not merely a small or uncertain assistance. The interpretation centers on Allah's commitment to support His messenger with complete authority and strength, assuring him that opposition will ultimately be overcome through divine intervention and power that cannot be resisted.

translation: He is the One who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers so that they would increase in faith along with their faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that faith is not a static state but a dynamic journey of continuous spiritual growth. The descent of tranquility (al-sakīnah) into the hearts of believers serves as both a sign of divine favor and a catalyst for deepening conviction. The phrase 'with their faith' suggests that the added faith builds upon existing belief, emphasizing that spiritual development is progressive and accumulative. The subsequent mention of Allah's command over all forces in creation reinforces His absolute authority and power, implying that the believer's increase in faith is a result of witnessing divine signs and recognizing Allah's sovereignty, while His knowledge and wisdom ensure that this increase occurs precisely as intended in His grand design.

translation: So that He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally, and will remove from them their misdeeds. And that is a supreme achievement in the sight of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate purpose of faith and righteous action is not merely worldly reward, but admission into Paradise where believers will dwell eternally, their past sins forgiven. The mention of both men and women entering together underscores the spiritual equality of all believers, while the removal of misdeeds signifies Allah's complete mercy and purification of the believers' state. The designation of Paradise as 'supreme achievement' (فوزا عظيما) reframes success not as material gain or worldly victory, but as attaining Allah's pleasure and eternal peace, thereby orienting the believer's entire moral framework away from temporal pursuits toward the hereafter.

translation: And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women - those who assume about Allah an assumption of evil nature. Upon them is a misfortune of evil; and Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who harbor false beliefs about Allah's character and justice - whether through hypocrisy, polytheism, or harboring suspicion about His divine nature - will face severe punishment. The focus on both masculine and feminine forms underscores the universal accountability before Allah regardless of gender. The succession of descriptions (misfortune, anger, curse, and Hell) demonstrates the comprehensive nature of divine judgment for those who persist in such spiritual corruption, serving as a warning about the grave consequences of maintaining negative assumptions about the Divine.

translation: And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over all creation. The mention of 'soldiers' (armies/forces) of the heavens and earth signifies all the celestial bodies, angels, natural forces, and earthly creatures that serve Allah's will. The verse communicates that nothing in existence operates independently; everything serves Allah's ultimate plan. By concluding with His attributes of might ('Aziz) and wisdom (Hakim), the verse reassures believers that Allah's dominion is not merely powerful but also perfectly guided by infinite wisdom, so whatever He ordains or permits in the universe is both absolutely authoritative and based on perfect knowledge and justice.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good tidings, and a warner.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Prophet Muhammad's threefold mission: to bear witness to the truth and righteousness of his message before Allah, to bring glad tidings of reward and paradise to those who believe and obey, and to warn the disbelievers and wrongdoers of the consequences of their rejection. These three roles encompass the complete purpose of prophethood—attestation to divine truth, encouragement toward righteousness, and deterrence from sin.

translation: That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and support him, honor him, and glorify Him in the morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the multifaceted nature of faith and its practical manifestations - belief in Allah and His Messenger must be accompanied by active support, respect, and continuous remembrance of God through devotion at all times, suggesting that true faith requires both internal conviction and external demonstration through consistent righteous action and worship.

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So whoever breaks his oath breaks it only to the extent of his own soul, and whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with Allah - He will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that loyalty to the Prophet is ultimately loyalty to Allah, emphasizing that the believer's covenant with the Prophet is a covenant with Allah Himself. By stating that 'the hand of Allah is over their hands,' the verse illustrates Divine presence and sovereignty in human pledges, suggesting that all oaths and commitments made before the Prophet are witnessed and guaranteed by Allah. The verse thus teaches that faithlessness to one's covenants is a betrayal directed primarily against oneself and one's relationship with Allah, while steadfastness in honoring one's word to Allah—particularly through loyalty to His Prophet—is rewarded by Allah with magnificent recompense, linking personal integrity to one's ultimate accountability before the Divine.

translation: The bedouins who remained behind will say to you, 'Our wealth and our families kept us busy, so ask forgiveness for us.' They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, 'Then who can avail you against Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you benefit?' Rather, Allah is ever aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse reveals the hypocrisy of those who make excuses for not participating in jihad, claiming that their wealth and families prevented them while their hearts are devoid of genuine faith. The Prophet is instructed to challenge their false reasoning by pointing out that no one has power over Allah's decree—neither to prevent harm nor to bring benefit. This establishes that true reliance must be on Allah alone, and that external excuses mask the real issue: a lack of sincere commitment to faith. The verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge of their actions and intentions is complete, making their deception futile.

translation: Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families ever, and that was made attractive to your hearts, and you assumed the worst assumption, and you were a ruined people.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who lost faith during a critical moment, expressing how doubt and despair took root in their hearts regarding the return of the Prophet and the believers from battle. The verse condemns this spiritual corruption by revealing that their negative assumptions were not accidental but were embellished and encouraged by their own doubts, reflecting a people who had become spiritually barren and devoid of faith. It serves as a rebuke to those whose hearts succumbed to hopelessness and ill-suppositions about Allah's promise of protection and victory.

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger - indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental consequence of rejecting Allah's guidance and denying His Messenger. The phrase 'We have prepared' indicates that punishment is an inevitable and certain consequence of disbelief, not something arbitrary or subject to change. The verse emphasizes personal accountability - each individual is responsible for their choice to accept or reject faith. The preparation of punishment reflects divine justice, as those who actively turn away from clear signs and guidance cannot expect reward. This serves as both a warning to those still deliberating and a reminder that rejecting the truth has real, eternal consequences.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah's absolute sovereignty and authority over all creation, emphasizing that forgiveness and punishment are acts of divine justice rooted in Allah's infinite wisdom rather than arbitrary decisions. The mention of Allah's names 'Forgiving' and 'Merciful' at the end suggests that despite His complete power to punish, His nature is fundamentally characterized by clemency and compassion, indicating that His justice is tempered with mercy and those who repent genuinely need not despair of His forgiveness.

translation: Those who were left behind will say when you set forth toward gains to take them, 'Let us follow you.' They wish to change the words of Allah. Say, 'You will not follow us thus. Allah has said it before.' So they will say, 'Rather, you envy us.' But they were not understanding except a little.
interpretation: This verse reveals the hypocrisy of those unwilling to strive in the way of Allah, who suddenly wish to participate when victory and spoils are assured. Their desire to rewrite Allah's decrees and their accusation of envy against the believers exposes their fundamental lack of understanding of divine commandments and the nature of true faith, which requires commitment and sacrifice regardless of immediate worldly gains.

translation: Say to those of the Bedouins who remained behind: 'You will be called upon to fight against a people of mighty prowess. You shall fight them, or they shall submit. If you obey, Allah will give you a fair reward; but if you turn away as you did before, He will punish you with a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Bedouin tribes who were reluctant to participate in military expeditions and had chosen to remain behind instead of migrating with the Prophet. It emphasizes that obedience to Allah's command and fulfilling the obligation to defend the Muslim community brings reward, while turning away from this responsibility—as they had done in the past by refusing to emigrate—results in severe punishment. The verse communicates that faith is not merely internal belief but requires action and sacrifice when the community faces external threats, and that consistency in obedience is essential, as past failures cannot be repeated without consequences.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of divine mercy and consideration for those with physical disabilities or ailments, exempting them from blame in fulfilling their religious obligations according to their capacity. It then presents the fundamental covenant of obedience: those who submit to Allah and His Messenger receive eternal reward in Paradise, while rejection and disobedience lead to severe punishment. The juxtaposition teaches that Islamic law is built on compassion for human limitations while simultaneously demanding absolute adherence to the divine message through one's ability.

translation: Certainly, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine pleasure with sincere believers who demonstrated unwavering loyalty to the Prophet Muhammad despite difficult circumstances. Allah's knowledge of their inner sincerity—that their hearts matched their outward actions—validated their pledge. The descent of tranquility (sakīnah) upon them signifies divine reassurance and peace granted to those whose faith is genuine, and the promise of near victory illustrates how true believers are supported by Allah's aid. The verse teaches that divine approval follows authentic faith coupled with righteous action and sincere devotion.

translation: And much booty that they will capture. And Allah is Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that along with spiritual victories, the believers will gain material benefits and spoils from their righteous endeavors. The mention that 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' following this promise affirms that these earthly provisions come through Allah's divine wisdom and power, not by chance or human effort alone, thus serving as a reminder that all success and provision ultimately derive from Allah's perfect decree and control over all affairs.

translation: Allah has promised you many spoils that you will take. So He hastened for you this one, and held back the hands of the people from you, and so that it may be a sign for the believers, and that He may guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's fulfillment of His promise to grant the Muslims victory and wealth, while demonstrating His divine intervention on their behalf. The reference to hastening 'this one' spoil (referring to the spoils from the Battle of Khaybar) illustrates God's immediate support, while restraining their enemies' hands demonstrates His active protection. The verse underscores that these tangible blessings serve as signs affirming God's covenant with the believers, thereby strengthening their faith and conviction. Ultimately, these victories are not mere worldly acquisitions but divine guidance towards the straight path—indicating that material success should deepen the believers' commitment to God's way rather than distract them from their spiritual purpose.

translation: And another [conquest] which you have not yet attained - Allah has already encompassed it. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that beyond the immediate victories they have achieved, there are further trials, tests, and opportunities for conquest and growth that remain beyond their current reach, yet Allah has already encompassed and determined them in His infinite knowledge. The verse conveys divine assurance that what appears as a limitation to human capability is never beyond Allah's absolute power and wisdom, encouraging believers to trust in divine providence while striving in their endeavors.

translation: And if those who disbelieved fought you, they would turn their backs in flight, then they would find no protector and no helper.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the believers, when supported by divine aid, possess inherent strength that would cause their enemies to flee despite any numerical disadvantage. The emphasis on having no protector or helper after their defeat underscores that those who oppose God and His believers are ultimately deprived of any genuine support or refuge, emphasizing that true protection and victory come from reliance upon the Divine rather than from worldly alliances or material power.

translation: This is the way of Allah which has occurred before, and you will never find in the way of Allah any change.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of divine consistency and unchanging natural laws. Allah's way refers to His established patterns and methods of dealing with creation, including how He brings about consequences for human actions. The verse emphasizes that divine principles operate with absolute regularity and immutability—what has happened according to Allah's wisdom in the past will happen again under the same circumstances. This conveys that there are no exceptions to Allah's justice, no arbitrary interventions, and no escape from the consequences of defying His laws. It is a fundamental principle of causality in the universe established by the Divine Will, serving as a reassurance that history follows patterns and that righteousness and unrighteousness have their foreordained outcomes.

translation: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the midst of Mecca, after He had given you victory over them. And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine providence in controlling the natural impulses of both believers and disbelievers during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, when Muslims were prevented from entering Mecca despite their military readiness. God's restraint of both parties' aggression despite the Muslims having tactical advantage demonstrates that military victory is not the ultimate measure of success, and that God orchestrates events according to His wisdom rather than human desire. The concluding statement that 'Allah is ever Seeing of what you do' reminds believers that even when immediate results appear unfavorable, God is aware of their sincere intentions and righteous conduct, implying that apparent setbacks may serve greater purposes in God's plan.

translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque while the sacrificial animals were prevented from reaching their destination. And had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and thus incur blame for them without knowledge—[this was so] that Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been apart [from the believers], We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's wisdom in withholding immediate punishment from the disbelievers at Hudaybiyyah. The presence of hidden believers among them served as a divine mercy that prevented a harsh retaliation, as the believers could not distinguish between the righteous and the wicked among the Meccans. This teaches that Allah's restraint in judgment is often rooted in compassion for the believers and an opportunity for guidance, and that the mixing of righteous and unrighteous people in a community is sometimes a protection for that community from divine wrath. The verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and wisdom in His decisions regarding punishment and mercy.

translation: When those who disbelieved had put into their hearts zealotry - the zealotry of the Jahiliyyah - Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and imposed upon them the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the contrast between the destructive passion of pre-Islamic pride and the transformative power of divine guidance. The 'zealotry of Jahiliyyah' represents blind, tribal fanaticism rooted in arrogance, while Allah's response was not to overcome it through force, but through sakīnah (tranquility and divine assurance), which settled the hearts of the believers with certainty. The 'word of righteousness' (kalimah al-taqwā) becomes their defining principle, replacing the false honor of pre-Islamic customs. The phrase 'they were more deserving and worthy of it' emphasizes that those who submit to Allah's guidance possess a truer nobility and worthiness than those clinging to the vanity of ignorance. Thus, the verse teaches that genuine honor comes not from tribal pride or worldly passion, but from submitting to divine truth and embodying piety.

translation: Certainly Allah has made true to His Messenger the vision with truth. You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and your hair cut short, without fear. He knew what you did not know, and He made that into a near victory besides that.
interpretation: This verse interprets a divine vision granted to Prophet Muhammad about entering Mecca peacefully. The passage emphasizes that God's promises to His messengers are certain and will be fulfilled as He wills. The mention of entering with shaved or shortened hair and without fear signifies the completion of pilgrimage and the removal of all danger and anxiety. The final phrase suggests that beyond the fulfillment of the vision, God granted an immediate opening or conquest (Hudaybiyyah treaty), demonstrating that divine wisdom often exceeds human expectations and provides blessings in ways not initially perceived or anticipated, teaching the believers trust in God's omniscience and providential care.

translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that it may prevail over all other religions. And Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah's purpose in sending the Prophet Muhammad with Islam is the ultimate triumph of this religion over all other belief systems, not through coercion but through the truth and guidance it embodies. The phrase 'Allah is sufficient as a witness' affirms that the reality of Islam's superiority and the Prophet's truthfulness require no validation beyond Allah's own testimony, indicating that believers need not be anxious about vindication—God Himself bears witness to the truth of this mission.

translation: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And those with him are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their example in the Torah, and their example in the Gospel is like a plant that produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow sturdy and stand upon their stalks, amazing the farmers, so that through them He may enrage the disbelievers. Allah has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse establishes the dual nature of the believing community under the Prophet Muhammad: their firmness and strength against external opposition paired with their internal compassion and unity. The description of physical signs of devotion (marks from prostration) serves as evidence of their sincere commitment. The botanical metaphor illustrates how the Muslim community grows organically from a single foundation into a strong, flourishing entity that naturally provokes the envy and hostility of disbelievers—not through aggressiveness, but through the very reality of their success and influence. The verse emphasizes that this growth and ultimate reward is contingent upon both faith and righteous action, establishing that belief alone without corresponding ethical conduct does not fulfill the covenant with Allah.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O you who have believed, do not put forward [anything] before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches the principle of complete submission and obedience to Allah and His Messenger, emphasizing that believers should not prioritize their own opinions, judgments, or desires over the guidance of Allah and the Qur'an. The phrase 'do not put forward before Allah and His Messenger' means followers should not precede divine revelation with their own reasoning, nor should they act hastily without consulting the Messenger's guidance. The verse instills consciousness of Allah's omniscience and omniscience, reminding believers that Allah hears all and knows all intentions, thereby encouraging humble reliance on divine wisdom and prophetic instruction as the ultimate source of truth and guidance.

translation: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him in speech as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the proper etiquette and respect due to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by establishing boundaries for how believers should conduct themselves in his presence. The prohibition against raising one's voice above his and speaking to him as one would speak to ordinary people serves as a reminder that the Prophet holds a special station and authority. The warning that deeds may be nullified without one's awareness suggests that disrespect toward the Prophet, even if seemingly minor, undermines the sincerity and acceptance of one's religious actions before Allah. The verse thus teaches that reverence for the Prophet is integral to the integrity of one's faith and works.

translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah - those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the practice of showing respect and humility before the Prophet Muhammad - specifically by controlling one's speech and tone - is an external manifestation of an inward spiritual quality: a heart that has been purified and refined by Allah for the purpose of piety (taqwa). The verse teaches that modesty in demeanor is not merely a social courtesy, but evidence of genuine God-consciousness and sincere devotion to the Divine, which merits Allah's forgiveness and magnificent recompense.

translation: Indeed, those who call you from behind the private chambers - most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who lack manners and wisdom in their approach to the Prophet Muhammad. The reference to calling from behind chambers emphasizes their disrespect for proper protocol and privacy. The phrase 'most of them do not reason' suggests that such behavior stems from a lack of understanding and rational judgment about what is appropriate conduct. The verse teaches that true understanding includes knowing when, how, and in what manner to address those in positions of authority, and that bypassing proper etiquette reflects a deficiency in intellect and spiritual perception.

translation: And if only they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that patience and proper conduct in awaiting authority or guidance leads to better outcomes than hasty action. The Prophet's delay in responding was a test of their patience, and had they waited respectfully, they would have received a superior result. The verse concludes with divine mercy and forgiveness, indicating that Allah understands human weakness and offers clemency to those who repent, emphasizing that submission to proper protocol and authority is favored by Allah over impatience and breach of etiquette.

translation: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a fasiq (a wicked person) with information, then verify it, lest you harm a people in ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of verification and critical discernment in receiving news, particularly from sources of questionable character or reliability. It teaches believers that accepting unverified claims from disreputable sources can lead to grave injustices against innocent people, resulting in lasting regret and spiritual damage. The verse emphasizes personal moral responsibility for the consequences of hastily believed falsehoods, implying that believers must exercise intellectual caution and demand evidence before acting on allegations that could harm others, thereby protecting both the innocent and one's own integrity.

translation: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in many matters, you would surely fall into hardship. But Allah has made faith beloved to you and has beautified it in your hearts, and has made disbelief, transgression, and disobedience hateful to you. Those are the rightly guided ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance comes not from following human desires or majority opinion, but from divine instruction through the Messenger. The Prophet's authority to lead is grounded in his role as Allah's messenger, not in popular consent. The verse teaches that Allah transforms the hearts of the believers, instilling love for faith and aversion to sin—this spiritual transformation is what constitutes true righteousness, not merely intellectual assent or external compliance. The verse thus distinguishes between those whose hearts Allah has guided (the truly rightly-guided) and those who merely claim guidance outwardly.

translation: A favor from Allah and a blessing. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes that all good things, spiritual knowledge, and divine blessings come solely from Allah's grace and mercy, not from human effort or merit. The mention of Allah being All-Knowing and All-Wise suggests that His bestowal of blessings is based on His perfect knowledge and wisdom in determining what is best for His creation, highlighting the theme of divine sovereignty and the importance of recognizing Allah as the sole source of guidance and blessing.

translation: And if two groups of the believers fight each other, make peace between them. But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of God. And if it returns, then reconcile between them with justice and act equitably. Indeed, God loves those who act with equity.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of communal responsibility in maintaining social order and justice within the Muslim community. It delineates a graduated response to internal conflict: first seeking reconciliation, then intervening against the aggressor to restore compliance with divine law, and finally reinstating justice through fair arbitration. The verse emphasizes that true obedience to God is demonstrated not merely through individual piety, but through the establishment of justice and equity in human affairs, particularly in resolving disputes between believers and preventing oppression within the community.

translation: Indeed, the believers are brothers, so make peace between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse establishes the spiritual kinship of all believers as a foundational principle of Islamic community life. By describing believers as 'brothers,' the Qur'an emphasizes their fundamental equality and mutual responsibility toward one another. The command to 'make peace between your brothers' is not merely a suggestion but an obligatory duty on all believers to actively work toward reconciliation and harmony within the Muslim community, preventing discord and division. The verse concludes with the connection between this peaceful conduct and God's mercy, teaching that obedience to Allah's command for unity and reconciliation is itself an act of piety (taqwa) that brings divine compassion and mercy.

translation: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them. And let not women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] names. Wretched is the name of disobedience after [one's] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of mutual respect and dignity among believers by prohibiting mockery, contempt, and name-calling based on the recognition that outward appearances and judgments cannot determine true virtue or spiritual worth. The emphasis on 'perhaps they may be better than them' teaches believers humility and cautions against arrogance, as one's true character and standing before God is known only to Him. The verse elevates the gravity of these social transgressions by naming them 'disobedience after faith,' suggesting that such behavior fundamentally contradicts the ethical foundation of belief itself, making the practice of contempt toward others incompatible with genuine faith.

translation: O you who have believed, avoid much assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that protecting one's honor and dignity, as well as the dignity of others, is a fundamental Islamic principle rooted in the sanctity of the Muslim brotherhood. By equating backbiting to consuming the flesh of a dead brother—an abomination—the verse conveys that slander violates the sacred bond between believers and perpetuates social harm through character assassination. The prohibition against excessive suspicion and spying serves to establish a community built on trust rather than paranoia, recognizing that unfounded doubts and invasive surveillance corrode the moral fabric of society. The verse teaches that Muslims are accountable for protecting each other's reputations as they would protect their own, understanding that once trust is violated through gossip or espionage, the damage becomes irreversible, much like consuming the flesh of the dead.

translation: O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female and made you into peoples and tribes so that you may know one another. Indeed, the most honored of you in the sight of Allah is the one who is most righteous among you. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental principle that all humans share a common origin and that their diversity in nations and tribes is divinely ordained for mutual recognition and interaction, not for hierarchy or superiority. The verse then pivots to reveal that true honor and distinction before Allah is determined solely by piety and righteous conduct, thereby dismantling any notion of racial, tribal, or genealogical superiority. The closing affirmation of Allah's knowledge and awareness emphasizes that He alone is the ultimate judge of human worth, which cannot be claimed by worldly status, lineage, or material possession.

translation: The Bedouins say, 'We have believed.' Say, 'You have not believed; rather say, "We have submitted," for faith has not yet entered your hearts. But if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse distinguishes between mere external submission (Islam) and true internal faith (Iman). The Bedouins had outwardly submitted to Allah and His religion, but this outward compliance had not yet been accompanied by genuine belief in the heart. The verse teaches that true faith requires both internal conviction and sincere commitment, not merely verbal profession or superficial obedience. However, Allah offers them reassurance that if they continue in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, they will not lose the reward of their deeds, indicating that sincere obedience can lead to the development of true faith, and that Allah's mercy encompasses those who strive toward Him with sincere intention.

translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then did not doubt and strived with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah. Those are the truthful ones.
interpretation: This verse defines true belief as not merely intellectual affirmation but as a comprehensive commitment that combines unwavering certainty (absence of doubt), sincere dedication to Allah's cause, and practical sacrifice of both material resources and personal effort. The designation of such believers as 'al-sadiqun' (the truthful ones) indicates that genuine faith is authenticated through consistent action and demonstrated resolve, not through claims alone. The progression from belief to steadfastness to active struggle illustrates that faith is a dynamic state requiring continuous renewal and practical manifestation in all circumstances.

translation: Say, 'Do you teach Allah about your religion while Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth? And Allah is All-Knowing of all things.'
interpretation: This verse rebukes those who arrogantly instruct others about faith while forgetting that Allah's knowledge encompasses all of existence. It emphasizes the presumption of humans who claim to define or prescribe religion to the Divine, when Allah alone possesses complete and perfect knowledge of all affairs. The verse serves as a humbling reminder of the vastness of divine omniscience in contrast to the limitations and inadequacy of human understanding and authority in matters of faith.

translation: They favor you by saying that they have submitted. Say: 'Do not favor me with your submission. Rather, Allah favors you by guiding you to faith, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse corrects a fundamental misunderstanding of gratitude and divine favor. The believers were being arrogant about their acceptance of Islam as if they had done the Prophet a personal favor, when in reality their guidance to faith is entirely a gift from Allah. The verse establishes that any human acceptance of Islam is itself preceded by Allah's grace and guidance, not the other way around. True thankfulness belongs to Allah alone, not to those who received guidance, as they did not earn it through their own merit but received it as divine bounty.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah's complete and absolute knowledge of all hidden matters beyond human perception, whether in the heavens or on earth, while also emphasizing His constant awareness of human actions. It serves as a reminder that nothing escapes God's knowledge - neither the secrets of creation nor the deeds of people - thus reinforcing accountability and the monitoring of one's behavior in light of divine omniscience.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an,
interpretation: This verse opens Surah Qaf with an invocation of God's mercy followed by the letter 'Qaf' and an oath by the Qur'an itself. The oath structure indicates that what follows is of immense significance; by swearing by the Glorious Qur'an, Allah emphasizes the weightiness and authority of the message about to be conveyed, while also affirming the Qur'an's own majesty and divine origin as a means of establishing truth and credibility for the subsequent discourse in this surah.

translation: Rather, they were astonished that a warner came to them from among themselves. And the disbelievers said, 'This is something strange.'
interpretation: The disbelievers' amazement at Muhammad's prophethood stems from their arrogance and rejection of God's natural way of sending messengers from within human communities. Their calling the message 'strange' reflects their unwillingness to accept the truth when it arrives through ordinary human means, exposing how their denial is rooted not in logical objection but in pride and refusal to acknowledge a messenger who shares their humanity, challenging their false beliefs and worldly ambitions.

translation: What, when we are dead and have become dust? That would be a return far remote.
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of the disbelievers who mock the concept of resurrection. They express astonishment and doubt about the possibility of being revived after death and decomposition into dust, considering such a return to life to be extremely distant and impossible. The verse illustrates their rejection of the Hereafter and their perception of resurrection as something contrary to reason and nature.

translation: We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a Preserved Record.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's perfect knowledge and comprehensive record of all deeds and states of His servants. The 'diminishment of the earth' refers to the gradual decay and reduction of bodies after death, yet Allah's knowledge is not diminished thereby. The 'Preserved Record' (Lauh Mahfuz) emphasizes that every action, intention, and consequence is eternally documented in Allah's knowledge and will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment, establishing the certainty of divine justice and accountability.

translation: Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused state of affairs.
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual and intellectual condition of those who reject divine guidance despite its clarity. When the truth of God's message reached them, they chose to reject it entirely. As a consequence, they find themselves in a state of profound confusion and disorder ('amr murej') regarding their beliefs, values, and direction in life. The verse illustrates that the rejection of truth inevitably leads to internal discord and the loss of clear guidance, demonstrating the natural consequence of turning away from divine revelation.

translation: Have they not looked at the sky above them - how We built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts?
interpretation: This verse calls humanity to observe and reflect upon the construction of the heavens as a sign of God's power and majesty. The lack of fissures or cracks in the sky is presented as evidence of the precision and perfection of God's creation, designed to inspire wonder and lead the observer toward acknowledging the Creator's dominion and inviting contemplation on the order and harmony of the universe as a pathway to faith.

translation: And the earth - We have stretched it out, and cast upon it firm mountains, and caused to grow therein every lovely pair of plants.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's creative power and deliberate design of the earth for human habitation and sustenance. The stretching of the earth represents its expansion and preparation as a habitable space, the firm mountains signify stability and preventing tectonic upheaval, and the growth of every beautiful pair of plants demonstrates Allah's providence in supplying diverse vegetation for nourishment and benefit. The use of 'lovely pair' suggests the complementary nature of creation - plants existing in diverse, harmonious pairs and varieties - reflecting the divine order and wisdom embedded throughout creation as a sign of Allah's oneness and care for His creation.

translation: An insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back (to Allah)
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes that the signs and teachings of the Qur'an are meant as clear evidence and admonition for those who are truly devoted to returning to Allah in repentance and submission.
